meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell arriving during roll call), the Durham City Council reviewed its FY 2017 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report—receiving four unmodified clean audit opinions—and received a legal and multi-agency update on lead paint contamination and housing-code jurisdictional gaps at 525 Holloway Street. The central debate concerned Item 13, six 2006–2010 petitioned water and sewer extension projects totaling roughly $1.6 million (including the failed 23-lot Red Coach/Grand Oaks subdivision package wastewater plant and a homeowner with a failed well). Council split 4-3 in an informal sense-of-the-council tally to have staff schedule a public hearing to consider rescinding the utility agreements (leaving the final decision to the incoming Council) rather than immediately committing to proceed at the original assessment rates; the transcript digest recorded the 4-3 count without naming which individual members voted on each side. All formal procedural votes—approving the City Attorney's closed session items and adopting the meeting agenda—passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, East End Park Tire Crumb Update, and Closed Session Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the session and welcomed Mayor Bill Bell alongside Council Members Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel. Members noted background materials on East End Park playground tire crumb, and Council unanimously approved the City Attorney's request for a closed session on pending litigation and an update on 525 Holloway Street during Citizens Matters.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Citizens Matter Tribute to Mayor Bill Bell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed administrative consent items—including DPAC Oversight Committee, Durham Housing Authority Board reappointment (with comments calling for a public housing mobility plan), audit reports, water deposits, Lynn Haven Apartments multifamily housing revenue bonds, and petitioned utility projects—pulling Items 3 and 4. During Citizens Matters, a resident performed a Neil Diamond song parody honoring outgoing Mayor Bill Bell.

agenda_items.title: 525 Holloway Street Lead Contamination and Housing Code Jurisdiction Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney reported on ongoing code violations at 525 Holloway Street and jurisdictional limits among city, county, and state agencies when lead exposure does not meet county/state blood-lead trigger thresholds. Staff noted participation in a Peach-led collaborative meeting and a Raleigh meeting convened by Senator Mike Woodard with state health and environmental officials.

agenda_items.title: Item 3: FY 2017 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: External auditors presented four unmodified ('clean') audit opinions covering financial statements, Government Auditing Standards (Yellow Book), and federal and state compliance programs for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2017. Auditors noted three minor operational observations: conducting periodic user-access reviews for financial systems, timely construction invoice cut-off accrual, and accruing grant receivables.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Six Previously Ordered Petitioned Utility Projects (~$1.6 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated six water and sewer extension petitions approved between 2006 and 2010 that remained unbuilt due to capital queue delays and rising costs (~$1.6 million), including Red Coach/Grand Oaks (14 lots on a failing private package plant) and a homeowner using a temporary above-ground water line after well failure. Residents urged Council to honor its 2007 agreements without further delay, while Council split 4-3 in an informal tally to schedule a public hearing on rescinding the projects rather than immediately directing construction.
agenda_items.vote_summary: 4-3 (Sense-of-council tally to schedule rescission public hearing)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adoption and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the agenda placing Items 1–10 on consent and Item 14 (Lynn Haven Apartments bonds) on the GBA public hearing docket, then transitioned into closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Priority Items (Closed Session Litigation and 525 Holloway St Update)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved holding closed session under GS 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation and scheduling the 525 Holloway Street lead update alongside Citizens Matter 15.

votes.item_title: Sense-of-the-Council Direction on Six Petitioned Utility Projects (Item 13)
votes.notes: Split 4-3 informal sense-of-council count; individual member names on each side were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Informal sense-of-the-council tally between scheduling a public hearing to consider rescinding the six 2006–2010 petitioned utility projects versus immediately proceeding with construction at original assessment rates. Presiding chair announced four members favored scheduling the public hearing and three favored proceeding immediately.

votes.item_title: Adopt City Council Agenda (Consent 1–10, GBA Public Hearing 14) and Move to Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted agenda setting Consent Items 1–10 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14 and moved into closed session.

disagreements.issue: Whether to Honor or Consider Rescinding Six 2006–2010 Petitioned Utility Projects
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 over whether to immediately affirm construction of six long-delayed water and sewer extension petitions (~$1.6M) or bring rescission resolutions to a public hearing for the incoming Council.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring the six utility extension projects forward for a formal public hearing on rescission in an upcoming cycle, allowing the newly elected Council to decide.
side_a_arguments: Work sessions cannot take final formal action, and newly seated Council members should weigh in on $1.6 million in capital commitments.
Significant time and DOT/construction cost changes have occurred since the 2006–2010 petitions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Give clear direction now to proceed with the petitioned utility work at the promised assessment rates (with one speaker suggesting voluntary annexation into the City as a condition).
side_b_arguments: The City made a formal commitment after public hearings in 2006–2010, and residents relied on it—including a Red Coach/Grand Oaks community paying $112/month to a failing package plant and a homeowner whose well failed.
$1.6 million is modest relative to the overall City budget.
disagreements.resolution: In an informal 4-3 sense-of-the-council tally (individual voter names not stated in the transcript), Council directed staff to bring the rescission items to a future Monday public hearing.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 20, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council heard the 2017 Third Quarter Crime Report from Police Chief C.J. Davis covering staffing gains (93% sworn), mandatory mental health first aid training for ~535 officers, body-worn camera deployment across 470 cameras, and Council questioning on misdemeanor diversion and use-of-force transparency. All 15 recorded formal votes passed unanimously 7-0, including a bond issuance public hearing for a new parking deck and debt refinancing, consolidated annexations and rezonings for 208 Smallwood Drive (155 townhouses, $10,000 DPS proffer) and Ellis Road Townhouses Phase 2 (110 townhouses), and rezoning for a Durham Rescue Mission bargain center at North Roxboro Street and Bose Drive. Council also voted 7-0 to confirm street-completion assessment rolls for Ravenstone and Stone Hill Estates subdivisions despite resident objections over bankrupt-developer bonds and microsurfacing workmanship, and approved 7-0 an updated City of Durham logo after hearing an alternative citizen design.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Ceremonial Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and Troop 405 from St. Matthew's Catholic Church led the Pledge of Allegiance. Audio during the subsequent ceremonial recognitions and consent agenda window (`00:04:47`–`00:29:47`) was largely unintelligible in the transcript prior to the crime report.

agenda_items.title: 2017 Third Quarter Police Crime and Operations Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief C.J. Davis and Deputy Chief Anthony Marsh reported property crime up 6% (larcenies 57% of Part 1 crime, prompting a Clean Car Campaign), Priority 1 response times averaging 6.12 minutes, 93% sworn staffing, 100% officer completion of 8-hour mental health first aid training, a new McDougald Terrace community engagement unit, and 470 deployed body-worn cameras. Council Members Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden questioned staff on 43 youth drug arrests relative to misdemeanor diversion, sexual assault reporting, body-camera complaints/tech glitches, beat realignment, and public use-of-force data disclosure.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Installment Finance Contract / Bond Issuance for Parking Deck and Debt Refinancing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd held the required public hearing on a proposed bond issuance to fund the new downtown parking deck, parking improvements, and debt refinancing. With no public speakers, Council Member Don Moffitt praised Finance staff for maintaining Durham's AAA bond rating, and Council approved the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — 208 Smallwood Drive (Catfish Farms LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young introduced a standardized multi-motion format for planning public hearings, and Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Catfish Farms LLC's request to annex 24 acres at 208 Smallwood Drive (effective Dec. 31, 2017) and rezone from RR to PDR 6.458 for up to 155 townhouses with Page Road turn-lane improvements (Planning Commission 10-0). In response to Council Member Steve Schewel regarding 44 projected new DPS students, applicant attorney Patrick Byker proffered a $10,000 contribution to Durham Public Schools prior to site-plan approval.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Ellis Road Townhouses Phase 2 (2725 Ellis Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a request covering ~16.5 acres across seven parcels at 2725 Ellis Road for a utility extension agreement, annexation effective December 31, 2017, FLUM change from low-density to low-medium density residential, and rezoning to PDR 6.678 for up to 110 townhouses (Planning Commission 11-0). Applicant representative Laura Holloman highlighted step-down density transitions and design commitments.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — DLLT RR / Durham Rescue Mission Bargain Center (N. Roxboro St at Bose Dr)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a rezoning of ~4 acres across six parcels at North Roxboro Street and Bose Drive to Commercial Neighborhood with a Development Plan (16,000–20,000 sq ft commercial) prohibiting drug stores, convenience stores, gas stations, and drive-thrus while closing Bose Drive (Planning Commission 14-0). Applicant agent Jared Edens explained the site is for a Durham Rescue Mission bargain center with an opaque fence buffer along the Eno River park area, and Bill Judge addressed Steve Schewel's questions on GoTriangle bus-stop review timing.

agenda_items.title: Confirmation of Assessment Roll — Street Completion in Ravenstone Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff Robert Joyner presented the street-completion assessment roll for 233 properties in Ravenstone subdivision, noting objections from seven properties (2.6%) arguing costs should be covered by taxes, HOA dues, or the developer. No public speakers addressed the item, and Council confirmed the assessment roll 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Confirmation of Assessment Roll — Street Completion in Stone Hill Estates Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner presented the Stone Hill Estates street-completion assessment roll across 203 properties ($800/lot payable over 10 years at 0% interest, with 22 objections including 15 HOA-owned parcels and one hardship claim). Resident speakers including Vanessa Brown criticized uneven paving, microsurfacing workmanship, and KB Home's bankruptcy without a secured bond; Assistant Public Works Director Tasha Johnson addressed microsurfacing quality, and Council confirmed the roll 7-0 while asking the City Attorney to follow up on HOA quitclaim-deed questions.

agenda_items.title: Updated City of Durham Logo (Pulled from Consent Agenda)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda for speaker Craig Carter (appearing as a private citizen), who presented an alternative logo concept and argued the staff design omitted key identity elements. Council members praised the thorough staff-led process and voted 7-0 to approve the updated City of Durham logo.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council heard presentations on $4 million in odor-control improvements across four high-odor areas affecting Highway 54 businesses and residences near South Durham sewer infrastructure, clarified transit fixed-route fare ordinance rules, and engaged in an extensive policy discussion on redeveloping City-owned downtown property for affordable housing and office space. Council members and staff debated the financial trade-offs between maximizing affordable units (including advocates' push for 175 units or 15% downtown affordability) versus the multi-million-dollar property tax subsidies required, 4% vs. 9% LIHTC feasibility, historic preservation value impacts, and potential $9 million land sale proceeds to help fund Police Headquarters. Council unanimously approved closed session litigation items, completed board and commission appointments (including breaking a Citizens Advisory Committee tie/plurality when a member switched to Vivian Slade for four votes), and unanimously adopted the November 20, 2017 meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Priority Items, and Closed Session Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the session to order with Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Members Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel present. The City Manager added supplemental Item 29 (proposed City logo update) and a horseshoe-pit citizen speaker, the City Clerk noted a supplemental Appearance Commission appointment, and Council unanimously approved two closed-session litigation items under GS 143-318.11(a)(3).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote on closed session items)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: Transit Fares, Park Accessibility, Crime Report, and Annexations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed departmental and public hearing items—pulling Item 5 (fixed-route transit fare schedule ordinance) and Item 12 (Kimley-Horn accessibility contract for Valley Springs Park and West Point on the Eno Park)—and noted upcoming items including dump trucks, refuse vehicles, the Q3 crime report, and consolidated annexations for 28 Smallwood Drive and Ellis Road Townhouses Phase 2.

agenda_items.title: South Durham Sewer Odor Control Improvements ($4 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley and staff addressed odor complaints along Highway 54 affecting nearby hotels, senior facilities, and restaurants, outlining force-main, air-release valve, and $4 million in odor-control improvements across four high-odor areas. Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden asked about resident health impacts and staff agreed to coordinate with the Durham County Health Department, while Greeley disputed a resident engineer's claim that the North Durham plant must be fully encapsulated.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Horseshoe Pitching Club Relocation to Rocky Creek Park
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives of Durham's five horseshoe-pitching teams discussed relocating their gathering space roughly one football field away to Rocky Creek Park. Speakers expressed willingness to move provided the site includes adequate lighting and capacity for eight teams.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Fixed-Route Transit Fare Schedule Clarifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members sought clarification on how technical school eligibility (such as Middle College High School at Durham Tech) and Monday-to-Friday fare rules were defined in the proposed transit fare ordinance versus the staff memo.

agenda_items.title: Downtown City-Owned Property Redevelopment: Office Space and Affordable Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff reviewed downtown office leasing demand (noting Durham ID and Chesterfield Building absorption by tenants like Duke and Nutanix), historic preservation cost trade-offs (~$500,000 value impact), and affordable housing financing scenarios for redeveloping City-owned downtown land. Members debated whether achieving 15% downtown affordability or ~175 units is financially realistic without excessive property tax subsidies, weighing 4% tax credits, 60%–70% AMI workforce units, and potential $9 million land-sale revenue to help fund the Police Headquarters.

agenda_items.title: City Logo Update, Board Appointments, and Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council left the supplemental City logo update on consent, announced board/commission appointments—with one member switching from Charles Smith to Vivian Slade to award the second Citizens Advisory Committee seat—and unanimously adopted the November 20 City Council meeting agenda before moving into closed session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote on agenda; ballot tallies recorded for appointments)

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Closed Session Items (GS 143-318.11(a)(3), incl. City v. Roberson)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized two closed-session attorney-client consultations including City of Durham v. Roberson.

votes.item_title: Board and Commission Appointments (BPAC, Appearance Commission, Citizens Advisory Committee)
votes.notes: Written ballot tallies announced aloud; individual voters' ballots were not read by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk read ballot tallies: Adeline received 7 votes for Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission; Lynn McClay received 6 votes for City-County Appearance Commission; for two Citizens Advisory Committee seats, Janie Washington received 5 votes, and Vivian Slade received 4 votes after a Council member shifted a vote from Charles Smith (3 votes), ahead of Marcus Carson (2 votes).

votes.item_title: Adopt November 20, 2017 City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Items 1–15, 28, and 29; GBA Item 20; and GBA Public Hearings 21–26.

disagreements.issue: Feasibility of 15% Downtown Affordability / ~175 Affordable Units on City-Owned Downtown Property
disagreements.summary: Council members and housing advocates diverged on how aggressively the City should subsidize affordable housing versus incorporating revenue-generating office space and workforce housing on City-owned downtown land.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize a major affordable housing investment (advocates sought ~175 units / 15% downtown affordability) using deeper public resources and mission-driven partners.
side_a_arguments: Downtown redevelopment offers a rare opportunity to create substantial affordable housing near jobs and services.
Additional funding sources such as social services or Housing Authority partnerships could support deeper affordability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pair 4% LIHTC/affordable housing (including 60%–70% AMI workforce housing) with revenue-producing office space and land-sale proceeds to limit property-tax subsidies.
side_b_arguments: Reaching 15% affordability in the downtown core requires millions in City subsidies that are unrealistic without raising property taxes.
Office demand is strong and can cross-subsidize housing while land sale proceeds (~$9M) help offset Police Headquarters costs.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Council provided feedback to staff to continue refining mixed office, green space, and affordable housing scenarios.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Nov 6, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council opened its November 6, 2017 meeting with recognitions for kinship caregivers, Durham Community Trail Watch volunteers, the late community leader F.E.J. McDonald-Still, and city runners before unanimously approving all five recorded votes 7-0. Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 (including Southside East Phase 2 environmental/construction amendments, Police Headquarters contracts, and Durham Athletic Park operating amendments) and adopted the 2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan alongside Urban Open Space Plan updates 7-0. Council also approved 7-0 the updated Durham-Morrisville annexation and utility service area boundary agreement and granted project-completion extensions on economic development incentive contracts with Migrate Property II LLC (through September 30, 2018) and A&J Capital LLC (through June 30, 2018), before closing with public comment on gun violence and state preemption.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions (Kinship Care, Trail Watch, F.E.J. McDonald-Still Memorial, Bull City Race)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council issued proclamations and recognitions for grandparents raising grandchildren, Durham Community Trail Watch's five years of trail monitoring, and a memorial resolution for F.E.J. McDonald-Still introduced by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden. Staff also recognized city participants in the Bull City 5-mile race.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Southside East Phase 2 Amendment, DCHC MPO Study, Sewer Contracts, DAP & Police HQ)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent headings covering minutes, board appointments, audits, McCormack Baron Salazar's Southside East Phase 2 environmental/construction amendment, a DCHC MPO downtown study, Eastern Outfall/MLK Parkway sewer relocation, installment finance negotiation, the September bid report, the 6th amendment to the Durham Athletic Park operating agreement, Police Headquarters art and equipment contracts, and utility locating services.

agenda_items.title: 2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (A1700002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Laura Woods presented the fifth annual Evaluation and Assessment Report rectifying city-county land-use map amendments (17 city and 3 county in 2016) and incorporating Board of County Commissioners-requested updates to the Urban Open Space Plan. Council praised the Urban Open Space Plan, and with no public speakers, adopted the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Morrisville Annexation and Utility Service Area Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith presented an updated annexation and utility service area agreement with the Town of Morrisville replacing the 1997 agreement that expired October 1, 2017, reflecting updated boundary PINs and approved by Morrisville on October 24. With no public speakers, Council adopted the ordinance and authorized the Mayor to execute the agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement — Migrate Property II LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reginald Jones of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented an amendment to the June 6, 2016 incentive agreement under G.S. 158-7.1 extending the project completion deadline to September 30, 2018. In response to the City Manager, Jones explained delays stemmed from replacing the project's engineering firm and additional bank-required brownfield environmental testing, and expressed confidence the project will execute.

agenda_items.title: Second Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement — A&J Capital LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reginald Jones presented a second amendment to the February 2, 2015 incentive agreement with A&J Capital LLC extending the project completion deadline from December 31, 2017 to June 30, 2018. Jones explained the delay resulted from the untimely death of the project's coordinating architect, and Council approved the extension 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Remarks on Gun Violence and Local Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A young resident asked Council what steps Durham can take within state law to protect residents from mass shootings and gun violence. Council members shared frustration over daily gun violence and state preemption, and Mayor Bell encouraged sharing proposals with Durham's General Assembly delegation for the city's annual legislative agenda.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Approving 2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (Item 8)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Planner Laura Woods' report on 2016 plan amendments and Urban Open Space Plan revisions, Council closed the hearing with no speakers and adopted Attachment A's resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance and Resolution Authorizing Execution of Durham-Morrisville Annexation Agreement (Item 23)
votes.discussion_detail: With no questions or public speakers, Council approved the ordinance and resolution authorizing the Mayor to execute the updated Morrisville annexation agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Migrate Property II LLC (Item 24)
votes.notes: Transcript ASR renders the entity name as 'my great property to LLC'.
votes.discussion_detail: After Reginald Jones explained the engineering replacement and brownfield testing delays, Council closed the hearing and authorized the City Manager to extend the completion deadline to September 30, 2018 on a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Second Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with A&J Capital LLC (Item 25)
votes.discussion_detail: After Reginald Jones explained the delay caused by the architect's death, Council closed the hearing and authorized the City Manager to extend the completion deadline to June 30, 2018 on a 7-0 vote.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council unanimously suspended the rules to adopt a supplemental resolution memorializing F.E.J. McDonald Still, reviewed $704,000 in added environmental/construction costs for Southside Phase II (138 affordable units at 60% AMI with McCormick Baron Salazar), and examined the sixth amendment to the Durham Bulls Athletic Park operating agreement. During debate on a property tax increment grant program, Council encountered three contested actions: a substitute motion for a two-year duration failed for lack of a second; a motion to extend the staff-proposed one-year program to three years drew a split voice/count vote in which Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece were named during the count (the full-board tally was truncated by a transcript gap); and a motion to eliminate a 10% holdback on the property tax increase grant failed on a 2-4 voice vote (two ayes vs. four nays, though individual voter names were not announced in the transcript). Council also confirmed appointments to the Durham Housing Authority Board (Patrice Nelson) and Workforce Development Board and unanimously adopted the business meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Comprehensive Plan Assessment & F.E.J. McDonald Still Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's correction reclassifying Item 8 (2016 Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan) as a public hearing. Council also unanimously added supplemental Item 30, suspended the rules, and adopted a resolution memorializing community leader F.E.J. McDonald Still.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Citizens Matters (Unopened Right-of-Way & Election-Day Free Transit)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members pulled Item 9 (Southside Phase II), Item 12 (installment financing), and Item 14 (Durham Bulls operating agreement), while praising Transportation's $12 million TIGER grant application for two-way conversion of the downtown loop and commenting on disaggregated workforce reporting in Item 13. During Citizens Matters, speakers addressed an unopened 1960s right-of-way, road delays, and a proposal for fare-free GoDurham transit on Election Days to expand voter access.

agenda_items.title: Property Tax Increment Grant Program: Duration and 10% Holdback Motions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated amendments to a staff-proposed property tax grant program: a substitute two-year duration motion failed for lack of a second, and a motion to expand the program from one year to three years produced a split voice vote/count naming Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece (who noted preferring a one-year term). A subsequent motion to eliminate a 10% holdback on the property tax increase grant failed on a 2-4 voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Contested / Failed motions (2-year substitute failed for lack of second; 3-year motion split; 10% holdback removal failed 2-4)

agenda_items.title: Audit Services Inventory Report & Workforce Development Board Makeup
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council asked the City Manager's office for demographic/composition information on the Workforce Development Board. On Item 7, Audit Services explained 'fairly stated' inventory testing across $2.4 million in City departmental inventory, including Water and Sewer Maintenance's perpetual inventory in Cityworks.

agenda_items.title: Item 9: McCormick Baron Salazar Southside Phase II Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development staff addressed a discrepancy between the memo ($5.1M) and resolution ($3.4M) after adding $704,000 for excess soil disposal and detention-pond surveying required for Phase II certificates of occupancy. Council discussed keeping Phase II focused on 138 affordable units at 60% AMI using 4% tax credits and why standard federal contracting language was added upon amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 14: Durham Bulls Athletic Park Sixth Amendment & Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff explained the Durham Bulls Athletic Park operating agreement's negotiated management fee and why net operating income shifted from negative (2012–2015) to positive. The Clerk then announced unanimous 7-vote appointments for Patrice Nelson (Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners) and to the Workforce Development Board, and Council unanimously adopted the agenda.

disagreements.issue: Duration (1 vs. 2 vs. 3 Years) and 10% Holdback for Property Tax Grant Program
disagreements.summary: Council divided over whether to keep the staff-proposed one-year property tax increase grant program with a 10% holdback or expand it to three years and remove the 10% holdback.
disagreements.side_a_position: Expand the grant program to three years (or two years as a substitute) and remove the 10% holdback to make the full tax increase available.
side_a_arguments: Several members expressed interest in a longer multi-year window to ensure continuity while a replacement program is developed.
Eliminating the 10% holdback (proposed by Jillian Johnson) directs the full property tax increase toward grant recipients.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain the staff-proposed one-year duration and 10% holdback rather than committing future Councils to a larger multi-year program.
side_b_arguments: Extending to three years creates a larger financial commitment, and the incoming Council can alter the program anyway.
One year is appropriate pending development of a permanent successor program.
disagreements.resolution: The two-year substitute failed for lack of a second, the three-year amendment drew a contested split vote/count naming Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece (outcome truncated by transcript gap), and removing the 10% holdback failed 2-4 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 16, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 and unanimously voted 7-0 to advance Concept B2—an 80-unit 100%-affordable LIHTC residential development paired with ground-floor retail, ~62,000 sq ft of office space, and a 260-space parking deck—as its preferred design for the Jackson-Pettigrew Street downtown site. Council approved 7-0 a Future Land Use Map amendment and Commercial General rezoning for 7130 NC Highway 751 (30,000 sq ft commercial, with self-storage prohibited via proffer and a follow-up 7-0 vote requested by Don Moffitt to ensure the zoning ordinance itself passed). On Item 27, Ample Storage's 200,000-sq-ft self-storage expansion at 4343 Garrett Road, Council divided 6-1—with Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Eddie Davis voting Aye and Don Moffitt voting No—on both the Comprehensive Plan amendment and the Commercial General rezoning, while voting 7-0 on the consistency statement after Moffitt switched his consistency vote to Yes. Council closed with 7-0 votes adopting initial Rural Residential zoning for 4618 Hobson Road following legislative donut-hole annexation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Recognitions, and Planning Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Council Member Eddie Davis led the Pledge with Troop 412, and Council recognized community events including a lead town hall at Holton Career and Resource Center and National Community Planning Month (accepted by Planning Director Patrick Young). City Manager Tom Bonfield also requested a closed session at meeting's end under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Dockless Bike Share Permits, Hybrid Bus Repowering, Duke Beltline Trail, Public Safety Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent headings covering Appearance Commission, street acceptances, Wake EMC service consent, dockless bike-share permit fees, Midwest Bus Corp. hybrid bus repowering, Duke Beltline Trail grant, Triangle Regional Model agreement, North Durham biosolids equipment, West Safety Services, auction authorization, August bid report, police/fire vehicle purchases, HUD fair housing and law enforcement grants, and City Code Sec. 70-95/70-96/70-129 revisions.

agenda_items.title: Jackson-Pettigrew Street Development Update (Concepts A1, A2, B1, and B2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson, DHIC's Michael Rogers, and Self-Help's Tucker Bartlett presented four development concepts for the two-acre city-owned site near the Durham Transit Station, comparing mixed-income versus 100%-affordable LIHTC scenarios with and without market-rate office space. Council members praised Mayor Bell's leadership in broadening the options, questioned parking ratios, pre-leasing risk, and affordable retail space for Black-owned businesses, and voted 7-0 to endorse Concept B2 (80 LIHTC affordable units with 25% at <=30% AMI, retail, ~62,000 sq ft office, and 260 parking spaces, carrying the lowest ~$2.8M post-voucher gap) as the preferred design.

agenda_items.title: FLUM Amendment and Zoning Map Change — 7130 NC Highway 751
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a 2.7-acre request across three parcels at 7130 NC 751 to shift from Office/OI(D) & RS-20 to Commercial/CG(D) capped at 30,000 sq ft with TIA roadway commitments (Planning Commission 12-0). At Council questioning, applicant agent Tim Sivers proffered a prohibition on self-storage; after voting 7-0 on the plan amendment and consistency statement, Council later voted 7-0 at `02:28:10` on Don Moffitt's motion to explicitly adopt the omitted zoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item — Ample Storage Sanding Creek (4343 Garrett Road, A1600014 / Z1600030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Ample Storage's request to re-designate 27–28 acres at 4343 Garrett Road from Medium-Density Residential/RR to Commercial/CG(D) for up to 200,000 sq ft of self-storage, preserving roughly 14 acres near a stream and proffering transit/light-rail right-of-way (Planning Commission 11-0). Council members debated self-storage concentration in southwest Durham, low job/tax generation, and Planning Director Pat Young's upcoming December white paper; Don Moffitt dissented 6-1 on both the FLUM amendment and zoning ordinance while switching to Yes on the 7-0 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning — 4618 Hobson Road (Session Law 2017-80 Technical Correction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented an exact-translation Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for 4618 Hobson Road, a donut-hole parcel inadvertently omitted from S.L. 2017-80 and annexed by July 31 technical corrections. With no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement and initial zoning ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Endorse Concept B2 as Preferred Design for Jackson-Pettigrew Street Development (Item 25)
votes.discussion_detail: Following presentations by DHIC and Self-Help and council consensus backing the 80-unit 100%-affordable LIHTC housing, retail, and ~62,000 sq ft office option, Council voted 7-0 to direct staff forward with Concept B2.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Amending Future Land Use Map for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Tim Sivers' proffer excluding self-storage and Don Moffitt's remarks on commercial node creep, Council approved the comprehensive plan amendment resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map Amendment Resolution for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: After debate over self-storage concentration in southwest Durham, low permanent job/tax yield, and impervious surface versus voluntary stream buffering, Council approved the FLUM amendment 6-1 with Don Moffitt voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Initially tallied 6-1, Don Moffitt immediately asked the clerk to change his vote on the consistency statement to Yes, resulting in a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (CG(D)) for Ample Storage Sanding Creek (Item 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the Commercial General with Development Plan rezoning for 200,000 sq ft of self-storage at 4343 Garrett Road 6-1, with Don Moffitt voting No.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Ordinance for 7130 NC Highway 751 (Item 26 Corrective Vote)
votes.notes: Prompted staff commitment to refine motion sequencing in future planning agendas.
votes.discussion_detail: Don Moffitt raised a point of order noting the two earlier motions on Item 26 covered the FLUM amendment and consistency statement without voting on the zoning map change itself; staff concurred and Council approved the Item 26 zoning ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 4618 Hobson Road Initial Zoning (Item 28)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for 4618 Hobson Road 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance (RR) for 4618 Hobson Road (Item 28)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted Rural Residential initial zoning for 4618 Hobson Road 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Ample Storage Sanding Creek Rezoning and Self-Storage Concentration (4343 Garrett Road)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over amending the Future Land Use Map and rezoning 27–28 acres at 4343 Garrett Road to allow a 200,000-square-foot self-storage expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the FLUM amendment and CG(D) rezoning for Ample Storage's expansion.
side_a_arguments: Self-storage generates minimal additional vehicle trips on Garrett Road and provides affordable space for small startup trades and service businesses.

The development plan preserves roughly 14 acres (50% of the site) including stream buffers above ordinance minimums, offers potential transit right-of-way/bus stops, and follows Ample's high-quality brick aesthetic.
The Planning Commission recommended approval unanimously 11-0, and Planning Director Pat Young pledged a December white paper on future self-storage concentration rules.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose converting residentially designated land to Commercial General for additional self-storage.
side_b_arguments: Self-storage facilities generate extensive impervious surface, and roughly eight of the 14 undisturbed acres are already constrained by steep slopes and stream buffers rather than genuinely developable land.
Self-storage is proliferating across southwest Durham while providing very few permanent jobs, low tax yield, and no street-activating retail.
disagreements.resolution: Both the Future Land Use Map amendment and the CG(D) zoning ordinance passed 6-1 (Moffitt voting No), while the consistency statement passed 7-0 after Moffitt switched his consistency vote to Yes.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council unanimously referred a City Attorney report on the legal status of inclusionary zoning in North Carolina back to staff, reviewed a proposed one-year permit process for dockless bike-share operators, and examined Wake Electric Membership Corporation's request for exclusive electric service consent in designated annexation areas. In the afternoon, Council held an extended work session review of the proposed Jackson/Pettigrew Street affordable housing and office redevelopment (Item 25), focusing on why adding market-rate residential units creates a $5.5–$6.9 million financing gap, threatens competitive 9% LIHTC investor appetite, and complicates constitutional 'private emolument' rules for below-market land conveyance—leading Council to request a written risk memo ahead of its next Monday meeting. All votes taken at the session were unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Referral of Inclusionary Zoning Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session, heard an announcement regarding Lakewood Elementary Walk to School Day, and entertained the City Attorney's priority request to refer Item 4 (Legal Status of Inclusionary Zoning in North Carolina) back to the City Attorney's Office for a future session.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Citizens Matters: Solicitation Permit Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed departmental items—including hybrid bus repowering, water biosolids, police vehicles, three fire trucks, HUD fair housing grants, police grants, and UDO affordable housing bonuses—and pulled Items 5, 6, 11, 13, 16, and 23. During Citizens Matters, Scott Barnet proposed restoring a $40/month solicitation permit with background checks, which Council referred to the City Attorney's Office.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Wake Electric Membership Corporation Exclusive Service Consent
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Wake Electric representatives explained that state statute allows Council to designate Wake Electric as the exclusive electric service provider in areas already assigned to it by the NC Utilities Commission as the City annexes outward, avoiding repeated per-annexation requests while leaving Duke Energy and Wake Electric's existing boundaries intact.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Dockless Bike-Share Permit Process and Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff recommended creating a one-year permit process and ordinance for dockless bike-share companies, noting private operators are poised to launch without existing regulatory guardrails and carry no direct financial risk to the City compared to smart-dock systems. Staff also noted ongoing discussions with operators on helmet access.

agenda_items.title: Item 25: Proposed Jackson/Pettigrew Street Mixed-Use Affordable Housing Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Development partners and City staff detailed subsidy requirements ($5.5M–$6.9M with vouchers; $9M–$10M without LIHTC), explaining how including market-rate housing increases financing gaps, lowers investor appetite for 9% tax credits, and triggers constitutional 'private emolument' limits unless an office component demonstrably cross-subsidizes affordable housing. Council requested a written memo summarizing those three market-rate risk buckets, heard support from Durham CAN, and discussed long-term affordability via land leases or mission-driven partners serving 15%–60% AMI.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adoption and Ample Self-Storage Zoning Map Note
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the agenda placing Items 2, 3, and 5–23 on consent, Item 25 on the General Business Agenda, Items 26–28 as GBA public hearings, and referring Items 1 and 4 back to staff. A member also urged colleagues to review a newly added map of nearby self-storage facilities ahead of the Ample Self Storage zoning hearing.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 4 (Legal Status of Inclusionary Zoning in North Carolina) back to the City Attorney's Office for a future meeting.

votes.item_title: Adopt City Council Agenda (Consent 2, 3, 5–23; GBA 25; Public Hearings 26–28; Refer Back 1 & 4)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the consent, GBA, and public hearing agenda while formally referring Items 1 and 4 back to staff.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Oct 2, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Steve Schewel excused 6-0 to attend his mother's funeral in Virginia, the remaining six Durham City Council members conducted a brief regular meeting featuring proclamations for National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, National Arts and Humanities Month, and Imagine a Day Without Water. Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda covering water reclamation facility improvements, youth workforce contracts, Fletcher's Chapel UMC sewer extension, brick paver repair, and DOST appointments. On its sole General Business item, Council voted 6-0 to adopt the revised City of Durham Social Media Policy for elected officials and appointed boards.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Steve Schewel, and October Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, and Council voted 6-0 to excuse Steve Schewel's absence for his mother's funeral. Mayor Bell presented proclamations for National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month (with speakers warning shelters were turning people away), National Arts and Humanities Month (accepted by Durham Arts Council's Sherry DeVries), and Imagine a Day Without Water (accepted by Water Management Director Don Greeley), followed by Charlie Reece's tribute to Roselle Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Water Reclamation Improvements, WIOA Youth Contract, Sewer Extension, Brick Paver Repair)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the City Attorney and City Clerk reported no priority items, Mayor Bell read consent items covering board attendance reports, a memorial resolution for F.E.J. McDonald-Still (requested by Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden for another meeting), North and South Durham Water Reclamation Facilities improvements, Made in Durham and Eckerd Youth Alternatives WIOA contracts, Fletcher's Chapel UMC sewer-only extension, 2018 brick paver repair (ST-266), and a DOST appointment.

agenda_items.title: Revised City of Durham Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Appointed Boards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the revised Social Media Policy for elected officials and appointed boards following prior council revisions and public-affairs review. Council Member Charlie Reece thanked Public Affairs staff for incorporating elected-official feedback alongside employee updates, and Council adopted the revised policy 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell absent and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden granted a unanimous excused absence, the longest-serving Council Member present, Steve Schewel, presided over the September 21 work session. Council heard from 527 Holloway Street residents Holly Dwan and her neighbor regarding environmental lead-paint contamination from neighboring 525 Holloway Street and potential ordinance amendments to close enforcement gaps. Staff also presented North and South Durham Water Reclamation Facilities process improvements (Items 3 and 4) for Jordan Lake and Falls Lake compliance, and Council reviewed board/commission attendance records. During a lengthy review of the newly adopted Elected Official Social Media Policy (Item 16), Council confirmed keeping out a 'rumor' prohibition that Charlie Reece and others argued infringed First Amendment rights and could not be fairly enforced, added a guideline referencing state public records retention schedules, and planned to expand ArchiveSocial archiving to boards, commissions, and officials' public accounts. All formal votes—including an Open Space and Trails Commission appointment for Christine Gorman—passed without dissent.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Mayor Pro Tem, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With both Mayor Bill Bell and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden absent, the longest-serving member present (Steve Schewel) called the meeting to order. Council unanimously granted Cole-McFadden an excused absence and approved City Manager and City Clerk priority items, adding supplemental Item 16 (Elected Official Social Media Policy discussion) and Item 15.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: 525 Holloway Street Lead Paint Contamination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council granted Holly Dwan and a neighbor three minutes each to detail confirmed lead-paint contamination affecting properties neighboring 525 Holloway Street and request Council action on ordinance changes. The City Attorney noted active consultation with Neighborhood Improvement Services and civil litigation, acknowledging surprise at a regulatory gap where uncertified blasting caused lead flakes to spread across neighboring lots.

agenda_items.title: Item 1: Boards, Committees, and Commissions Attendance Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece questioned procedures for members showing zero percent attendance on the July 1, 2016–June 30, 2017 boards and commissions attendance report. The Clerk explained that low attendance triggers a letter to the respective board chair, often resulting in member resignations.

agenda_items.title: Items 3 & 4: North and South Durham Water Reclamation Facilities Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented Phase 1 construction and Contract Amendment #4 with Hazen and Sawyer for process improvements at the North and South Durham Water Reclamation Facilities, implementing 2011 master plans. Greeley highlighted floodwall protections at North Durham and treatment upgrades required for Jordan Lake and Falls Lake regulatory compliance.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Elected Official Social Media Policy Revisions and Public Records
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Council's Monday night vote, members finalized revisions to the Elected Official Social Media Policy: confirming deletion of a restriction against posting 'rumors' after Charlie Reece and others cited First Amendment concerns and unenforceability in censure proceedings, debating commercial spam moderation on City pages, and planning an ArchiveSocial contract amendment to capture boards/commissions and official accounts. Don Moffitt proposed adding guideline #8 referencing NC Department of Natural and Cultural Resources retention schedules, and Council requested clean and redlined drafts.

agenda_items.title: Open Space and Trails Commission Appointment and Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported Christine Gorman received four votes for the Open Space and Trails Commission appointment. Council then adopted the business meeting agenda placing Items 1–9 and 15 on consent and Item 16 on the General Business Agenda before adjourning at 4:09 PM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (4-vote appointment; unanimous voice vote on agenda)

disagreements.issue: Prohibiting 'Rumors' or Unverified Statements in the Elected Official Social Media Policy
disagreements.summary: Council reviewed whether to reinsert language barring elected officials from posting 'rumors' or unverified statements on social media, following differing interpretations from the Procedures Committee and City Manager.
disagreements.side_a_position: Exclude the 'rumor' prohibition from Item 3 of the social media policy.
side_a_arguments: Barring unconfirmed statements on personal social media accounts infringes First Amendment rights (such as political commentary or urgent safety warnings about downed power lines or flooded streets).
A 'rumor' standard is vague and cannot be fairly enforced in a Council censure motion, whereas existing language already forbids knowingly false statements.
disagreements.side_b_position: Address City Manager's concern about elected officials amplifying unverified rumors about City employees or incidents (while seeking a clearer definition).
side_b_arguments: Staff sought to curb the spread of false or unverified rumors affecting City employees and operations.
disagreements.resolution: Council members converged on keeping the 'rumor' phrase deleted from Item 3 and requested clean and redlined drafts reflecting Monday night's adopted policy plus public-records guidance.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Sept 18, 2017 (1 of 2)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council encountered three split votes across a contentious September 18, 2017 meeting alongside unanimous 7-0 approvals of the consent agenda, the Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall rezoning, and a resolution supporting continuation of the federal DACA program. On Item 21 (Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Boards), Council voted 4-3—with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece voting No—to adopt an amended interim policy deleting board/commission content-based speech rules while directing staff to review First Amendment and public-records critiques for Thursday's work session. On Item 19 (Barbee Road Retail, 160,000 sq ft at Barbee Road and NC 54), Council voted 6-1 on both the consistency statement and rezoning with Charlie Reece dissenting over traffic capacity and commercial need. Finally, on supplemental Item 22 (117 Goodwin Road split-zoning cleanup to Rural Residential for Eno Animal Hospital), Council divided 5-2—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Bill Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden voting No—after nearby seniors raised fears over property taxes, traffic, and noise.

agenda_items.title: Youth/School Announcements, Rosh Hashanah Absence, Supplemental Item 22, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council praised Police Chief C.J. Davis and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden's school integration legacy, heard announcements on Read for the Record, and granted Steve Schewel an excused absence (7-0) for Thursday's work session on Rosh Hashanah. Council voted 7-0 to add supplemental Item 22 (117 Goodwin Road rezoning) and passed the consent agenda 7-0 (including FY16-17 budget carryovers, NC 54 corridor study, Triangle ITS plan, Vision Zero Durham resolution, and DPAC excess seating).

agenda_items.title: Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Appointed Boards/Commissions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece and Don Moffitt requested delaying the policy to address late-breaking public and First Amendment/public-records concerns raised by NC Open Government Coalition Director Jonathan Jones and others, while Jillian Johnson warned against adopting potentially unconstitutional content-based restrictions on board pages. Mayor Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden insisted on putting an interim policy in place immediately, leading to a 4-3 substitute motion by Moffitt (seconded by Cole-McFadden) adopting Reece's Sections 3/5 revisions and deleting board content-based restrictions pending Thursday's work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Moffitt, Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis Aye; Johnson, Schewel, Reece Nay)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Z1700002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented a 0.5-acre rezoning along Renaissance Drive from CC(D) to CG(D) to incorporate the parcel into the existing 300,000-sq-ft Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall development plan without adding development (Planning Commission 10-0). With no public speakers, Council approved both the consistency statement and zoning ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Item — Barbee Road Retail (A1600011 / Z1600026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented Edens Land's request to change 14+ acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 from Office/RS-20 to Commercial/CG(D) for up to 160,000 sq ft of retail (Planning Commission 9-3). Proponent Jared Edens added floor proffers (at least 3 buildings, 15k–60k sq ft anchor, <=50% per building, no self-storage, internal sidewalks, west parcel cross-access, and conditional NC 54/Barbee left-turn signal), while opponent George Bryan warned NC 54 between Barbee and Revere Roads would exceed 110% capacity; Council passed both motions 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Zoning Map Change — 117 Goodwin Road (Eno Animal Hospital)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Brad Grinstead's request to unify a 1.5-acre split-zoned RS-20/RR parcel at 117 Goodwin Road under Rural Residential (RR)—a down-zoning that happens to permit an indoor-only veterinary clinic with no outdoor runs under 2 acres. Nearby residents Vera Hughes, Rev. Benny Torain, and Theresa Moody feared property tax spikes on seniors, noise, and traffic; Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Davis, and Moffitt voted 5-2 to approve, while Bell and Cole-McFadden voted No in deference to neighborhood seniors.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Continuation of the Federal DACA Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the resolution authored by Jillian Johnson supporting continuation of the federal Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program. Council unanimously adopted the resolution 7-0 before hearing public comment from Eliazar Posada (captured in Part 2 of the meeting video).

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence for Council Member Steve Schewel (Sept. 21 Work Session / Rosh Hashanah)
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Schewel requested an excused absence from Thursday's work session for Rosh Hashanah, which Council approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Add City Manager Priority Item (Supplemental Item 22: 117 Goodwin Road Zoning Map Change)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Bonfield requested adding supplemental Item 22 (inadvertently omitted from the work session agenda though properly advertised), and Council approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Amended Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Appointed Boards (Substitute Motion, Item 21)
votes.notes: Confirmed aloud on the record after electronic voting system misrecorded buttons.
votes.discussion_detail: Don Moffitt offered a substitute motion seconded by Cora Cole-McFadden to adopt the policy with Charlie Reece's edits to Sections 3 and 5, delete Subsection 3's content-based board restrictions flagged as First Amendment risks, and direct staff to review Jonathan Jones's email for Thursday's work session. After a voting-machine glitch, the Mayor and Clerk confirmed the 4-3 tally with Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis, and Moffitt voting Aye and Johnson, Schewel, and Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council closed the public hearing with no speakers and adopted the consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (CG(D)) for Hendrick Southpoint Auto Mall (Item 18)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the zoning map change incorporating the 0.5-acre Renaissance Drive parcel into the existing auto mall development plan 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Barbee Road Retail (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: Following debate over NC 54 congestion, commercial need, and applicant proffers, Council approved the consistency statement 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Approve Barbee Road Retail Plan Amendment and Zoning Map Change with Floor Proffers (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the FLUM amendment and CG(D) rezoning including proffers prohibiting self-storage, requiring 3+ buildings (<=50% floor area per building, 15k-60k anchor), internal pedestrian connections, contingent west cross-access, and conditional NC 54/Barbee turn-phase signalization 6-1, with Charlie Reece voting No.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 117 Goodwin Road Zoning Map Change (Item 22)
votes.notes: Bell and Cole-McFadden confirmed as the two Nays (`02:36:31`-`02:38:03`).
votes.discussion_detail: Cora Cole-McFadden stated she would vote No out of deference to neighborhood seniors' fears, and Mayor Bell confirmed he also voted No. After correcting voting-machine display confusion, the consistency statement passed 5-2.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance (RR) for 117 Goodwin Road (Item 22)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands correction confirmed Moffitt voted Aye and Bell/Cole-McFadden voted Nay.
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the Rural Residential rezoning for 117 Goodwin Road 5-2. When the electronic board misattributed a No vote to Don Moffitt, Moffitt confirmed by show of hands that he voted Yes, with Bill Bell and Cora Cole-McFadden casting the two No votes.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Supporting Continuation of Federal DACA Program (Item 23)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the DACA support resolution authored by Jillian Johnson 7-0, with Charlie Reece thanking Johnson and urging Congressional action.

disagreements.issue: Immediate Adoption vs. Delay of Elected Officials and Boards Social Media Policy (Item 21)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 over whether to immediately adopt an amended social media policy on the floor or refer it back to committee/work session to vet First Amendment and public-records objections raised by the NC Open Government Coalition.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt an interim social media policy immediately with floor amendments while scheduling work-session review of external legal critiques.
side_a_arguments: Council had already spent substantial committee time drafting guidelines and needed rules in place right away to prevent council members from posting personal views on official accounts.

Deleting Subsection 3's board content-based restrictions temporarily and incorporating Charlie Reece's Sections 3 and 5 edits mitigated immediate First Amendment concerns while leaving the policy open to Thursday amendments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay adoption and refer the policy back to the Procedures Committee or work session before voting.
side_b_arguments: Late addition to the prior work-session agenda deprived residents and open-government advocates of adequate notice and input.

NC Open Government Coalition Director Jonathan Jones raised serious First Amendment, public-records retention ('may' vs. 'shall'), and text-messaging gaps that require City Attorney vetting rather than rushed floor edits.
disagreements.resolution: Don Moffitt's substitute motion (seconded by Cora Cole-McFadden) passed 4-3, adopting the interim policy with floor edits and directing staff review for Thursday's work session.

disagreements.issue: Barbee Road Retail Comprehensive Plan Amendment and Rezoning (Item 19)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over rezoning 14+ acres at Barbee Road and NC 54 from Office/RS-20 to Commercial General for a 160,000-sq-ft shopping center.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the commercial rezoning with added design, anti-storage, cross-access, and transit/signal proffers.
side_a_arguments: Downtown/area-wide office land is already over-allocated by >100% for 30 years, and multi-family housing surrounding the intersection makes a walkable neighborhood grocery/retail node logical.

Floor proffers barring self-storage, capping anchor size at 60,000 sq ft across 3+ buildings, adding internal sidewalks and west cross-access, and improving Barbee/Grandale LOS mitigate design and traffic concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose commercial rezoning at the Barbee Road and NC 54 intersection.
side_b_arguments: The applicant failed to make a compelling case that another commercial center is needed near existing retail at Southpoint Mall, NC 55, and Fayetteville Road.
Nearby NC 54 segments (Barbee to Revere Road) already face severe congestion exceeding 110% of LOS D capacity.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and consolidated plan amendment/rezoning with proffers passed 6-1 with Charlie Reece dissenting.

disagreements.issue: 117 Goodwin Road Rezoning for Eno Animal Hospital (Item 22)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to unify 117 Goodwin Road under Rural Residential zoning to enable relocation of Eno Animal Hospital despite opposition from nearby elderly residents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve unifying the parcel under Rural Residential (RR) zoning.
side_a_arguments: Changing the split RS-20/RR parcel to RR is actually a residential down-zoning matching surrounding parcels rather than commercial rezoning, so it should not trigger commercial tax hikes.
UDO rules prohibit outdoor kennels on lots under two acres, and the clinic plans daytime hours and modern soundproofing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote No in deference to neighboring senior residents' concerns.
side_b_arguments: Nearby fixed-income seniors and church members fear increased traffic, noise, and property tax pressure in an established residential community.
Even if taxes may not legally rise from RR down-zoning, residents perceive real harm and deserve deference.
disagreements.resolution: Both the consistency statement and the RR zoning ordinance passed 5-2 with Mayor Bell and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden voting No.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council heard announcements of an upcoming resolution supporting the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program from Council Member Jillian Johnson, an update on Hurricane Irma shelter preparedness, and McDougald Terrace public safety concerns raised by resident Ashley alongside Housing Authority and Police leadership. Council Member Charlie Reece urged strengthening the Vision Zero traffic-safety resolution (Item 7) to emphasize street engineering and built-environment protections for cyclists and pedestrians. On Item 16, the Police Department presented its After-Action Report on the August 18, 2017 downtown counter-protest following the courthouse Confederate monument removal, detailing inter-agency coordination with Sheriff Andrews, open-carry firearm de-escalation, and balancing First Amendment rights with emergency vehicle access; Council members praised officers' professionalism and referenced a Human Relations Commission resolution opposing weapons at peaceful demonstrations. Council also reviewed the supplemental Social Media Policy for Elected Officials (Item 21) and unanimously approved the manager's priority items and meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, DACA Resolution Notice, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with Council Members Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel, and Eddie Davis/Mayor Pro Tem present on roll call. Jillian Johnson announced plans to introduce a DACA support resolution at the next business meeting, Don Moffitt recognized Community Development's HUD fiscal commendation, and Council unanimously approved manager priority items referring Item 17 (REA Commercial) back to staff and adding supplemental Item 21 (Social Media Policy).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote on priority items)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Hurricane Irma Briefing, and Downtown Traffic Study Carryover
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council highlighted FY 2016–17 carryover funding in Item 3 for the Downtown Durham Traffic Study—including evaluating conversion of the downtown loop to two-way traffic with NCDOT funding—and pulled Items 7 and 16. Staff also provided a brief Hurricane Irma readiness update noting Emergency Management leads shelter activation.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: McDougald Terrace Public Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: McDougald Terrace resident Ashley addressed Council on neighborhood public safety alongside Housing Authority and Police leadership. Officials acknowledged McDougald Terrace as a top priority and committed to holding a follow-up community meeting on site.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Vision Zero Traffic Safety Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece welcomed the Vision Zero resolution but advocated strengthening its language to prioritize roadway engineering and built-environment changes that physically protect pedestrians and cyclists even when drivers are distracted or speeding.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: August 18, 2017 Downtown Counter-Protest After-Action Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Police leadership reviewed the August 18 counter-protest response, explaining coordination with Sheriff Andrews around courthouse barricades, persuading several armed individuals not to enter crowds with weapons, clarifying initial confusion over Klan versus Sons of Confederate Veterans reports, and reopening streets for hospital and commuter access. Council members praised DPD and Sheriff deputies' professionalism and discussed a Human Relations Commission resolution opposing guns at peaceful demonstrations.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Social Media Policy for Elected Officials and Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members reviewed the draft Social Media Policy recommending separate official pages and protecting First Amendment rights, and asked the Clerk to notify boards and commissions chairs prior to Monday's GBA vote. Council then unanimously adopted the business meeting agenda.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Item 17 Back; Add Supplemental Item 21)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 17 (REA Commercial consolidated item) back to administration, added supplemental Item 21 (Social Media Policy), updated citizen speakers, and requested an Irma update.

votes.item_title: Adopt City Council Agenda (Consent 1–13; GBA 21; GBA Public Hearings 18–19)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name.
