meetings.title: Durham City Council January 3, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The seven-member Durham City Council convened on January 3, 2017, proclaiming January 2017 as Human Trafficking Awareness Month and celebrating Mayor Bill Bell's birthday before approving a City Attorney priority date correction (7-0) setting the municipal election public hearing for January 17, 2017. Council unanimously passed the consent agenda 7-0, including HOME CHDO affordable rental housing funds for Durham Community Land Trustees at 1207 Kent Street, downtown garage elevator modernization, a Wake County $7 vehicle registration tax interlocal agreement with GoTriangle, and acquisition of ~50.173 acres for a future park on North Hoover and Cheek Roads. On General Business Item 19, Council debated the $700,000 purchase price for ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for future Fire Station 18—exceeding the $600,000 appraised value of five lots—and approved the acquisition 6-1, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Eddie Davis voting Aye and Don Moffitt voting No.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Human Trafficking Awareness Month Proclamation, and Mayor's Birthday
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Council Member Eddie Davis led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Mayor Bell read a proclamation declaring January 2017 Human Trafficking Awareness Month, accepted by Charlene Reiss of Durham Crisis Response Center alongside outreach staff and Transforming Hope Ministries, followed by Council Member Davis leading Happy Birthday for Mayor Bell.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item: Municipal Election Process Public Hearing Date Correction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield and the City Clerk reported no priority items. City Attorney Patrick Baker corrected the proposed public hearing date for Consent Item 1 (Municipal Election Process) from January 16 to Tuesday, January 17, 2017, which Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (DCLT Kent St. Housing, Pay-by-Phone Parking, Garage Elevators, Wake Transit Tax, Eno Zone, Park Land, Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles including Item 1 (municipal election process), Item 3 (SunTrust Mortgage contract amendment), Item 4 (HOME CHDO funds to Durham Community Land Trustees for affordable rental housing at 1207 Kent Street), Item 5 (pay-by-phone parking), Item 6 (C.T. Wilson Construction downtown parking garage elevator modernization), Item 7 (Wake County $7 vehicle registration tax distribution interlocal with GoTriangle), Item 8 (Eno Economic Development Zone amendment with Orange County), Item 9 (November 2016 bid report), Item 10 (~50.173-acre future park acquisition at 632 N. Hoover Rd and 621 Cheek Rd), Item 11 (Duke Health FY16-17 grant), and Item 12 (Training-to-Work grant ordinance).

agenda_items.title: Proposed Acquisition of ~2.19 Acres for Future Fire Station 18 (Herndon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following City Attorney Patrick Baker's memo on potential involuntary taking, Council Member Don Moffitt apologized to the sellers for work-session phrasing and presented a valuation sheet arguing the $700,000 price exceeded the $600,000 appraised value once unbuilt lot improvements were deducted, while questioning siting near Parkwood Fire Station. General Services staff David Fleischer explained the seller planned to build homes themselves (foregoing 18-20% builder profit and incurring survey/subdivision costs), had graded and removed structures, and refused price reductions, while Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson cited call-response modeling and potential county consolidation of the Parkwood station. Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Jillian Johnson backed the staff recommendation as the only available parcel in the service epicenter, passing the purchase 6-1 with Moffitt opposed.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Correct Municipal Election Process Public Hearing Date to January 17, 2017

votes.notes: Mayor Bell announced: 'It passes six to one with Council Member Moffitt voting no.'
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $700,000 purchase contract for ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for Fire Station 18 after extended debate over the $100,000 premium above the $600,000 five-lot appraisal and coordination with Parkwood Fire Station.

disagreements.issue: Purchase Price Valuation and Siting for Fire Station 18 Land Acquisition (Item 19)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve a $700,000 contract to buy ~2.19 acres along Herndon Road for Fire Station 18, with Don Moffitt dissenting over paying above the $600,000 appraised value of five improved lots.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $700,000 negotiated purchase contract as the only viable site in Fire Station 18's target response area.
side_a_arguments: General Services confirmed the seller would not negotiate below $700,000, was foregoing home-building upside and incurring re-subdivision/sewer costs, and had graded and cleared the site.

Across-the-street Herndon family land is in permanent conservation trust, leaving no alternative sites short of eminent domain, and Fire Station 18 sits at the optimal call-service epicenter with potential county consolidation of Parkwood.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the $700,000 purchase price as exceeding fair market value.
side_b_arguments: The $600,000 appraisal assumed five finished, buildable lots, whereas the seller is not delivering water, stormwater sand filters/ponds, road paving, or impact fees—creating a substantial premium above net value.
Questioned why a new city fire station is needed near the existing Parkwood station.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve the $700,000 acquisition passed 6-1 at 00:44:09 with Don Moffitt voting No.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in the final work session of 2016, the Durham City Council reviewed consent items, citizen safety concerns, and major infrastructure and housing proposals. Key discussions included a housing stabilization and Southside property tax assistance proposal from Reinvestment Partners, park land acquisition on North Hoover and Cheek Roads, the Durham Bike+Walk Implementation Plan covering 75 draft corridors, and a proposed Mayor's Committee for Women that was held back for finalized bylaws and clarification of its role relative to the Durham County Women's Commission. Council also scrutinized pricing and potential condemnation options for a 2.19-acre parcel on Herndon Road for future Fire Station No. 18 and requested court/legislative timeline projections before triggering statutory deadlines on municipal election process changes. The Council approved the agenda by unopposed voice vote (5-0 among members recorded at roll call).

agenda_items.title: Fire Station No. 18 Land Acquisition & Southside Property Tax Assistance Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager flagged supplemental Item 19, carried over from the prior Council meeting, regarding acquiring approximately 2.19 acres at 6911 and 6919 Herndon Road for future Fire Station No. 18. Staff also reported compiling county tax office data on the Southside property tax assistance program alongside a new housing stabilization proposal from Reinvestment Partners following the November 22 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items: Housing, Reservoir Protection, Parkland & Workforce Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed and pulled several consent items for follow-up questions, including a SunTrust Mortgage contract amendment (Item 3) regarding alternatives to costly second mortgages for affordable homeownership, HOME CHDO funding for Durham Community Land Trustees at 1207 Kent Street (Item 4), and an Eno Economic Development Zone interlocal amendment praised for reservoir land protection (Item 8). Members also questioned General Services on public engagement for a 50-acre parkland purchase on North Hoover and Cheek Roads (Item 10), elevator modernization overruns in downtown parking garages (Item 6), tech contractor workforce diversity (Item 5), and reimbursement structure for the Training to Work grant (Item 12).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Safety, Maintenance, and Parking at Eagle Point Apartments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident of Jubilee Lane addressed Council regarding safety, property maintenance, and parking issues at Eagle Point Apartments following the recent fatal shooting of a 17-year-old boy. The speaker urged the city to push the apartment complex to install surveillance cameras, add security, and maintain police presence in the community.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Durham Mayor's Committee for Women
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Advocates presented a proposal to establish a Durham Mayor's Committee for Women modeled on San Francisco and other cities to conduct gender analysis of city budgets and address pay equity, reproductive justice, and domestic violence. Council members questioned whether bylaws were finalized, how appointments would align with standard publicly advertised advisory boards, and what the committee would do that the existing Durham County Women's Commission could not; the item was held from the agenda to resolve those details.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bike+Walk Implementation Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants and staff presented the Durham Bike+Walk Implementation Plan, outlining a draft list of 75 prioritized corridor and spot projects (such as North Roxboro Road) and planned neighborhood outreach through PACs and open houses. Discussion focused on balancing slower federal grant delivery timelines (four or more years) against faster Capital Improvement Program (CIP) funding for smaller projects.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Fire Station No. 18 Property Acquisition (Herndon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the proposed acquisition of ~2.19 acres on Herndon Road for future Fire Station No. 18, with concern raised that the city was being overcharged by the seller. Members requested that staff explore condemnation/eminent domain versus outright purchase and bring options back to a closed session before the January 3 Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Election Process Inquiry & Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before setting the agenda (consent Items 1 and 3-12, plus GBA Item 19, holding Item 2), Council discussed Item 1 on the municipal election process because adopting a resolution of intent triggers statutory timelines. Members requested projections on state court reviews and legislative action regarding state primaries to avoid holding redundant or unfinishable elections, then approved the agenda by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1, 3-12 and GBA Item 19)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition; Bill Bell and Don Moffitt did not answer the initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager summarized consent Items 1 and 3 through 12 and GBA Item 19, while Item 2 (Mayor's Women's Committee) was held back to resolve governance details.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 19, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized South Durham community volunteer Michael Wilson with the Neighborhood Spotlight Award, held a moment of silence for Dr. Deborah Saunders White's mother Irene Sanders and local football player Ty Brown, and unanimously referred a Herndon Road item to the December 22 work session while authorizing a closed session for attorney-client privilege. Council approved the consent agenda 7-0 after pulling four items for separate discussion and votes. All four pulled items subsequently passed 7-0: a letter of support for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit project, a $1 million-plus state-contract purchase of replacement Durham Police Department vehicles (over public objections calling for youth job training stipends instead), an interlocal agreement with Durham County for a 911 emergency communications facility, and an amendment to the nearly $2 million Employment and Training 2015-2017 grant project ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight Recognition (Michael Wilson) and Memorial Moments of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and the Department of Neighborhood Improvement Services presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Michael Wilson, a resident of Fitzpowell Apartments in South Durham recognized for his volunteerism with NCCU's Partnership for Healthy Durham and his church. Council also observed a moment of silence for Irene Sanders (mother of former NCCU Chancellor Dr. Deborah Saunders White) and football player Ty Brown, and heard council remarks praising the Scrap Exchange's 25th anniversary and Durham police officers exceeding service expectations.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Herndon Road Item to Administration for December 22 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented a priority item referring an item beside Herndon Road back to the administration, scheduling it for discussion at the December 22, 2016 work session.

agenda_items.title: Authorization of Closed Session for Attorney-Client Privileged Communication (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Assistant City Attorney requested a closed session pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privileged communication to be held in the second-floor City Council Committee Room. At the end of the meeting, the attorney clarified that a formal motion to enter closed session was also required before leaving the chamber.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-17, 22, 26; Excluding Pulled Items 16, 18, 21, 24 and Referred Item 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda titles including council minutes, multiple board and commission appointments, the FY 2017-2018 budget development schedule, CDBG and HOPWA agreements (Urban Ministries of Durham, Durham County DSS, and Durham Housing Authority), the Continuum of Care planning grant, Piedmont Reynolds/Southside Durham Community Land Trust loan extensions, the October 2016 bid report, pre-employment medical testing, and a Water Shortage Response Plan update. After clarifying that Item 10 was not pulled, council approved the remaining consent items excluding pulled Items 16, 18, 21, and 24 (and referred Item 20).

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project Letter of Support for Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda, the item sought a letter of support for funding the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project, with Danny Rogers of GoTriangle addressing the council. A council member emphasized remaining engaged on funding alternatives to uphold fiscal responsibility ahead of April 17, and Mayor Bell affirmed council members' right to ask questions before the letter of support was approved.

agenda_items.title: State Contract Purchase of Replacement Vehicles for Durham Police Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Victoria Peterson and Umar opposed spending over $1 million on replacement police vehicles, arguing the city had failed to fund youth job-training stipends to curb crime in East Durham and criticizing police shootings (referencing Frank Clark) and unmarked cars. Council Member Don Moffitt noted the replacements were requested by fleet maintenance based on vehicle wear and tear and moved approval.

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement Between Durham County and City of Durham for 911 Emergency Communications Facility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled for public comment on an interlocal agreement for design and construction of a joint 911 emergency communications facility, resident Victoria Peterson criticized low African American employment she observed at the new police station construction site and urged council to require reporting on how many Durham residents are hired on city-funded projects.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to City of Durham Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance (No. 14937)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson spoke on the nearly $2 million employment and training grant amendment, requesting outcome data on how many young men and women actually secured jobs after completing training. A council member commended staff's presentation and advised submitting specific questions ahead of council meetings so staff can prepare detailed figures.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Herndon Road Item to December 22 Work Session
votes.notes: Referred item back to administration for discussion at the December 22, 2016 work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority item referring the Herndon Road matter back to staff for the December 22 work session.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Accept Request for Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Initial approval of City Attorney priority request to hold closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Assistant City Attorney requested a closed session for attorney-client privileged communication under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), which passed 7-0.

votes.notes: Over $1 million state contract vehicle replacement recommended by fleet maintenance.
votes.discussion_detail: Public speakers Victoria Peterson and Umar objected to spending over $1 million on police vehicles rather than youth job training stipends and raised policing concerns. Council Member Don Moffitt noted fleet maintenance requested the replacements due to wear and tear and moved approval, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Interlocal Agreement for Design and Construction of 911 Emergency Communications Facility
votes.notes: Joint City-County 911 emergency communications facility agreement.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson urged council to require reporting on Durham resident and African American hiring on city construction projects before the interlocal agreement passed 7-0.

votes.notes: Nearly $2 million employment and training grant amendment.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson asked for job-placement outcome reports from prior training funds; council approved the amendment 7-0.

Council also heard annual performance and planning presentations on GoDurham transit service and updates to the Water Shortage Response Plan's drought triggers ahead of a formal resolution vote. All procedural motions—including priority items, setting the agenda with Items 8 and 23 referred back and Item 26 moved to consent, and two closed-session motions—passed unanimously by voice vote among the six members recorded present.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on Orange County's unanimous adoption of its light rail MOU paired with direction to its manager to seek renegotiation of the Durham-Orange funding split. Council and staff discussed the $135 million floor for local funding gaps, potential post-2020 federal MPO funds, Durham County's upcoming MOU vote, and submitting the financial plan to the FTA by year-end to enter the New Starts engineering phase.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Service Performance Annual Report (FY 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff presented the FY 2016 GoDurham annual report, detailing adjustments on Routes 2, 2A, and 3 to improve on-time performance, community outreach events, and headway and service-span constraints. Staff also reported partnering with GoTriangle to accelerate bus shelter construction, launching a new rider survey, and scoping a five-year transit plan.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Former Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden presented a resolution memorializing former City Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown, praising her civic, religious, and educational leadership and presenting the resolution to her family. Council Member Charlie Reece also highlighted the Durham County Fraternal Order of Police's annual Cops and Kids shopping event for 30 local children, and Mayor Bell recognized Board of County Commissioners Vice Chair James Hill.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Item 14 (Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan) to December 8 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested that Agenda Item 14, Fire and Police Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations, be referred back to administration and deferred to the December 8, 2016 work session for further discussion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-16, Including Referral of Item 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda covering the boards/commissions attendance report, Workforce Development Board appointment, November 2016 Street Maintenance Performance Audit, parking meter and Republic Parking contracts, Durham-Orange Light Rail right-of-way donation, water line and facility contracts, public safety radio replacement, DPAC seating replacement, Transformation in Ten funding, and the 2016 COPS Hiring Program grant ordinance. Council Member Don Moffitt noted 11 appointees with under 60% attendance would receive letters from the clerk and thanked Durham County commissioners for co-funding a community health worker for Transformation in Ten.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Ellis Road Townhouses (Continued from November 21, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Jacob Wiggins presented a request for a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, plan amendment, and zoning map change to Planned Development Residential across four contiguous parcels totaling approximately 25.6 acres on Ellis Road. The proposal included a $50,000 payment to the City of Durham for affordable housing prior to final plan approval; the remainder of the hearing and vote fell in a truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC1600001: Technical Revisions to Wireless Communication Facilities Regulations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented TC1600001, technical amendments to Section 5.3.3 (Wireless Communication Facilities) of the Unified Development Ordinance to maintain 2015 standards and comply with state and federal law, following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. With no public speakers, council unanimously approved both the UDO text amendment ordinance and the statement of consistency.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC1600004: Historic Preservation and General Process Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC1600004, clarifying and reorganizing UDO provisions for historic preservation, certificates of appropriateness, and application review and notification procedures, which the Planning Commission had recommended 11-1. With no public comment, council passed both the ordinance and the statement of consistency 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Triangle Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented the Triangle Church utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning request, reporting that city water mains had adequate capacity and that Budget and Management Services projected the annexation to be immediately revenue positive. Following no public comment, council unanimously approved the annexation/utility extension and initial zoning requests in two 7-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing: University-College Zoning District Addition (145-Foot Major Special Use Permit and Major Site Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council conducted a quasi-judicial hearing for a Major Special Use Permit and associated Major Site Plan proposing a 145-foot building height, exceeding the 120-foot height limit in the University-College zoning district. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Led by Mayor Bill Bell, the City Council reviewed contractor workforce diversity, Southside property tax impacts, Fire and Police compensation, and a major debate over integrating affordable housing into the planned downtown parking deck. Staff reported that adding 18 affordable housing units (Options B/C) to the $18 million construction-budget garage would add roughly $3.9 million-$4 million (over $215,000 per unit) and delay delivery by six months; Mayor Bell expressed openness to including the 18 units if feasible, whereas Council Member Steve Schewel raised doubts about diverting Dedicated Housing Funds needed for Liberty/Oldham, McDougald Terrace, and Habitat second mortgages. Council also paused in silence to honor former Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown and received a brief update on an unfolding McDougald Terrace incident. Motions approving the City Manager's priority items, setting the agenda (consent Items 1-17, GBA Items 18 and 21, and public hearings 23-26 and 29), and entering closed session on economic development incentives passed unanimously (6-0 among confirmed present members).

agenda_items.title: Contractor Diversity, McDougald Terrace Incident & Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden praised Mayor Bell's national reputation following the National League of Cities Summit, and a Council member asked the City Manager to obtain a written minority hiring and recruiting plan from a recent contractor with outlier low diversity rates. The City Manager then gave a brief update on a police incident at McDougald Terrace where a suspect was deceased, pulled Item 14 (Fire/Police compensation) for presentation, moved Item 31 (Ellis Road townhouses annexation) to GBA, and requested a closed session on economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Cynthia Denise Brown & Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council observed a moment of silence in memory of former Council Member Cynthia Denise Brown and thanked Cora Cole-McFadden and the City Clerk for preparing the memorializing resolution. Members also pulled several consent items for questioning, including parking contracts (Items 5 and 7, noting UBE data errors on Item 6), Light Rail right-of-way donation (Item 8), waterline replacement (Item 10), public safety radios (Item 12), DPAC seating (Item 13), and Transformation in Ten (Item 15).

agenda_items.title: Southside Homeowners Revaluation Tax Relief & Maintenance Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council heard about steep 2016 property tax increases affecting elderly, disabled, and low-income homeowners in the revitalized Southside neighborhood. Discussion noted that many affected residents also lacked savings for urgent home maintenance and identified homeowners who had been missed in earlier Southside rehabilitation phases.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Parking Garage Conceptual Design & Affordable Housing Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public remarks urging a more economical design, staff and Finance Director David Boyd reported that adding 18 affordable housing units (Options B/C) to the downtown parking garage would raise the ~$18M-$18.5M construction budget by ~$3.9M-$4M (over $215,000 per unit), delay the December 2018 target by six months, and require reallocating Dedicated Housing Funds already committed elsewhere. Mayor Bell expressed willingness to pursue the 18 units if funds could be found, while Steve Schewel questioned spending that amount per unit given competing redevelopment needs at Liberty/Oldham, McDougald Terrace, and Habitat second mortgages.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda & Closed Session on Incentives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the agenda with consent Items 1-17, GBA Items 18 and 21, and public hearings 23-26 and 29 (noting Item 31's hearing was closed), and confirmed Fire and Police compensation data would follow before or at the next meeting. Council then voted unanimously to enter closed session on an economic development incentive.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote passed without opposition; Eddie Davis did not answer initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Manager's priority items (pulling Item 14, moving Item 31 to GBA, and scheduling a closed session).

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed unanimously among confirmed present members; Eddie Davis did not answer initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent Items 1-17, GBA Items 18 and 21, and public hearings 23-26 and 29.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Economic Development Incentive)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously among confirmed present members; Eddie Davis did not answer initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session regarding an economic development incentive.

disagreements.issue: Integrating 18 Affordable Housing Units into the Downtown Parking Garage
disagreements.summary: During the Item 19 conceptual design review, Council members differed over whether to spend roughly $3.9 million-$4 million in scarce housing or fund-balance dollars to add 18 affordable apartments atop the planned downtown parking deck.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore funding the 18 affordable housing units alongside the urgent parking garage project.
side_a_arguments: Meets downtown parking space targets and timeline better than larger 40- or 78-unit tax-credit concepts.
Funds could potentially be identified from the Dedicated Housing Fund or fund balance if Council prioritizes the units.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question the cost-effectiveness of spending ~$215,000+ per unit on top of a parking deck given competing housing priorities.
side_b_arguments: Dedicated Housing Funds are already allocated and face major upcoming demands for Liberty/Oldham, McDougald Terrace redevelopment, and Habitat second mortgages.
Constructing apartments above a seven-story parking deck carries high per-square-foot costs and delays project delivery by six months.
disagreements.resolution: Informational work session discussion only; no formal vote was taken on selecting a housing option.

meetings.title: Durham City Council November 21, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized Neighborhood Spotlight Award recipient Marvin Eli and celebrated Durham's #1 Digital City ranking from the Center for Digital Government before hearing council remarks denouncing recent hate crimes and racist graffiti and reaffirming resolutions supporting immigrant youth, LGBTQ equality, and Durham's Muslim community. Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including acquisition of county-owned property for affordable housing and four sidewalk grants (the consent vote fell within a truncated section of the transcript). At the end of the meeting, council debated a contentious rezoning proposal near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill roads that the Planning Commission had unanimously opposed. After an initial electronic voting error, a corrected vote defeated the rezoning 1-6, with Eddie Davis casting the sole Aye vote and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Spotlight Award (Marvin Eli) and #1 Digital City Award Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Marvin Eli for volunteering his electrician skills, supporting HOA maintenance, and welcoming neighbors. Council also recognized Technology Solutions staff and Budget Director Martha Johnson after the Center for Digital Government named Durham the #1 ranked Digital City in its 125,000-249,999 population category, citing the city's new website and IT governance model.

agenda_items.title: Council Statement Condemning Hate Crimes and Reaffirming Civil Rights Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following playful remarks on a city five-mile race, council members delivered a statement denouncing recent hate displays in Durham, including racist graffiti near downtown and an incident targeting a council member. The remarks reaffirmed council's 2016 unanimous resolutions calling to halt federal immigration raids on Durham youth, opposing House Bill 2, and expressing solidarity with Durham's Muslim community.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (2017 Legislative Agenda, Affordable Housing Property Acquisition, Sidewalk Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read headings for consent items including minutes, a Human Relations Commission appointment, the 2017 council meeting schedule, the 2017 legislative agenda, acquisition of county-owned property for affordable housing, a Triangle Regional Model agreement with NC State University, and four sidewalk construction grants (LaSalle Street EB-5703, Raynor/Rainell Street EB-5704, NC 54 EB-5708, and North Duke Street EB-5715). The middle of the meeting, including the consent vote, was truncated in the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads (RS-20 Alternative)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated a controversial rezoning proposal involving traffic on Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill roads, clear-cutting, mass grading, sound abatement, and construction stormwater runoff, which the Planning Commission had unanimously recommended denying. Although Don Moffitt and Mayor Bell warned that by-right RS-20 development could lack proffered stormwater controls or buffers, Moffitt, Charlie Reece, Cora Cole-McFadden, Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, and Mayor Bell opposed the rezoning—citing inadequate early community engagement and neighborhood impacts—and defeated it 1-6 on a corrected voice/hand vote, with only Eddie Davis voting Aye.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed 1-6 (Ayes: Davis; Nays: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Moffitt)

votes.item_title: Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads
votes.notes: After several council members accidentally voted Aye electronically on a motion intended for denial, Mayor Bell conducted a clear voice/hand vote, with the clerk confirming Eddie Davis as the sole Aye and the motion failing 1-6.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Don Moffitt noted state law prohibits requiring conditions beyond RS-20 ordinance minimums without a development plan and warned RS-20 could allow more rooftops or lack stormwater retention and sound walls, yet announced he would vote to deny. Council Member Charlie Reece said this rezoning had consumed more of his time than any issue since taking office in Dec. 2015, criticized the national developer for waiting until after unanimous Planning Commission denial to offer substantial revisions, and weighed Durham's housing supply pressures against holding developers to higher standards. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden said she listened to neighborhood opposition, and Mayor Bell voiced concern about stormwater runoff costs falling on the city under RS-20 before joining the 6-member majority voting No.

disagreements.issue: Approval vs. Denial of Proposed Rezoning Near Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill Roads
disagreements.summary: Council split 1-6 in rejecting a revised rezoning proposal that the Planning Commission had unanimously recommended denying, weighing neighborhood opposition, late developer revisions, and stormwater/grading concerns against the risk of worse by-right RS-20 development.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support the rezoning proposal
side_a_arguments: Voted in favor of the revised development-plan rezoning proposal rather than leaving the site subject to by-right RS-20 development.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning proposal
side_b_arguments: Developer failed to engage neighbors in honest dialogue before receiving a unanimous negative recommendation from the Planning Commission, creating stark last-minute revisions.
Neighborhood residents raised substantial concerns over traffic on Kimball, Burini, and Cole Mill, mass grading, clear-cutting, sound abatement, and stormwater runoff.
As an attractive, growing city, Durham should hold national developers to high community standards rather than accepting inadequate initial proposals.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve the rezoning failed 1-6 on a corrected vote after an initial electronic button error.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, the City Council heard an opening post-election statement from Council Member Charlie Reece reaffirming Durham's commitment to inclusion, equality, and past resolutions supporting Muslim American residents and opposing House Bill 2. Police Chief C.J. Davis briefed Council on new General Orders expanding justice diversion and citations in lieu of arrest for Class 3 misdemeanor marijuana possession, while Council also pulled the police body-worn camera contract for review. Additional presentations covered RDU Airport Authority's $8.5 billion regional impact and $3.5M-$5M parking revenue system replacement, citizen budget advisory and participatory budgeting models, a Kessler Consulting waste stream audit and organics pilot, and an Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association stormwater critique of the Berini Drive rezoning. All formal motions—approving priority items, entering closed session on City of Durham v. Burkett, setting the agenda, and adjourning into closed session—passed unanimously among the six members recorded on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Council Reaffirmation of Inclusion, Muslim Support, and Opposition to HB2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the November 2016 election, Charlie Reece spoke to reassure anxious residents of Durham's shared values of inclusion, equality, and safety. He cited Council's recent resolution supporting Muslim American community members (drafted by Steve Schewel) and its earlier unanimous resolution opposing House Bill 2.

agenda_items.title: DPD Misdemeanor Marijuana Citation & Diversion General Orders; Burkett Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief C.J. Davis briefed Council on two General Orders promoting justice diversion and officer issuance of citations rather than arrests for Class 3 misdemeanor marijuana possession to help residents avoid criminal records. Council approved the Manager's priority items (including supplemental Items 27 and 29) and unanimously approved the City Attorney's closed-session request for City of Durham v. Burkett.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: Body-Worn Cameras, FLSA Status, and Q3 Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including the 2017 Council meeting schedule (Item 3), FLSA exempt status changes (Item 15), and pulled the contract for police body-worn cameras for questions. Presentations on resident budget engagement, RDU Airport Authority, and the 2016 Q3 Crime Report were also scheduled.

agenda_items.title: RDU Airport Authority Annual Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RDU officials presented the airport's $8.5 billion economic impact, over 10 million annual passengers, and federal MWBE/small-business contracting programs. They highlighted urgent runway funding needs, ongoing dialogue on commercial development, and a recommendation to scrap a failed $1.2 million parking revenue control system in favor of a $3.5M-$5M replacement.

agenda_items.title: Resident Engagement in the Budget Process & Participatory Budgeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented options for deepening resident engagement in budgeting, including forming a Citizen Budget Advisory Committee or expanding the existing CCIP committee's quarterly review role while aligning with existing strategic plans. Public speaker Aaron Parrish spoke in favor of adopting participatory budgeting.

agenda_items.title: Waste Characterization Study & Planned Organics Pilot Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Solid Waste and Kessler Consulting reviewed seasonal waste stream data (single-family, multifamily, and commercial) showing significant unrecycled paper and food waste. Staff outlined a planned organics composting pilot coordinating with Water Management's biosolids drying beds.

agenda_items.title: Berini Drive Assemblage Stormwater Modeling Critique & Procedural Caution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kathy Barnathan of the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association presented technical objections to Pulte's nitrogen and phosphorus stormwater modeling for the Berini Drive rezoning and urged Low Impact Development (LID) standards. The City Attorney cautioned Council against delving into the merits of a public hearing item set for a date certain without both sides present.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the agenda (consent Items 1-17, GBA Items 18 and 21, and public hearings 23-26 and 29) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including a stormwater audit, FY 2015-16 budget carryovers, the Big Jump project, and a resolution supporting Durham's Muslim community (pulled for remarks), though the consent vote occurred inside a truncated middle portion of the transcript. In the final public hearings, council unanimously approved a mixed-use development allowing up to 381 upper-story residential units, the 742 Avin/Avon Drive consolidated annexation, and the Copley Farm consolidated annexation after addressing a neighbor's sewer and sidewalk-gap concerns.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution Honoring Representative Paul Luebke (Paul Luebke Day, November 8, 2016)

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Housing Authority of the City of Durham Grant Funding Request
meetings.executive_summary: In a special meeting chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Durham City Council considered an urgent grant request for the Durham Housing Authority (DHA) and its nonprofit development arm, Development Ventures Inc. (DVI). Staff and DHA leadership explained that nearly two-year closing delays on the Morreene Road and Damar Court public housing rehabilitations had stalled developer fees, leaving DVI with $805,000 in sunk costs and DHA needing to eliminate an operating deficit to satisfy HUD closing requirements. Although Council members sharply questioned DHA/DVI board overlap, incomplete consolidated budget visibility, and the use of Dedicated Housing Funds to cover a past deficit rather than current housing construction, Council voted unanimously (7-0) to approve the Community Development staff recommendation. Council also unanimously approved preparing a resolution honoring the late NC Representative Paul Luebke.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority & Development Ventures Inc. Grant Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development staff and DHA's CEO presented a two-part grant request to eliminate an existing DHA operating deficit required by HUD before closing and to bridge cash flow for DVI after nearly two-year delays on the Morreene Road and Damar Court (102-unit) public housing rehabilitations. Council scrutinized DVI's governance overlap with DHA, sunk pre-development expenses ($805,000), lack of a full consolidated DHA operating budget in the packet (though staff cited clean audits), local/minority firm participation (noting DTW Architects), and using Dedicated Housing Funds to cure a past deficit. Council voted 7-0 to approve staff's recommendation.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring NC Representative Paul Luebke
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell noted the recent passing of NC Representative Paul Luebke and requested that the City Clerk prepare a Council resolution honoring him rather than a mayoral proclamation alone. Council moved, seconded, and approved preparing the resolution by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Community Development Staff Recommendation: Durham Housing Authority Grant Agreement
votes.notes: All seven members answered roll call and vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the Community Development Department recommendation on page 2 to provide grant funding to DHA/DVI to clear HUD closing requirements and bridge Morreene Road and Damar Court development delays.

votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed the City Clerk's Office to prepare a Council resolution honoring the late NC Representative Paul Luebke.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened and chaired by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with Mayor Bill Bell joining later, the City Council addressed Southside revaluation tax relief, a revised Durham ID incentive agreement, neighborhood lease terms, and urban forestry planning. After suspending the rules, Council approved an amended economic development agreement with Durham ID Phase One Developer LLC (Item 25); although Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson reiterated earlier reservations about the incentive model, both supported the revision because developer commitments held and city participation scaled down proportionally, with Johnson calling for Community Benefits Agreements on future deals. Council also referred a proposed 1017 Juniper Street lease with the Albright Community Association (Item 13) back to staff over its $1 million insurance requirement and reviewed a $45,000 street tree inventory and citywide canopy assessment.

agenda_items.title: Southside Property Revaluation Impact & City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized State Senator Mike Woodard and reported meeting with Southside homeowners alongside Jillian Johnson and Steve Schewel regarding sharp tax increases from the 2016 county property revaluation, urging city-county tax stabilization efforts. Council approved the City Manager's priority items (bringing forward supplemental Item 25 and recognizing Public Works Director Marvin Williams) by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: Muslim Resolution, DAP, Fire Station 9 & Planning Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including the FY16-17 budget carryover ordinance (Item 4), a resolution supporting Durham's Muslim community (Item 5), an Enterprise Community Partners contract (Item 6), a Durham Athletic Park agreement amendment (Item 9), Fire Station 9 architectural amendment (Item 12, pulled), and the SW-49C consultant project manager contract (Item 17). Members also previewed planning public hearings for Southpoint Trails 2, Berini Drive Assemblage, Ellis Road Commercial, and 7422 Auburn Drive.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Agreement Amendment: Durham ID Phase One Developer LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted to suspend the rules and take up supplemental Item 25, amending the economic development agreement with Durham ID Phase One Developer LLC. While Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson noted their prior skepticism toward the incentive's size and financing model—with Johnson advocating for Community Benefits Agreements in future projects—both supported the revision because developer commitments remained unchanged and city participation would drop proportionally if capital investment fell.

agenda_items.title: Albright Community Association Lease at 1017 Juniper Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jesse Gibson spoke on behalf of the Albright Community Association regarding renewing its lease for city-owned property at 1017 Juniper Street used for community and poverty-initiative efforts since 2010. Council expressed concern over the lease's $1 million liability insurance requirement and the precedent of city assistance with insurance costs, ultimately referring Item 13 back to administration.

agenda_items.title: Street Tree Inventory and Citywide Tree Canopy Assessment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Urban Forestry staff presented the $45,000 FY 2017 street tree inventory focusing on aging Willow Oaks within a core corridor (Junction, Guess, University, and West Murray) and a broader citywide tree canopy assessment spanning Treyburn to Scott King Road. Council discussed Duke University forest boundaries, Duke Energy tree-removal coordination, and addressing tree-deficient neighborhoods such as North Roxboro.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the agenda with consent Items 1-12 and 14-17, GBA public hearings 19-24, noting Items 18 and 25 were disposed of and Item 13 was referred back to staff.

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 17, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized MomsRising for thanking council's universal pre-K task force resolution, honored Forest Hills volunteer Sue Watson with a Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and deferred six public hearings (Items 15-20) to November 7 due to a Herald-Sun publication oversight. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 7 and 13, closed a public hearing on extending A&J Capital Corporation's economic development incentive deadline for 406 South Driver Street while directing the City Attorney to draft three contract clarifications by Thursday, and unanimously adopted a resolution supporting the Equal Rights Amendment (Item 7). On pulled Item 13—a Construction Manager at Risk guaranteed maximum price amendment with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex—the council split 6-1, passing with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson casting the lone Nay vote.

agenda_items.title: MomsRising Universal Pre-K Recognition, Neighborhood Spotlight (Sue Watson), and SNAP Challenge Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MomsRising steering committee member Jessica Burrows thanked council for supporting a universal pre-K task force and presented a card signed by young children, and Mayor Bell presented the Neighborhood Spotlight Award to Sue Watson of the Forest Hills Neighborhood Association. Council Member Charlie Reece also spoke about participating with Council Member Jillian Johnson in the $4.20/day NC SNAP Challenge and donating food savings to the Durham CROP Hunger Walk.

agenda_items.title: Deferral of Public Hearings (Items 15-20) to November 7, 2016 Due to Herald-Sun Publication Oversight
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager apologized for a second deferral of six public hearings (Items 15-20) caused by a Herald-Sun newspaper publication oversight and reported the issue was resolved so hearings could proceed on November 7, 2016.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 7 and 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved board appointments (Carolina Theatre, Convention & Visitors Bureau, Bike/Ped Commission, Historic Preservation Commission), the June/August 2016 Inventory Performance Audit, DCHC MPO database support, an emergency action plan contract for a critical 48-inch sewer main, a city auction resolution, and the August 2016 bid report, while pulling Item 7 and Item 13.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Amendment to Economic Development Incentive Agreement with A&J Capital Corporation (406 S. Driver Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey of Economic and Workforce Development presented a request to extend A&J Capital Corporation's completion deadline to December 31, 2017 for its $107,000 grant ($395,000 capital investment) to redevelop 406 South Driver Street into commercial bays and two second-floor apartments. Council Members Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt raised questions about incremental tax value ratios, contractor worker protections, and adding proportional incentive reductions if investment falls short, voting 7-0 to close the public hearing and have the City Attorney revise the contract by Thursday.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (closed public hearing and directed contract revisions)

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, the resolution urged Congress to lift the ERA ratification time limit and called on the NC General Assembly to ratify the Equal Rights Amendment. Speakers Sarah Delos Santos (Action NC) and Marina Groll (NC4ERA) applauded Durham as the first municipality in decades to re-engage with the ERA before council passed the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment (Balance of Trades) with LeChase Construction Services and CIP Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Jillian Johnson pulled Item 13 from the consent agenda solely to record a separate vote on the Police Headquarters Complex GMP amendment and CIP ordinance amendment without offering additional remarks. The item passed 6-1 with Johnson casting the sole Nay vote.

meetings.title: Special City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, this special work session began with the announcement of board and commission ballot results: Mark Lee received 7 votes, Dr. John Rott received 6 votes (with one unspecified member not voting for him), and a third appointment received 4 votes after Don Moffitt and Jillian Johnson changed their votes (individual voters for the other three votes on that 4-vote tally were not read into the transcript). The remainder of the session featured an extensive briefing by police staffing consultants and Chief C.J. Davis on Durham Police Department workload models—recommending 243 active patrol officers (up from 196) and sworn strength above 532 to maintain a 30% community-policing buffer. Sharp debate erupted when the consultant dismissed prior UNC and RTI racial-disparity traffic stop studies as materially flawed and criticized Council directives as causing organizational stress; Council Member Charlie Reece pushed back forcefully, defending the credibility of the UNC/RTI researchers, asserting Council oversight builds public trust, and questioning police rather than guidance counselors performing mentoring roles in schools.

agenda_items.title: Board & Commission Appointment Balloting Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon reconvening, the City Clerk announced ballot tallies for board and commission appointments: Mark Lee received 7 votes, Dr. John Rott received 6 votes, and Don Moffitt and Jillian Johnson changed their votes resulting in 4 votes for another appointment. Council then concluded that segment before moving to the police study briefing.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department Staffing & Operations Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants presented a workload-based patrol model showing Durham's obligated call-for-service workload at 37.26% versus a 30% target, indicating a need for 243 active patrol officers (up 47 from 196) and authorized strength above 532 to offset academy and field-training lag. The study also recommended District 5 and specialty unit reallocations and a co-production community policing model, while prompting sharp debate with Charlie Reece over the validity of UNC/RTI racial-bias stop studies, Council oversight of DPD, and police roles in schools. Police Chief C.J. Davis concluded by noting ongoing work on a department-wide disciplinary matrix including body camera compliance.

disagreements.issue: Police Department Oversight, Racial-Disparity Stop Studies & Police Role in Schools
disagreements.summary: During the police staffing study presentation, the consultant criticized Council policy directives, dismissed UNC and RTI racial-disparity traffic stop studies as flawed, and defended officers mentoring youth in schools, prompting strong pushback from Charlie Reece.
disagreements.side_a_position: DPD racial-disparity studies have material flaws, internal department-community dialogue should drive policing policy without rigid Council directives, and officers can positively mentor students in schools.
side_a_arguments: Prior traffic-stop studies (including Veil of Darkness) contain extraneous variables and cannot establish causal racial bias.
Council directives created organizational stress; the department should engage the community directly.
School-based officers can build positive relationships and pursue alternatives to arrest.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell arriving later), the City Council heard citizen advocacy for misdemeanor marijuana decriminalization/lowest-priority enforcement, reviewed major water/transit contracts, and debated sharp ridership declines on the Bull City Connector. FADE Coalition and Self-Help Credit Union speakers urged Council to mandate citations over arrests and make misdemeanor marijuana the lowest enforcement priority; Charlie Reece expressed personal support while noting other members had legal considerations. On Item 19, Council members questioned why staff eliminated busy Bull City Connector stops (including Durham Station) without formal Council approval, triggering a one-third drop in ridership, while staff cited Duke University's $350,000 co-funding and proposed evaluating fixes in the Five-Year Transit Plan. In end-of-meeting appointments, Julia Kate and Gary Davis each received 7 votes, while Robert Glenn received 6 votes for the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners (one unspecified member did not vote for Glenn).

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Water/Transit Contracts, Living Wage & Planning Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council accepted the City Manager's priority items (scheduling the US 70 corridor presentation and moving up the DOLRT NCCU extension item) and reviewed consent items, pulling the Williams Water Treatment Plant upgrade award (Item 11) and Police Headquarters Complex materials testing contract (Item 15). Members also noted Beechwood Cemetery improvements (Item 14), a minimum livable wage ordinance revision, GoDurham bus purchases, and combining Bethpage Village public hearings (Items 21-22).

agenda_items.title: FADE Coalition & Self-Help Petition on Misdemeanor Marijuana Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers from the FADE Coalition and Self-Help Credit Union asked Council to adopt an ordinance or resolution making misdemeanor marijuana possession the lowest police enforcement priority, require annual reporting, mandate citations over arrests, and bar public funds from targeting low-level marijuana offenses. Charlie Reece voiced support for the ordinance's goals while acknowledging colleagues had legal questions referencing Fayetteville's consent-search experience.

agenda_items.title: Bull City Connector Transit Service Performance & Route Changes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff reviewed the Bull City Connector's route modifications, which bypassed Durham Station and Duke South to cut ~7 minutes and reduce headways to 17 minutes but coincided with a one-third drop in ridership and severed direct access to Broad and Main Streets. Council members pressed staff on why the route change was presented informationally rather than for Council approval and asked about reverting the route, while staff pointed to Duke University's $350,000 funding partnership, $350,000 operating plus $400K-$450K capital costs per additional bus, and the upcoming Five-Year Transit Plan.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda & Advisory Board/Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted to set the agenda (consent Items 1-3 and 5-16, GBA public hearings 23-24, Item 4 referred back, and Items 17, 18, 25, 26, and 27 disposed of). The Clerk also announced 7-0 appointment votes for Julia Kate (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission) and Gary Davis, and a 6-vote appointment for Robert Glenn (Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council reviewed strong year-end fiscal performance, the Durham Station/Jackson-Pettigrew redevelopment RFQ, and potential changes to Durham's municipal election system. Finance reported FY 2015-16 general fund expenditures $7.6 million under budget and a $7.9 million revenue surplus, avoiding use of $10.5 million in budgeted reserves. On Item 23, staff outlined the February 2017 Master Development Agreement target and 2018-2020 LIHTC timeline for the Durham Station/Jackson-Pettigrew project while ensuring no Penny for Housing funds would be misused. On Item 1, Council debated replacing the October nonpartisan primary/November general election format with a November election using a 50%-plus-one majority threshold and runoff (proposed by Eddie Davis) versus nonpartisan plurality or keeping the current structure, ultimately referring Item 1 back for further work; all procedural and closed-session voice votes passed without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Berini Drive Referral, Item 3 Referral & Historic Preservation Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council accepted the City Manager's priority items—referring the Berini Drive rezoning (Item 13) back at the developer's request, adding supplemental citizen matters (Items 20-22), adding Item 23 (Durham Station RFQ), and scheduling a closed session. Council also voted to refer Item 3 back to the City Clerk's office and approved a motion regarding a Historic Preservation Commission vacancy/term.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015-16 Fourth Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Finance reported that FY 2015-16 general fund expenditures finished ~$7.6 million below budget alongside a ~$7.9 million revenue surplus, eliminating the need to draw $10.5 million from reserves and fund balance. Growth was driven by sales tax revenues, unbudgeted fiber-optic fees ($400,000), street cut permits ($400,000), and occupancy tax at 112% of budget.

agenda_items.title: Durham Station / Jackson-Pettigrew Development Project RFQ Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the RFQ timeline for the Durham Station / Jackson-Pettigrew redevelopment, targeting a Master Development Agreement by February 2017 and 2018 LIHTC awards with a December 2020 placed-in-service deadline. Council reviewed the multi-department evaluation committee (including Downtown Durham Inc. and potentially Durham County) and confirmed Penny for Housing funds would be protected.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Election Process Reform Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated alternatives to Durham's nonpartisan October primary and November general election format, including Eddie Davis's proposal for a November election with a 50%-plus-one majority threshold and runoff (similar to Raleigh/Chapel Hill) to boost turnout and reduce voter confusion seen in 2015. Members also noted drawbacks of pure nonpartisan plurality in close multi-candidate ward races and recalled 2009 public hearing concerns before referring Item 1 back for further study.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Agenda & Closed Session Motions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved setting the agenda (consent Items 2, 4, 6, 7, and 8; GBA public hearings 11, 12, and 14; Item 1 referred back) by voice vote. Council then voted to enter closed session, including for personnel review.

disagreements.issue: Municipal Election Format: October Primary/November General vs. November Election with 50%+1 Runoff
disagreements.summary: Council members weighed whether to keep Durham's existing nonpartisan October primary and November general election system or transition to a single November election with a 50%-plus-one majority runoff (or plurality) as proposed for discussion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move toward a November election with a 50%-plus-one majority threshold and runoff only when needed.
side_a_arguments: Eliminates unnecessary second elections in many cycles while preserving a majority runoff option.
Addresses voter confusion and low turnout experienced between the October primary and November general election in 2015.
disagreements.side_b_position: Exercise caution about altering the existing primary/general system, rejecting nonpartisan plurality for ward seats and noting prior public resistance and election-cost tradeoffs.
side_b_arguments: Nonpartisan plurality in multi-candidate ward races risks electing someone without a runoff opportunity.
2009 public hearing feedback reflected strong public concern against changes perceived as subverting democracy, and election cost alone should not deter voter participation.
disagreements.resolution: Item 1 was referred back without a vote on changing the municipal election format.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 6, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council recognized Scripps National Spelling Bee finalist Betty Lee-Him Closs, marked Water/Day Without Water and Hispanic Heritage Month, and held a moment of silence for late Human Relations Commission member Norm Swicker. Council referred Item 16 (Fendol Farms utility extension) to Public Works, accepted Durham Rescue Mission exclusion petitions for the Golden Belt historic district, struck Item 3 (municipal election process) to the Thursday work session, and passed the remaining consent agenda and Item 14 (2016 Holiday Parade report) 7-0. In the night's defining split vote on Item 21 (Golden Belt Local Historic District Preservation Plan boundaries), council voted 4-3 to approve the consultant-recommended boundaries—with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voting Aye, and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eddie Davis voting Nay—before passing a companion motion 7-0 and unanimously approving downtown parking meter fee changes (Item 7) following resident comments on Hunt Street.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations (Betty Lee-Him Closs, Water Awareness, Hispanic Heritage Month) and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Jillian Johnson presented a proclamation honoring Lucas Middle School rising eighth-grader Betty Lee-Him Closs for finishing 15th in the 2016 Scripps National Spelling Bee, and Mayor Bell recognized Water/Day Without Water and Hispanic Heritage Month (presented to Human Relations Manager James E. Davis Jr.). Council held a moment of silence for late HRC member Norm Swicker, praised joint city-county racial equity training, and heard Eddie Davis describe an upcoming law enforcement community panel.

agenda_items.title: Manager Referral of Item 16 (Fendol Farms) and Clerk Receipt of Golden Belt Exclusion Petitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 16 (Fendol Farms / formerly Doc Nichols utility extension agreement) back to Public Works at the City Manager's request. Council also voted 7-0 to accept the City Clerk's priority item noting petitions filed September 1, 2016 by Rev. Mills asking to exclude the Durham Rescue Mission from the Golden Belt Local Historic District.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 7, Referred Item 16, and Struck Item 3) and Item 14 (2016 Holiday Parade)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After pulling Item 7 (parking fees) and striking Item 3 (municipal election process, which had been continued to Thursday's work session), council approved the consent agenda 7-0—including Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit corridor plans, housing loan/mortgage items, water treatment plant contracts (Crowder Construction), the Great Loop pathway easement in Durham Central Park, and Durham Housing Authority Section 8 funding—followed by a 7-0 vote on Item 14 (2016 Durham Holiday Parade report).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Farrington Place South (7221 Farrington Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation petition, and zoning map change from Grayson Dare Homes for 5.5 non-contiguous acres at 7221 Farrington Road for single-family residential lots. The remainder of this item and Items 19-20/22-23 fell within a truncated middle portion of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Golden Belt Local Historic District Preservation Plan and Boundary Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming during council deliberations on Item 21, consultants from MDM Historical Consultants explained how historic maps and development patterns informed the proposed eastern boundary around the Durham Rescue Mission. While Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson argued the historic district would preserve compatible neighborhood architecture without obstructing the Rescue Mission's ongoing work (noting no other property owners opposed inclusion), Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eddie Davis opposed the boundary over property-owner freedom and Rescue Mission concerns; the boundary passed 4-3 and a companion consistency motion passed 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Ayes: Schewel, Johnson, Reece, Moffitt; Nays: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis); companion motion passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Ordinance to Change Parking Fees (Downtown Parking Meters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda, the ordinance established parking meter rates downtown, drawing testimony from Hunt Street resident Doug Henderson-James supporting meters to manage congestion from the growing Center for Senior Living. Council Members Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel clarified the vote set rates rather than specific meter locations and asked Transportation staff (Thomas Leathers) to explore residential parking permit options for Hunt Street before passing the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Refer Item 16 (Fendol Farms Utility Extension) to Public Works
votes.notes: Formerly known as Doc Nichols subdivision.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred back to Public Works at the City Manager's request.

votes.item_title: City Clerk Priority Item: Accept Golden Belt Historic District Exclusion Petitions
votes.notes: Petitions delivered Sept. 1, 2016 by Rev. Mills requesting Durham Rescue Mission exclusion from Golden Belt district.
votes.discussion_detail: Council formally accepted the clerk's priority item reporting receipt of the petitions 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 7, Referred Item 16, and Struck Item 3)
votes.notes: Item 3 (municipal election process) struck to Thursday's work session; Item 7 pulled by Mayor Bell.
votes.discussion_detail: Included DOLRT corridor plan, mortgage/housing authority items, water treatment contracts, Great Loop easement, and Section 8 funding request; passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 14: 2016 Durham Holiday Parade Report
votes.notes: General business item approved without debate.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Approve Golden Belt Local Historic District Boundary as Recommended by Consultant
votes.notes: Mayor Bell initially announced 5-2 before correcting the tally to 4-3 with Bell, Cole-McFadden, and Davis voting No.
votes.discussion_detail: Consultant Cynthia De Miranda (MDM Historical Consultants) explained how historic development patterns shaped the proposed eastern boundary. Council Member Steve Schewel moved the consultant-recommended boundary, backed by Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson, who argued it would not hinder current Rescue Mission operations and noted no other property owners objected. Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Eddie Davis voted No over property-owner freedom and Rescue Mission concerns.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consistency Statement (Golden Belt Local Historic District)
votes.notes: Companion consistency vote following the 4-3 boundary approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 7: Ordinance to Change Parking Fees (Downtown Parking Meters)
votes.notes: Established meter fee rates; DOT staff agreed to explore residential parking options on Hunt Street.
votes.discussion_detail: Hunt Street resident Doug Henderson-James spoke in support of parking meters to address Center for Senior Living spillover; Council Member Don Moffitt clarified the vote set rates rather than specific meter locations before passing 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Durham Rescue Mission and Eastern Boundary in Golden Belt Local Historic District
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 in approving the consultant-recommended boundaries for the Golden Belt Local Historic District despite petitions from the Durham Rescue Mission seeking exclusion from the eastern side of the district.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the consultant-recommended Golden Belt historic district boundaries
side_a_arguments: Boundaries follow historic maps and full mill-village development patterns identified by MDM Historical Consultants.
Historic district rules govern compatible future exterior construction and would not alter the Durham Rescue Mission's current operations.
No other property owners in the proposed district appeared at the hearing to request exclusion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the proposed eastern boundary including the Durham Rescue Mission
side_b_arguments: Property owners should retain freedom over how they use and modify their individual properties.
Concerns raised by the Durham Rescue Mission and Rev. Mills' exclusion petitions warranted opposing the full proposed boundary.
disagreements.resolution: Consultant-recommended boundary passed 4-3, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement vote.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council reviewed a 'City Hall on the Go' public service announcement, the municipal election reform process, Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit planning, a Section 8 funding request from the Durham Housing Authority, and extensive updates to the City's housing and non-residential building codes. On Jillian Johnson's motion, Council voted unanimously to place the municipal election process discussion on the next work session agenda after the City Attorney outlined the 2009 memo and statutory notice-of-intent procedures. Neighborhood Improvement Services presented proposed housing code amendments—covering roof vegetation, moisture/drainage, lead debris referrals, and non-resident landlord agents—prompting Council questions on impacts to low-wealth seniors, tenant hoarding, and corner-lot trash storage ahead of the public hearing. All motions, including priority items, two closed-session requests, placing elections on the next work session agenda, and setting the agenda, passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: City Hall on the Go PSA & Closed Session Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (previewing a 'City Hall on the Go' commercial scheduled for 490 cable airings, the Recreation Advisory Commission report, housing/building code presentations, and supplemental Item 25 for DHA Section 8 funding) and the City Attorney's request for two attorney-client closed-session consultations.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Election Process Statutory Procedure & Work Session Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney reviewed the 2009 public hearing minutes and explained the statutory process required to change municipal election methods (drafting a resolution of intent, holding a public hearing, and adopting an ordinance within 60 days). At Jillian Johnson's motion and second, Council voted unanimously to place the municipal election process discussion on the next work session agenda.

agenda_items.title: DOLRT Corridor Plan & Transportation/Parks Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled and discussed metered parking spaces (Item 8), signalized pedestrian upgrades (Item 9), the Great Loop pedestrian pathway easement in Durham Central Park (Item 13), and the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit corridor plan (Item 4, pulled by Jillian Johnson), with members asking about contractor location prior to voting.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority Section 8 Program Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Recreation Advisory Commission report (Item 17), Council discussed DHA's supplemental Section 8 funding request, emphasizing direct engagement with families and developing a strategic plan alongside Council and community stakeholders. Jillian Johnson sought clarification on whether the vote would appropriate money from fund balance or the alternate Penny for Housing option.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Modifications to Housing Code & Non-Residential Building Code
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Neighborhood Improvement Services presented Healthy Home Comparative Analysis updates and civil-penalty alignments for the housing and non-residential building codes, including guardrail safety, crawl space moisture/drainage, overhanging roof vegetation, non-resident owner agents, and state referral for lead hazards. Council members questioned citing owner-occupied homes for overhanging branches—citing burdens on low-wealth seniors—as well as owner liability for tenant hoarding and corner-lot trash storage rules, and confirmed they could adopt portions of the proposals at the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Agenda & Entering Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the agenda (consent Items 1-13, 15-17, and 25; GBA Item 14 for the Holiday Parade; and GBA public hearings 18-23) and voted unanimously to move into closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Motion passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Manager priority items including Item 17, Items 22-23, and supplemental Item 25.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Closed Session Items (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Motion passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved two attorney-client consultation items for closed session.

votes.item_title: Place Municipal Election Process Discussion on Next Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Jillian Johnson moved to place the municipal election process discussion on the next work session agenda.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Motion passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent Items 1-13, 15-17, and 25, GBA Item 14, and GBA public hearings 18-23.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Motion passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session at the conclusion of the open work session.
