meetings.title: Durham City Council August 15, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council issued proclamations for National Recovery Month and Women's Equality Day and welcomed members of the Youth Commission. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering Downtown Parking Garage design, testing, and CMAR contracts, a Duke University land lease, a HUD grant, and water/utility contracts, and heard the 2016 second-quarter crime report from newly appointed Police Chief Cerelyn Davis (truncated in the middle of the digest). In public hearings, council unanimously approved proactive East End / Eastern Connector land-use and zoning changes across seven areas—modifying staff's recommendation on a 7-0 motion by Don Moffitt to keep Area 2 as low-medium residential rather than industrial—and unanimously approved the Shannon Road Retail rezoning (Z1500036).

agenda_items.title: National Recovery Month and Women's Equality Day Proclamations and Youth Commission Welcome
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a National Recovery Month proclamation to Robert Davis and Paula Harrington of Recovery Community of Durham, highlighting addiction and mental health treatment gaps. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden presented the August 26 Women's Equality Day proclamation, and Youth Commission members introduced themselves.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Downtown Parking Garage Contracts, Duke Lease, HUD Grant, Water/Sewer Fees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council passed the consent agenda 7-0 without pulling items, approving board appointments, pipe/manhole repairs, Chapter 70-15 water/sewer connection fee updates, Downtown Parking Garage design/testing/CMAR contracts (Little Diversified, Falcon Engineering, Balfour Beatty), a Duke University land lease, a HUD Partnership Initiative Grant, a USGS streamflow agreement, an Emory Woods CIP amendment, and MUNIS software support.

agenda_items.title: 2016 Second Quarter Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Newly appointed Police Chief Cerelyn 'CJ' Davis thanked Mayor Bell, City Manager Tom Bonfield, and the council for welcoming her to Durham before presenting the 2016 second-quarter crime report; the substantive presentation fell within a truncated portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Eastern Connector Future Land Use Map and Zoning Changes (Areas 1-7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented proactive land use and zoning updates across seven areas near the Eastern Connector. Following questions about net industrial land, neighborhood park/commercial parcels near Andrew Avenue, and the Planning Commission's 8-4 split on Area 2 (Carr Road), Council Members Don Moffitt and Charlie Reece argued against redesignating Area 2 to industrial without an active applicant given surrounding residential designations; council voted 7-0 to adopt Future Land Use Map changes for Areas 1 and 3-7 while keeping Area 2 as low-medium residential, then approved zoning for all seven areas (7-0) and consistency (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036, 3230 & 3232 Shannon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin of Planning presented Z1500036 (1.913 acres, Planning Commission 11-0) for developer Robert Gaunum, represented by Jared Edens of Edens Land Corp. After confirming the site plan included full frontage sidewalk and a direct pedestrian connection to Parkway Plaza requested by the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, council passed the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 1): Future Land Use Map Changes for Eastern Connector Areas 1 and 3-7 (Retaining Area 2 as Low-Medium Residential)
votes.notes: Modified staff proposal by retaining Area 2 (Carr Road) as low-medium residential rather than changing it to industrial.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Members Don Moffitt and Charlie Reece agreed with the four dissenting Planning Commissioners that Area 2 should not be changed to industrial without an active developer request, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 2): Zoning Changes for All Seven Eastern Connector Areas
votes.notes: Adopted staff's recommended zoning changes across all seven areas.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Council Member Don Moffitt and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Vote 3): Consistency Statement for Eastern Connector Amendments
votes.notes: Consistency statement for Item 20.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Vote 1): Zoning Map Change — Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036)
votes.notes: 1.913 acres at 3230 & 3232 Shannon Road; included sidewalk and Parkway Plaza pedestrian connection on site plan.
votes.discussion_detail: Developer representative Jared Edens confirmed sidewalk and pedestrian connectivity were already included on the site plan under review; passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Vote 2): Consistency Statement — Shannon Road Retail (Z1500036)
votes.notes: Consistency statement for Z1500036.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 4, 2016 Work Session, all seven members of the Durham City Council were present with Mayor Bill Bell presiding. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (7-0), referred Item 1 (minutes approval) back to the City Clerk's office for proofreading (7-0), suspended the rules and approved Item 6 (7-0, 7-0), and set the agenda for the upcoming regular meeting (7-0). During Citizens Matters, residents urged City support for adult Scout leaders in local schools and presented a proposal for a local Commission/Council on Women, citing infant mortality disparities and affirming transgender inclusion while Council discussed staff support limits and a future Equal Rights Amendment resolution. Council also questioned staff on pre-construction and concept design alternatives incorporating affordable housing in the downtown parking garage project, and heard a 30-minute presentation on the proposed Golden Belt Local Historic District and Preservation Plan (noting unanimous Historic Preservation Commission support and a 7-4 Planning Commission vote over the southeast boundary) ahead of a September 6 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. and the Clerk called the roll with all seven Council members present. City Manager Tom Bonfield noted that Item 26 (Elizabeth Foster under Citizens Matters) would not appear, and City Clerk requested that Item 1 (City Council minutes) be referred back to the Clerk's office for proofreading. Council also suspended the rules and approved Item 6 before reviewing the remaining consent and public hearing items.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review of Departmental Items and Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and public hearing items including Water Management pipe rehabilitation and capital facility fees (Items 7-8), downtown parking garage project (Item 9), USGS rainfall and streamflow monitoring agreement (Item 14), Durham County road salt interlocal agreement (Item 16), software licensing (Item 17), Golden Belt Historic District presentation (Item 18), 2016 Q2 crime report deferred to August 15 (Item 19), Eastern Land Use Analysis A1600005/Z1600009 (Item 20), and Shannon Road Retail rezoning Z1500036 (Item 21).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: School Scouting Volunteers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker requested City assistance in recruiting adult volunteer leaders for Cub Scout packs and Girl Scout troops in Durham schools, noting ScoutReach scholarship funds are available through the Occoneechee Council. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden noted the City's employee volunteer leave policy and Council members discussed potential outreach through city employees and the police department.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Proposed Women's Council and Infant Mortality Disparities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A presenter advocated for establishing a Women's Council/Commission inclusive of transgender women, citing NC State Center for Health Statistics data showing Black infant mortality in Durham County (13.2 per 1,000 births) was more than three times the white rate (4.0 per 1,000) from 2010 to 2014. Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Eddie Davis cautioned that city staff capacity is stretched and internal officers would need to self-support the body, while Council Members Charlie Reece and Don Moffitt expressed support and Reece proposed bringing forward an Equal Rights Amendment resolution.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Parking Garage Pre-Construction and Affordable Housing Alternatives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned staff regarding the structure of pre-construction and design contracts (including Balfour Beatty's role in cost estimating, logistics, and scheduling) for the downtown parking garage. Staff explained that consultants would return within roughly two months with concept design alternatives and cost estimates incorporating affordable housing alongside the original parking deck program.

agenda_items.title: Golden Belt Local Historic District and Preservation Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants (MDM) and Planning staff presented the proposed Golden Belt Local Historic District designation, design review process, reinstated 15%-20% state historic rehabilitation tax credits, and boundary analysis, noting unanimous Historic Preservation Commission approval and a 7-4 Planning Commission vote over the southeast corner boundary. Council members questioned the relationship between historic design rules and housing affordability, asked staff to revise the affordable housing goal language before the September 6 public hearing, and heard public comments questioning housing prices and neighborhood representation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Ballots and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced ballot results for the Pedestrian and Bicycle Advisory Commission (7 votes), Workforce Development Board (Scott McGregor, 7 votes), Human Relations Commission (Michael Barton, 4 votes), and Durham Historic Preservation Commission (7 votes). Council then approved the agenda assignments placing Items 2-5 and 7-17 on consent, Item 19 on GBA, Items 20-21 on GBA Public Hearings, and disposing of Items 1, 6, 18, and 22-25.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 1, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council proclaimed August 2, 2016 as the 33rd annual National Night Out across 108 Durham neighborhoods, presented the inaugural Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and heard City Manager Tom Bonfield unveil the new 'City Hall on the Go' mobile outreach vehicle. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript covering the consent agenda vote and initial public hearings, council unanimously approved a public hearing item (7-0) and debated pulled Item 14 (Downtown Durham Inc. FY 2017 funding), where Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved to require quarterly diversity breakdowns of downtown businesses—specifically African American-owned firms—and residents. On pulled Item 27, approving the second Construction Manager at Risk guaranteed maximum price amendment with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex over public opposition prioritizing community investments and minority contracting transparency, council passed the amendment 6-1, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: 33rd Annual National Night Out Proclamation, Inaugural Neighborhood Spotlight Award, and 'City Hall on the Go' Unveiling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the National Night Out proclamation to Evan Allen ahead of August 2 events in 108 neighborhoods and presented the city's first Neighborhood Spotlight Award. City Manager Tom Bonfield also unveiled the new 'City Hall on the Go' mobile vehicle, coordinated by NIS to bring one-on-one staff services, job searching, and utility bill payments directly into neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Utility Bonds, Refuse Trucks, Fire Admin, Park Accessibility, Pulled Items 14 & 27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including board appointments, performance audits, a National League of Cities financial inclusion grant, FY 2017 Downtown Durham Inc. funding (later discussed under pulled Item 14), utility system revenue refunding bonds, automated refuse trucks, Fire Administration renovations, Downtown Parking Garage elevator modernization, park accessibility improvements, and the Police Headquarters CMAR second amendment (pulled as Item 27). The consent vote occurred inside a truncated middle portion of the transcript.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item (Downtown Security, Cochran Garage, and Downtown Durham Inc. Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after truncation, speakers addressed construction impacts, security in the Corcoran/Cochran parking garage, nighttime visibility of Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) ambassadors, and tracking African American business representation downtown via tax rolls. After council closed the public hearing, the item passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: FY 2017 Agreement to Fund Economic Development Programs and Services Operated by Downtown Durham Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden pulled Item 14 and moved that DDI provide quarterly deliverables reporting diversity breakdowns of existing downtown businesses, residents, new businesses locating downtown, and businesses leaving downtown, emphasizing concerns about African American-owned businesses. Another council member requested women-owned business data as well, and Victoria Peterson urged using tax records and outreach to ensure minority businesses know how to apply for funding; the transcript transitioned to Item 27 before recording a vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Vote not captured in transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR Guaranteed Maximum Price Second Amendment (LeChase Construction Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Assistant Director Gina Price presented the second GMP amendment (~$14M+ for earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, and site logistics) for the Police Headquarters Complex. Public speakers opposed spending $60 million/40% of the city budget on policing and building the headquarters instead of youth centers, affordable housing, infrastructure, and healthcare, while Victoria Peterson demanded exact African American firm participation figures (Price noted 83% M/WBE on package 1 and pending bids on package 2); Council Member Don Moffitt thanked the speakers before the item passed 6-1 with Jillian Johnson voting No.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Schewel, Reece, Davis, Moffitt; Nay: Johnson)

votes.item_title: Public Hearing Item (Downtown Security and DDI Services)
votes.notes: Preceded pulled Item 14; public hearing title occurred prior to digest truncation.
votes.discussion_detail: Speakers discussed Cochran/Corcoran parking garage security, DDI ambassador nighttime visibility and demographics, and tracking downtown business ownership before council closed the hearing and voted 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP Second Amendment with LeChase Construction Services
votes.notes: Second GMP package covering earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, and site logistics.
votes.discussion_detail: Public speakers urged council not to break ground on the Police Headquarters and instead redirect funds to affordable housing, infrastructure, youth centers, and healthcare, while Victoria Peterson pressed for African American-only subcontractor breakdowns excluding materials. Council Member Don Moffitt thanked residents for engaging and searching for new ways forward before the motion passed 6-1 with Council Member Jillian Johnson voting No.

disagreements.issue: Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP Second Amendment (Funding Policing Infrastructure vs. Community Investments)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve the second construction GMP package with LeChase Construction Services for the Police Headquarters Complex, with Council Member Jillian Johnson voting Nay amid community opposition urging council to halt the project and redirect funds to social infrastructure.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Police Headquarters Complex CMAR GMP second amendment
side_a_arguments: Proceed with the second construction scope (earthwork, foundations, concrete, structural steel, precast, site logistics) for the approved Police Headquarters Complex.
Staff noted 83% minority/women business participation on package one and committed to providing detailed breakdowns carving out materials.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the Police Headquarters GMP amendment
side_b_arguments: Public coalition speakers argued the city already spends ~40% of its budget ($60M) on policing and urged halting construction before breaking ground to invest instead in infrastructure, youth centers, affordable housing, and healthcare.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-1 with Jillian Johnson voting Nay.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 21, 2016 Work Session, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened and chaired the early portion of the meeting (leading a moment of silence for recent victims of community and police-related violence) before Mayor Bill Bell later assumed the chair, with all seven Council members participating. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (7-0), suspended the rules (7-0) and approved Item 22 awarding a construction services contract to Hockaday Mechanical Corporation for Edison Johnson Pool dehumidification and LED lighting improvements (7-0), and set the August 1, 2016 Council agenda (7-0). Council reviewed performance audits on the Citywide Strategic Plan and Economic Development Incentives, questioned staff on utility revenue refunding bonds, Morgan Street parking deck retail potential, and Downtown Durham Inc.'s (DDI) $12,000 special events funding while urging stronger goals for minority-owned businesses and diverse housing downtown. Finally, the Clerk reported board and commission ballot results, including a 4-4 tie for the second Board of Adjustment seat (behind Michael Shultz with 5 votes) that was placed on the August 1 General Business Agenda for a tie-breaking vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Announcements, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence regarding recent national tragedies and local violence, and proposed scheduling annual evaluations for the City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk on August 18 at 9:00 a.m. City Manager Tom Bonfield reported that Eva Lee (Item 38) would appear on August 4 instead and requested suspending the rules on Item 22 (Edison Johnson Pool equipment replacement) due to failing pool equipment during summer operations.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review of Departmental Contracts, Audits, and Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed and flagged items including the Strategic Plan and Economic Development Incentives audits (Items 10-11), Financial Inclusion grant (Item 13), DDI agreement (Item 14), Series 2016 utility revenue refunding bonds (Item 17), automated refuse trucks (Item 18), fire administration and parking garage projects (Items 19-20), Miss Lake land acquisition (Item 23), 101 West Chapel Hill St. easements (Item 24), Police Headquarters GMP second amendment with LeChase Construction Services (Item 27), street closings (Items 32-33), and Murphy USA rezoning Z1500035 (Item 34).

agenda_items.title: Edison Johnson Pool Dehumidification and LED Lighting Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following City Manager Bonfield's priority request citing failing pool equipment during summer use, Council suspended the rules and voted immediately to approve construction services with Hockaday Mechanical Corporation for dehumidification and LED lighting improvements at Edison Johnson Pool.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Job Access, Violence, and Sewer Backup Claim
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers addressed barriers facing residents who lack computer skills for online job applications and raised concerns about local shootings. Property owner Mr. Ali presented photos of basement sewage contamination caused by concrete-like material in a sewer line; Risk Management explained that while Water Management responded promptly, the City lacked prior constructive notice and acted under Sewer Ordinance Resolution 87-15.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Items: Incentives Audit, Refunding Bonds, Parking Deck, and DDI
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members praised the Economic Development Incentives audit for highlighting the need to verify job creation metrics by recipient firms. Staff explained Series 2016 utility bond refinancing and co-counsel roles, while Council members expressed concern about Morgan Street parking deck retail potential and urged Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) to incorporate goals for Black-owned businesses and diverse downtown housing alongside its $12,000 special events funding (World Beer Festival, CenterFest, and Southern Documentary Fund).

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Ballots and Setting the August 1 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported ballot votes for the Citizens Advisory Committee (Rebecca Winders, 7), Housing Appeals Board (Bert Rausch and John Green, 7 each), Appearance Commission (Mark Ribold, 4), Convention Center Authority (Jason Friday, 7), and Recreation Advisory Commission (7 each for two seats). For two Board of Adjustment seats, Michael Shultz received 5 votes while Ronald Rodney and a third nominee tied at 4 votes each, prompting placement on GBA Item 40 for a tie-breaker; Council then set the August 1 agenda.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council accepted City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority requests deferring Item 38 to August 4 and flagging Item 22 for immediate rule suspension.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Item 22 (Edison Johnson Pool)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council suspended the rules to act immediately on the failing Edison Johnson Pool equipment contract.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 22 (Edison Johnson Pool Dehumidification and LED Lighting Contract)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved construction services contract with Hockaday Mechanical Corporation for Edison Johnson Pool dehumidification and LED lighting improvements.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for the August 1, 2016 City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Consent items 1-21 and 23-31; GBA item 40 (Board of Adjustment tie-breaker); GBA public hearings 32-35; disposed items 22 and 36-39.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 20, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on June 20, 2016 with all seven members present, experiencing intermittent chamber microphone and voting display issues noted by City Manager Tom Bonfield. Early in the meeting, the council unanimously passed 7-0 resolutions of condolence for the Pulse nightclub massacre in Orlando, addressing violence among young African American males, and supporting Durham's local Faith ID initiative, along with adopting the FY 2016-17 non-exempt pay structure adjustment establishing a three-year path to a $15/hour minimum wage. In planning business, the council unanimously approved 7-0 the Witherspoon Rose Culture relocation on Garrett Road (A15-0023 / Z15-0037), three UDO text amendments (TC15-0002, TC15-0007, TC15-0006), four annexations/rezonings (Estates at Findle Farm, T.W. Alexander at NC 55, Crescent Drive right-of-way, and Herndon Road), and the Wilkerson Avenue street closing (SC1600004). However, after a lengthy public hearing over stormwater runoff, floodplain wetlands, and Colony Park buffering, the council defeated Pulte Homes' Cornwallis Road rezoning (Z15-0031), with Mayor Bill Bell, Steve Schewel, and Charlie Reece stating opposition on the record (exact electronic tally not verbally announced amid chamber AV issues) because the associated comprehensive plan amendment had failed on April 4. Following public debate over policing versus youth programming, the council adopted the FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan (voice/display confirmation without verbally announced tally, with Bill Bell, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt voicing support) and approved remaining pulled youth workforce and police psychological services contracts 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Memorializing Resolution for Angela Van Doren Langley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read and presented a memorializing resolution (previously adopted June 9, 2016) honoring former Durham City Council member Angela 'Angie' Van Doren Langley (1961-2016) for her advocacy for children, persons with disabilities, and affordable housing. Family friend Destiny Quick spoke in tribute.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Condolence and Support Following the Pulse Massacre in Orlando, Florida
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt introduced and read Supplemental Item 55 condemning the June 12, 2016 massacre at Pulse nightclub in Orlando that killed 49 people and wounded 53. The resolution expressed grief, condemned gun violence, and affirmed Durham's support for its LGBTQ and Latinx communities.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Action to Address Violence Among Young African American Males
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read a resolution addressing elevated homicide and incarceration rates affecting 15-to-24-year-old African American males and listing city youth, gang prevention, and workforce programs. Speaker Victoria Peterson later criticized the resolution at 03:00:00 as lacking concrete stipend funding compared to police headquarters spending.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of the Faith ID of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel highlighted the Faith ID partnership between El Centro Hispano, Immaculate Conception Church, partner congregations, and the Durham Police Department to provide community-issued identification after state legislation restricted acceptance of consular IDs. Director Pilar Rocha-Goldberg was recognized in attendance.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Supplemental Items 53 and 54 & AV Notice)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield introduced Supplemental Item 53 (Cornwallis Road zoning map change Z15-0031 carried over from June 6) and Supplemental Item 54 (FY 2016-17 non-exempt pay structure adjustment). He also cautioned council that chamber microphones and the electronic voting display were experiencing intermittent malfunctions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 5, 7, 8, 21, 25, 46, and 54)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items covering commissions, FY16 budget amendments, BPAC annual report, Duke Belt Line Trail master plan, water and sewer infrastructure contracts, radio renewal, aquatic master plan, and youth workforce contracts. Items 5, 8, 21, 25, 46, and 54 were held for separate action.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 Non-Exempt Pay Structure Adjustment Recommendation ($15/Hour Path)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell noted the staff-recommended non-exempt pay structure adjustment establishing a three-year path to a $15/hour minimum wage for city employees. A council member moved the item without objection.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment - 4800 Garrett Road / Witherspoon Rose Culture (A15-0023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented A15-0023 to change 4.5 acres at 4800 Garrett Road (former Yates Baptist Association site) from Office to Low Density Residential so Witherspoon Rose Culture could relocate from Watkins Road, freeing 8 acres near the proposed Patterson Place transit station. Nearby resident Margaret Cameron opposed potential traffic and noise, while proponents Dexter Smith and John Kent supported the downzoning and New Hope Creek bottomlands preservation.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - 4800 Garrett Road / Witherspoon Rose Culture (Z15-0037)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Companion rezoning Z15-0037 downzoned 4800 Garrett Road from Office Institutional to Rural Residential with committed elements for Witherspoon Rose Culture's relocation. No further opposition was raised.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Graphics and Signage (TC15-0002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC15-0002 updating graphics and signage provisions. No members of the public spoke on the item.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Statutory Updates (TC15-0007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on UDO text amendment TC15-0007 aligning local ordinance language with state statutory updates. No members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Reasonable Accommodation (TC15-0006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on UDO text amendment TC15-0006 establishing reasonable accommodation procedures. Speaker Victoria Peterson raised Americans with Disabilities Act accessibility concerns regarding City Council meetings and online streaming, and City Manager Bonfield noted staff was acquiring accessible devices for visually impaired attendees.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation, UEA & Initial Zoning - Estates at Findle Farm, Doc Nichols Road (BDG1500008 / Z15-0038)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a contiguous annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial RR-FJB zoning for 116 acres along Doc Nichols Road for a 200-unit residential development that BMS projected would be immediately revenue positive. Applicant Jared Edens noted approximately $860,000 in Lick Creek regional pump station reimbursement fees.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation, UEA, FLUM & Zoning - T.W. Alexander Drive at NC 55 (BDG1500015 / A15-0013 / Z15-0039)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented annexation, utility extension, FLUM amendment to Medium-High Density Residential, and rezoning to RS-M(D) for 192 to 300 multifamily units (townhomes and/or apartments) at T.W. Alexander Drive and NC 55. At council questioning, applicant Jared Edens proffered sidewalk construction (rather than payment in lieu) and confirmed a $500 per student school proffer.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Initial Zoning - Crescent Drive Right-of-Way (BDG1500016 / Z16-0010A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented a 2.36-acre contiguous right-of-way annexation and RS-20/MTC/FJB initial zoning for Crescent Drive adjacent to the approved Farrington Mixed Use development to allow public street upgrades.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation, UEA & Initial Zoning - Herndon Road at Massey's Chapel Road (BDG1500017 / Z16-0011A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented voluntary annexation, UEA, and RS-10/FJB zoning for 2.633 acres at Herndon Road and Massey's Chapel Road for four single-family homes, projected to be revenue positive.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Amending City-County Planning Department Fees (Chapter 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented FY 2017 Planning Department fee schedule updates under Chapter 6 aligned with service improvements under the Development Services Center. No public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing - Wilkerson Avenue (SC1600004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kyle Taylor presented street closing SC1600004 to permanently close 414.35 linear feet of Wilkerson Avenue bordered by Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC to consolidate parcels for a parking deck.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker advised that because the companion Comprehensive Plan amendment had been denied in a negative motion on April 4, a motion to renew was procedurally problematic and the rezoning remained inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan under the UDO. Pulte attorney Patrick Byker highlighted 3.672 units/acre (122 single-family homes), five 60% AMI affordable ownership homes, greenway easements, and a 50-foot buffer, while Colony Park attorney Jim Connor and scientist Curt Richardson opposed mass grading, floodplain stormwater wetlands, and Tanglewood stub-out issues. Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece stated they would not support the proposal due to floodplain impacts and UDO constraints, and Mayor Bell noted noncompliance with the Comprehensive Plan.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed (motion defeated; exact tally not verbally announced)

agenda_items.title: FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the pulled budget item, speakers Victoria Peterson, Nimasheena Burns/FADE-aligned resident, and Cathy Briesch opposed the $65M-$71M police headquarters and funding 20 additional police officers, urging stipends and restorative justice instead, while Steve Hopkins supported the 20 officers and headquarters for neighborhood safety. Council Member Don Moffitt noted the Bull City Connector would be studied in the five-year transit plan; Charlie Reece supported the dedicated housing penny, trail acquisition, and 20 officers including a NECD liaison; and Mayor Bell defended the budget's direction.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2017 Planning Department Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson questioned workforce participation and youth stipends on city development projects before council clarified Item 8 covered the Planning Department's annual work program.

agenda_items.title: Contract for Provision of Police Psychological Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled the ~$86,000 police psychological services contract to urge mental health crisis co-responders and mental health support for impacted community families.

agenda_items.title: Contract with Community Partnerships, Inc. (WIOA Youth Services / Durham YES Program)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson questioned whether the WIOA-funded Durham YES program serving 150 youth aged 16-24 reached public housing residents and urged expanded funding. OEWD staff James Dickens and program manager Coolidge Taylor reported serving 450 Summer Youth jobs and transitioning homeless families, earning diplomas/GEDs, and placing youth in college.

disagreements.issue: Cornwallis Road Property Rezoning (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes)
disagreements.summary: Neighborhood opponents and experts contested Pulte Homes' 40.95-acre single-family rezoning at 2417 West Cornwallis Road over floodplain stormwater structures, tree clear-cutting, Tanglewood stub-out connectivity, and Colony Park compatibility, while council ultimately defeated the rezoning due to noncompliance with the Comprehensive Plan.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defeat Z15-0031 due to Comprehensive Plan inconsistency, floodplain disturbance, and tree/stormwater impacts
side_a_arguments: Comprehensive Plan amendment A15-0009 was rejected on April 4, making Z15-0031 inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan under the UDO
Stormwater BMP wetlands should not remove trees from the 100-year floodplain above Sandy Creek
Developers failed to satisfy Colony Park residents on mass grading, density transition, and environmental protections
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve or defer Z15-0031 for infill single-family housing, affordable ownership units, and greenway links
side_b_arguments: Project offered 3.672 units/acre (122 single-family detached homes) as a transition between Colony Park and commercial/US 15-501
Developer proffered five affordable ownership homes at 60% AMI, 50-foot buffer, turn/bike lanes, and greenway trail easements
Applicant requested deferral to evaluate relocating stormwater BMPs outside the floodplain
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve Z15-0031 was defeated at 02:27:39 (exact electronic tally not verbally announced amid chamber AV issues).

disagreements.issue: FY 2016-17 Police Expansion Spending vs. Community Youth Investments
disagreements.summary: Community speakers challenged funding 20 new police officers and a $65M-$71M police headquarters in the FY 2016-17 budget, calling instead for youth job stipends and restorative justice investments, while council members defended balanced investments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reject adding 20 police officers and expensive police headquarters construction without addressing racial disparities and youth stipends
side_a_arguments: Public speakers noted disproportionate arrests (including resist/delay/obstruct) and fatal police encounters
Requested reallocating funds toward $2,000-$3,000/month stipends, restorative justice, and neighborhood ambassadors
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt the FY 2016-17 budget including 20 police positions, police headquarters CIP, dedicated housing penny, and trail investments
side_b_arguments: New officers improve priority-one response times, case clearances, and include a NECD community liaison requested by the Poverty Reduction Initiative
Budget raised dedicated housing funding to a full penny and funded fleet, greenway land acquisition, and retention measures
disagreements.resolution: FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 CIP adopted at 02:51:26 (exact tally not verbally announced).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 9, 2016 regular Work Session (the final work session of FY 2015-2016), Mayor Bill Bell presided with all seven Council members present. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (7-0), added Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's supplemental resolution addressing violence among young African American males (7-0), suspended the rules and adopted the Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations ahead of July 1 pay adjustments (7-0, 7-0), suspended the rules and adopted the Durham Public Schools Career and Technical Education grant project ordinance (7-0, 7-0), and set the June 20, 2016 Council agenda (7-0). Council also questioned OEWD staff on Item 20 (a state-funded employment and training grant with a 60-day execution deadline) before the transcript truncated prior to that vote. In the afternoon presentation on Item 45, canvassers and community partners shared results from knocking on 800-1,000 doors in Northeast Central Durham, recommending an expanded FY 2016-2017 urgent home repair and rehabilitation program and lower application barriers for elderly, disabled, and low-income homeowners.

agenda_items.title: Opening Comments and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt shared calculations from HR data indicating City employee raises since 2006 outpaced CPI inflation by over 9%, and highlighted teacher pay and student debt driving a fifth-grade drama teacher out of teaching. City Manager Tom Bonfield presented priority requests including rule suspensions for Items 19, 20, and 23, supplemental Items 45, 47-49, 51, and 52, and referring Item 50 (DDI funding agreement) back to administration, while the Clerk added supplemental Item 46 (resolution addressing violence among young African American males).

agenda_items.title: Compensation and Classification Plan Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To allow Human Resources to process compensation adjustments taking effect July 1, Council voted to suspend the rules and immediately approve the Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a motion to suspend the rules, OEWD staff (Jennifer Solomon) explained that state Department of Commerce federal pass-through funds carried a 60-day contracting deadline from the May 13 funding letter, prompting immediate action to preserve execution cushion. The transcript digest truncated during discussion before recording the final roll/voice vote, though the item was omitted from the June 20 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Career and Technical Education Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion of third-party workforce/grant continuity and police psychological services (Item 25), Council voted to suspend the rules and approve the Durham Public Schools Career and Technical Education grant project ordinance ahead of the July 1 fiscal start.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Stabilization in Northeast Central Durham Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters reported findings from knocking on 800-1,000 doors (nearly 200 conversations) in Northeast Central Durham, noting low-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners face major computer-access and form barriers to property tax relief and repairs, and recommending an expanded FY 2016-2017 rehab and urgent repair program. Council Member Jillian Johnson inquired about allocating unallocated dedicated housing funds; City Manager Tom Bonfield noted $200,000-$300,000 already budgeted for urgent repairs and offered a staff briefing on the repair backlog while Council discussed concentrated vs. scattered-site revitalization and Rebuilding Together in East Durham.

agenda_items.title: Set the Agenda for the June 20, 2016 City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved agenda placements for the June 20, 2016 regular meeting, assigning Items 1-5, 7-18, 21-22, 24-28, 46-49, and 51-52 to Consent, Items 29-38 to GBA Public Hearings, and listing Items 6, 19, 23, 39, 45, and 50 as disposed of, before adjourning at 3:41 p.m.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Preliminary FY 2016-2017 Budget (Flagged Items)
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 9, 2016 Special City Council Meeting on flagged FY 2016-2017 budget items, Mayor Bill Bell presided and no formal votes were taken. Budget Director Bertha Johnson walked through follow-up responses—including the revenue-neutral tax rate calculation, Business Improvement District (BID) assessed values and top taxpayers, Keep Durham Beautiful locations, and OEWD performance measures—before focusing on two primary flagged decision items: Human Resources' $15/hour minimum livable wage scenarios and Downtown Durham Inc.'s (DDI) BID budget. HR staff presented multi-year cost projections showing an increase of approximately $1.6 million over baseline to accelerate pay-grade minimums by 6% annually toward $15/hour while managing pay compression. Council also reviewed earmarking Poverty Reduction Initiative (PRI) funds pending staff vetting, requested a multi-year affordable housing revenue plan for the fall retreat, flagged continued interest in funding Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) training, and saw Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece push to allocate one-time funds for greenway trails in the Capital Improvement Plan prior to June 20 budget adoption.

agenda_items.title: Review of Budget Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson reviewed written follow-up responses on the revenue-neutral tax rate formula, BID assessed value growth and top five BID taxpayers, General Services lead paint and Keep Durham Beautiful project locations, OEWD performance metrics, and Parks and Recreation vendor-by-vendor costs. Council clarified that housing stabilization was not yet a formal budget decision item unless added to the discussion.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources Livable Wage ($15/Hour) Scenarios
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR staff presented alternative multi-year scenarios to raise the City's minimum livable wage to $15/hour starting July 1, 2016 or July 1, 2017, allowing pay-grade minimums to float upward by 6% per year (vs. 3% baseline) while keeping midpoints and maximums market-aligned. Staff projected a $1.6 million multi-year cost above baseline and explained how shifting minimum rates affects pay-grade differentials and compression.

agenda_items.title: PRI Funding, Dedicated Housing Revenue, CIT Training, Trails CIP, and BID Retention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed Poverty Reduction Initiative (PRI) funds would be earmarked in the budget but held pending summer vetting and Council authorization, and agreed to prepare a multi-year affordable housing funding proposal for the fall retreat. Council also flagged Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) training, while Council Members Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece advocated using one-time funds to advance five stalled CIP trails; Bertha Johnson concluded that the budget was balanced for June 20 adoption, with Council needing to decide on June 20 whether to retain 7% of BID revenue.

meetings.title: Durham City Council June 6, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At a five-and-a-half-hour meeting on June 6, 2016 with Council Member Charlie Reece excused absent all evening and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden excused at 03:50:25, the Durham City Council held public hearings on the FY 2016-17 budget and major land-use cases. Following reconsideration of a previously defeated plan amendment, the council passed the Hope Valley Commons Business Park comprehensive plan amendment (A15-0010) 5-1, with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, before approving the companion Z15-0023 rezoning 6-0. After Cole-McFadden's departure left five members seated, the council unanimously adopted Compact Neighborhood Tier policy updates (A15-0020) and boundary/FLUM updates for Erwin Road, South Square, Patterson Place, and Leigh Village 5-0 (after Moffitt's substitute motion on Leigh Village died for lack of a second), while approving the Alston Avenue Compact Neighborhood amendment (A15-0018) 4-1 with Jillian Johnson voting No and Bill Bell, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voting Aye. The council also approved the Police Headquarters CMAR demolition/GMP contract (Item 22) 4-1, with Jillian Johnson voting No and Bill Bell, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, after Johnson voiced opposition during the budget hearing and item vote; passed a $100,000 revitalization grant for 2201 Angier Avenue (Item 39) despite Johnson's concern over missing community benefits; and unanimously approved Habitable Space LLC (Item 40), a downtown parking garage design amendment (Item 13), and a restricted 549 Continental Drive sewer UEA (Item 43).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Council Member Charlie Reece
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell entertained a motion to excuse Council Member Charlie Reece from the June 6, 2016 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 22)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted on the consent agenda with Item 22 (Police Headquarters CMAR demolition/GMP contract) pulled by a public speaker for separate consideration.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change Continuance - Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the scheduled continuance request for Cornwallis Road Property (Z15-0031, Pulte Homes) and continued the public hearing to the June 20, 2016 City Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Code Amendments on Solid Waste, Undergrowth, Trash, and Junked Vehicles
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered Neighborhood Improvement Services / Priority Residential Improvement Program (PRIP) code amendments tightening enforcement timelines and penalties on overgrown lots, trash, and junk vehicles.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Revitalization Grant - 2201 Angier Avenue LLC ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Chris Dickey presented a $100,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant alongside $400,000 private investment (with $125,000 committed to Durham-based contractors) to renovate 2201 Angier Avenue for retail/service space. Jillian Johnson expressed discomfort voting for the grant without a tenant in place and legally binding community benefits/local hiring guarantees, while Eddie Davis, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Steve Schewel supported neighborhood commercial investment.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement - Habitable Space LLC ($100,000)

meetings.title: Special City Council Work Session - Affordable Housing Guidelines and Policies
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 2, 2016 Special City Council Work Session called to order by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell on his way), Council conducted an informational review of two major items without taking formal votes. First, Community Development and Enterprise Community Partners presented updated Affordable Housing Guidelines and Policies centered on expanding very-low-income rental housing, preserving affordability in appreciating historic neighborhoods (such as Northeast Central Durham and Southside), partnering with the Durham Housing Authority on higher-density redevelopment, adopting green building standards, and supporting affordable homeownership. Second, staff presented unvetted Poverty Reduction Initiative (PRI) task force budget proposals—including $200,000 for rental education and bilingual housing counseling, $66,490 for informal childcare provider training, regional bus passes, and Legal Aid targeting census tract 10.01, and $9,500+ for middle- and high-school mentoring/EDCI programs (roughly $285,000 overall). Council reached informal consensus to set funds aside in the budget while directing administration to vet the PRI proposals for redundancy, outside funding dependencies, and existing staff capacity before authorizing expenditures.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Guidelines and Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters outlined three core affordable housing goals: expanding affordable rental supply for very-low-income residents, preserving affordability in rapidly appreciating neighborhoods, and engaging the broader community. Key strategies included higher-density redevelopment of Durham Housing Authority properties, capturing market-rate development via density bonuses, adopting green building standards to lower utility costs and asthma triggers, strengthening Continuum of Care coordination, and providing long-term affordable homeownership and down payment assistance, with Council questioning Southside redevelopment costs vs. standard homeownership.

agenda_items.title: Poverty Reduction Initiative (PRI) Budget Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented unvetted PRI task force funding requests totaling roughly $285,000 across housing/rental education ($200,000 for counselors in target census tracts), early childhood/jobs ($66,490 for childcare provider training via Durham Tech and NCCU, regional bus passes, and a Legal Aid attorney in tract 10.01, minus a redundant $30,000-$35,000 communications coordinator), and education ($9,500 middle-school mentoring and EDCI expansion). Administration recommended earmarking funds in the budget and returning with vetted recommendations.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Legislative Breakfast
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 27, 2016 Special Legislative Breakfast, Mayor Bill Bell opened the meeting and Council met informally with Durham's North Carolina General Assembly delegation, taking no formal votes. Following a moment of silence in memory of former colleague Howard Clement, participants discussed state budget and policy proposals affecting Durham, including Senator Brown's sales tax redistribution bill and efforts in the Senate to lift the state light rail funding cap despite Senate leadership opposition. Delegation members briefed Council on body-worn camera access and civilian review legislation, clarified that two statewide police-involved shooting prosecution bills were not a 'Durham police misconduct bill,' and explained new two-vote requirements and opt-out protections for Municipal Service Districts. The group also reviewed Jordan Lake and Falls Lake environmental rules, City opposition to repealing landfill disposal bans on recyclable materials, and a DOT-backed bill diverting Wake County truck traffic onto Durham County roads, on which legislators urged Council to pass a formal opposition resolution quickly if it wished to stop the bill.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence for Howard Clement, Sales Tax, and Light Rail Cap
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the breakfast and Council observed a moment of silence for former Council Member Howard Clement before Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace moderated the legislative agenda. Legislators discussed the financial risks of Senator Brown's sales tax redistribution bill (more likely for the long session) and efforts by Senators Harrington and Rabon to lift the state light rail funding cap in the Senate budget despite opposition from Senate Leader Phil Berger.

agenda_items.title: Police Body Cameras, Misconduct Bills, and Municipal Service Districts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and legislators discussed state legislation governing public release of police body-camera footage and the role of civilian review boards or independent bodies when compelling public interest exists. Delegation members clarified that two filed bills requiring grand jury action and out-of-county/citizen-assisted prosecution in police-involved shootings were statewide measures rather than a 'Durham-specific' misconduct bill, and reviewed Municipal Service District legislation requiring two local votes and limiting opt-out 'donut holes.'

agenda_items.title: Environmental Regulations, DOT Truck Route Diversion, and 'Sanctuary Cities'
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants reviewed Jordan Lake rules and SolarBee project failure, regulatory reform bills, and the City's opposition to repealing landfill material bans that keep transfer-station recycling markets viable. Delegation members warned that an NC DOT-requested bill diverting trucks off Victory Church Road onto Carpenter Pond Road, Kemp Road, and NC 98 would require a formal Council opposition resolution immediately to halt it in the short session, and discussed why Durham's 2003 immigrant-relations resolution did not meet statutory 'sanctuary city' definitions.

meetings.title: City Council Budget Work Session FY 2016-2017 - Part II
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 25, 2016 FY 2016-2017 Budget Work Session (Part II), Council heard departmental budget and strategic-plan presentations without taking formal votes. Staff presented Strategic Plan Goal 3 initiatives covering affordable housing production, neighborhood code enforcement, the Beltline Master Plan ($2.5 million for land acquisition), GoDurham transit expansions, $2 million for Durham Rocks, and $1 million for street and sidewalk maintenance. Parks and Recreation detailed the transfer of six park and trail maintenance FTEs from General Services, facility fee waivers, $45,400 to restore the December 10 Holiday Parade, and a $60,000 trails condition assessment, while Fire and Emergency Communications (911) highlighted Fire Station 9 opening costs, KnoxBox key security, radio maintenance transfer, and exceeding the 90% national call-answering benchmark at 95%. At the close, staff summarized the four flagged budget items—livable wage and pay raises, an additional holiday, the BID/DDI budget, and Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) training—while Council Member Jillian Johnson voiced dissatisfaction that CIP trails and ball fields remained deferred.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 3 and Parks and Recreation Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined Goal 3 progress across affordable housing (225 units produced since FY15), community-centered code enforcement, $2.5 million for Beltline land acquisition, GoDurham route improvements, and street/sidewalk funding. Parks and Recreation presented the transfer of six landscaping/trails maintenance FTEs from General Services, $280,000+ in facility fee waivers, 100% audit compliance on half-penny parks/trails spending, $45,400 for the December 10 Holiday Parade, the Holton Career & Resource Center free programming pilot, and a $60,000 trails condition assessment.

agenda_items.title: Fire Department and Emergency Communications (911) Budget Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fire leadership reviewed station engagement meetings, station CAD monitors, operating increases for Fire Station 9 at Midland Terrace and Camden Avenue, KnoxBox key security equipment, the Junior Fire Marshal Academy, and Fire Academy diversity (two women among eight trainees). Emergency Communications reported answering 95% of 911 calls within 10 seconds, integrating radio maintenance staff and diagnostic equipment, and responded to a Council request to include raw call volume metrics next year.

agenda_items.title: Flagged Budget Items Wrap-Up and Trails CIP Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed the June 9 schedule (Southside Phase II ribbon cutting at 10:00 a.m. followed by flagged items) and listed four flagged budget items: livable wage and pay raises, an additional holiday, BID and DDI funding, and additional CIT training costs. Council Member Jillian Johnson expressed dissatisfaction that trails and ball fields were left out of the CIP even with fund balance capacity constraints noted by staff, urging that trails be prioritized next year rather than delayed until 2020.

meetings.title: City Council Budget Work Session FY 2016-2017
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 24, 2016 FY 2016-2017 Budget Work Session (Part I), Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order and presided while Mayor Bill Bell was en route, with no formal votes taken. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 5, 2016 Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided and Council unanimously voted to set the May 16, 2016 regular City Council agenda (7-0), placing Items 1-15 on Consent and Item 16 (the proposed FY 2016-2017 budget and FY 2017-2022 Capital Improvement Plan) on the General Business Agenda. During Citizens Matters, residents presented a list of deteriorating streets requesting expanded paving funds—prompting Council discussion of equity concerns with complaint-based street prioritization—and LGBTQ+ advocates (including Jake Brooks) urged Council to adopt police standard operating procedures protecting transgender and gender-nonconforming residents in response to HB2. Council also engaged in a sharp procedural and policy debate over the Procedures Committee proposal on work session start times: after debate over whether daytime work sessions exclude working citizens, a substitute motion affirming daytime work sessions and nighttime action meetings was routed to the next meeting's Consent Agenda over objections from Council Member Jillian Johnson (and an unnamed colleague) who argued non-unanimous items affecting public participation belonged on the General Business Agenda rather than Consent, while Mayor Bell and the City Attorney explained Consent allows public speakers whereas GBA discussion is discretionary. Finally, Council reviewed Southside redevelopment Phase 2 details and questioned contractors on Items 10 and 12 regarding minority workforce hiring practices.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Police Body Camera Remarks, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. Council Member Don Moffitt commended the Human Relations Commission's early policing reforms in response to FADE—particularly adopting police body-worn cameras prior to Ferguson—and Council pulled Items 10 (Reservoir Residuals Removal) and 12 (Citywide Security Assessment) while reviewing Items 11-16.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Street Repaving Requests and Pavement Equity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents submitted a highlighted list of streets needing repair beyond currently funded work and asked Council to allocate more paving dollars. Staff noted $1 million in additional repaving funds in the proposed budget and agreed to check pavement ratings (target 75 for collectors, 65 for residential), while a Council member cautioned against complaint-based paving models that favor residents with greater capacity to complain.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Transgender and Gender-Nonconforming Police SOPs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Jake Brooks urged Council and the Durham Police Department to enact standard operating procedures requiring officers to respect gender identity regardless of government ID during arrest, search, and detention housing, and to use correct pronouns. Citing East Point's policy revision, speakers asked that transgender community members be directly included in drafting the DPD language.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Start Time and Consent vs. GBA Placement Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated the Procedures Committee report on work session start times, with criticism that daytime work sessions hinder working residents compared to other major North Carolina cities, followed by a substitute motion affirming daytime work sessions and evening action meetings for placement on the next meeting's Consent Agenda. Council Member Jillian Johnson questioned placing a contested item on Consent instead of GBA; Mayor Bell and the City Attorney clarified that residents have a right to pull and speak on Consent items, whereas public comment on GBA items is discretionary.

agenda_items.title: Southside Phase 2 Review and Contractor Minority Hiring Practices
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel questioned Community Development staff (Richard Valzano) on Southside Phase 2 30-year affordability covenants, Deed of Trust figures, stormwater control, and site gate/fountain repairs. Council then interviewed contractors for Items 10 and 12 regarding workforce diversity and minority hiring practices, with a Council member offering referrals to qualified local candidates.

agenda_items.title: Set the Agenda for the May 16, 2016 City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the May 16, 2016 regular meeting agenda, assigning Items 1-15 to the Consent Agenda and Item 16 (proposed FY 2016-2017 budget and FY 2017-2022 CIP) to the General Business Agenda, before adjourning at 3:06 p.m.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript.

disagreements.issue: Work Session Start Times and Consent Agenda vs. GBA Placement
disagreements.summary: Council disagreed over keeping work sessions during the day versus moving them to evening hours for working residents, and over placing a substitute motion affirming daytime work sessions on the next meeting's Consent Agenda rather than the General Business Agenda (GBA).
disagreements.side_a_position: Affirm daytime work sessions alongside evening action meetings and place the substitute language on the Consent Agenda.
side_a_arguments: Holding work sessions during the day and action meetings at night allows different residents to attend one or the other.
Under Council rules, residents have a right to pull and speak on any Consent Agenda item, whereas public comment on GBA items is only at the presiding officer's discretion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold work sessions at times accessible to working citizens and place non-unanimous items on GBA rather than Consent.
side_b_arguments: Daytime work sessions force working residents to choose between earning a living and participating in city governance.
Pulling a Consent item forces residents to wait until the end of the meeting to speak, and Consent items are ordinarily expected to reflect unanimous agreement.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken on the start-time motion at the work session; Mayor Bell confirmed the substitute affirming daytime work sessions would be placed on the Consent Agenda two weeks later so any member or resident could pull it for discussion.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 2, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present on May 2, 2016, the Durham City Council began by unanimously adopting resolutions memorializing former council member Angela Langley and supporting Black boys and young men (both 7-0) and approving the consent agenda 7-0. Under General Business Item 13, Interim Police Chief Larry Smith presented the Q1 2016 Crime Report and reflected on community policing and rising armed robberies and drug-turf gun violence ahead of his June 24/July 1 retirement. The main policy debate centered on Item 19, the proposed new downtown parking garage procurement on Morgan Street: local developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could be delivered sooner and incorporate rooftop affordable housing units, while administration staff warned rebidding to add housing could push an RFP to early 2017 and delay downtown projects. Council voted unanimously 7-0 to defer the parking garage decision two weeks to the work session so staff could detail timeline constraints, affected downtown developments, and affordable housing options.

agenda_items.title: Mental Health Proclamation, Angela Langley Memorial Resolution, and Resolution Supporting Black Boys/Young Men
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a proclamation on mental health and substance abuse recovery, council voted 7-0 to draft a memorializing resolution for former Council Member Angela Langley and voted 7-0 in general support of a resolution addressing challenges facing Black boys and young men.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles, noting Items 13 and 19 were on the General Business Agenda, and council approved the full consent agenda unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Q1 2016 Crime Report Presentation by Interim Police Chief Larry Smith
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Police Chief Larry Smith presented Q1 2016 crime statistics, noting violent gun crime confiscations (68 firearms), elevated armed robberies, declining burglaries under predictive RAPID/WRAP patrol initiatives, and recent homicides linked to street-level drug turf disputes. Council members praised Smith's leadership ahead of his June 24 / July 1 retirement as incoming Chief Cerelyn 'CJ' Davis prepared to take office.

agenda_items.title: Proposed New Downtown Parking Garage Procurement and Affordable Housing Integration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Terry Bellamy/staff (with Terry/Tony Leathers) requested approval to maintain the existing procurement timeline for a new downtown parking garage without re-scoping to include affordable housing. Developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could finish in 2017 and support 24+ affordable apartments over retail, whereas Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell warned a mixed-use RFP/legal/management re-scope could delay an RFQ until early 2017; council unanimously voted 7-0 to defer two weeks for detailed answers.

votes.item_title: Resolution Memorializing Former Council Member Angela Langley
votes.notes: Unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Directed preparation/adoption of a resolution honoring Angela Langley.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Proposed New Downtown Parking Garage Procurement (Two-Week Deferral)
votes.notes: Steve Schewel seconded and asked staff to detail Opportunity Cost on Liberty/Old and transit-oriented affordable housing.
votes.discussion_detail: Deferred Item 19 for two weeks to the May work session for staff to explain the 2017 RFQ timeline, downtown developments dependent on garage timing, and tradeoffs of integrating affordable housing.

disagreements.issue: Downtown Parking Garage Delivery Timeline vs. Integrating Affordable Housing
disagreements.summary: Staff and Downtown Durham stakeholders urged proceeding immediately with the standalone Morgan Street parking garage procurement, while Mayor Bell and council members questioned why affordable housing over the garage had not been fully evaluated before voting 7-0 to defer two weeks for answers.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore integrating affordable housing and faster cast-in-place delivery before locking in standalone garage design
side_a_arguments: Developer Mark Anthony argued a cast-in-place deck could finish in 2017 and accommodate ~24 affordable housing units above retail
Unanswered questions remained on income targeting (60% vs 80% AMI), Penny for Housing subsidy, and Durham Community Land Trust management
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against re-scoping if multi-month legal/RFP delays stall critical downtown parking and divert housing staff
side_b_arguments: Staff estimated researching ownership/rental legalities and releasing a mixed-use RFQ could push procurement to early 2017
Steve Schewel cautioned that staff work on 24 garage units could pull capacity from Liberty Street and other large affordable housing priorities
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 at 01:57:00 to defer two weeks to allow staff to present feasibility details, staffing tradeoffs, and affected downtown developments.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden before Mayor Bill Bell arrived and assumed the chair, the April 7, 2016 City Council Work Session focused on the City Attorney's legal assessment of North Carolina House Bill 2 (Session Law 2016-3) and a resolution affirming LGBTQ rights and calling for HB2's repeal. The City Attorney advised that HB2 did not require changes to Durham's internal livable-wage or non-discrimination policies—since Durham did not apply those mandates to outside private contractors—while noting HB2 preempted local private-sector anti-discrimination ordinances and eliminated state court employment discrimination claims. Following public comments urging strong municipal leadership against HB2, Council unanimously passed a voice vote to suspend the rules (introduced by Council Member Charlie Reece) and then unanimously passed the resolution affirming LGBTQ dignity, encouraging gender-nonspecific restrooms in local businesses where practicable, and urging repeal of HB2. Council also reviewed routine consent items and unanimously approved the agenda for the upcoming regular meeting (Consent items 1-5 and GBA public hearing item 6) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Priority Items, and Administrative Consent Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the meeting while Council Member Charlie Reece gave notice of a resolution to be introduced under suspension of the rules. The City Manager reported no priority items, and Council reviewed consent items including street and infrastructure acceptances (Item 1), dam inspections and rehabilitation (Item 2), a liquid aluminum sulfate contract (Item 3), and an aquatic item (Item 4), as well as citizen matters.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Assessment of House Bill 2 (Session Law 2016-3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon arriving, Mayor Bill Bell asked the City Attorney to present his April 4 legal memo evaluating HB2's operational impacts on Durham. The City Attorney reported that Durham's internal non-discrimination and livable-wage policies remained valid because the city had not designated outside contractors under its livable-wage ordinance since 2013 and did not impose private-sector anti-discrimination mandates, though HB2 barred future local private-sector ordinances and removed state-court employment discrimination remedies. Discussion also noted National League of Cities executive committee support for keeping its 2017 City Summit in Charlotte to avoid penalizing Charlotte for state preemption.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Affirming LGBTQ Rights and Calling for Repeal of House Bill 2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously suspended its rules so Council Member Charlie Reece could introduce and read a resolution affirming the rights and dignity of LGBTQ residents, encouraging local businesses to offer gender-nonspecific restrooms where practicable, and calling on state leaders to repeal HB2. At Council Member Jillian Johnson's request, Mayor Bell opened the floor for three-minute comments from audience members, including Helena Craig, who thanked Council and urged proactive action and legal support against HB2. Council then adopted the resolution unanimously.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice votes to suspend rules and adopt resolution)

agenda_items.title: Set City Council Meeting Agenda and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt reminded the Mayor to set the upcoming City Council meeting agenda prior to adjournment. Council unanimously approved placing Items 1 through 5 on the Consent Agenda and Item 6 as a GBA public hearing.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Affordable Housing Workshop
meetings.executive_summary: At a Special City Council Workshop presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council and Community Development staff (led by Director Reginald Johnson and consultants from Enterprise Community Partners) conducted a strategic work session to translate Enterprise's affordable housing report into actionable city policy. Members discussed prioritizing deeply affordable rental housing for households below 30% and 50% of Area Median Income (AMI), coordinating with the Durham Housing Authority (DHA) on its 1,700 public housing units and upcoming Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) conversions, and avoiding concentrated poverty by favoring mixed-income models such as Southside Lofts. Council also explored leveraging city-owned downtown parcels for affordable housing alongside a broader 20-year downtown visioning effort and debated how to engage private developers through zoning density bonuses and UDO text amendments in compact neighborhoods. No formal motions or votes were taken; the session concluded with direction for the City Manager and Community Development staff to draft formal Affordable Housing Policy Guidelines—modeled on the city's budget guidelines—for future Council adoption.

agenda_items.title: Framing Priority Populations, Geographies, and DHA Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell convened the full Council to determine next steps on the Enterprise Community Partners affordable housing report. Community Development Director Reginald Johnson framed key decision points around priority populations (homeless, renters, and homeowners), geographic focus vs. citywide spending, and HUD's Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing requirements. Mayor Bell, Don Moffitt, and Eddie Davis emphasized targeting households below 30% to 50% AMI while coordinating with the Durham Housing Authority on its 1,700 public housing units, Section 8 vouchers, and RAD redevelopment to create mixed-income communities rather than concentrated poverty.

agenda_items.title: Downtown City-Owned Property Leverage and Eastern Downtown Visioning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Council examined whether city-owned downtown properties (and potential county-donated land) could be leveraged to maximize affordable rental housing or whether the city should undertake a broader 20-year visioning plan for eastern downtown addressing market-rate housing, commercial space, and parking displacement. Consultants sought clear Council direction on focusing resources on very affordable rentals and stabilizing very-low-income homeowners.

agenda_items.title: Private Developer Incentives and Compact Neighborhood Density Bonuses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed Mayor Bell's proposal to engage private market developers through incentive structures—such as zoning density bonuses tied to a 15% affordable housing goal—without exhausting city cash reserves. Planning and housing staff discussed form-based compact neighborhood zoning tiers (Core, Support 1, Support 2), ongoing UDO text amendments, and the tradeoff between master planning and piecemeal developer requests.

agenda_items.title: Mixed-Income LIHTC Development and Direction for Policy Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants explained Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) scale constraints (typically ~80 units max) and warned against geographically isolating extreme poverty. At the conclusion of the workshop, staff confirmed they had sufficient Council input to draft formal Affordable Housing Policy Guidelines—similar to annual budget guidelines—to bring back for Council action before reconvening at 1:00 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 4, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: On April 4, 2016, all seven Durham City Council members addressed major land-use disputes, an industrial recruitment incentive, and municipal workforce concerns. After unanimously approving Rosewalk at Club Boulevard (Z15-0020) 7-0, West Point 751 Revision 3 7-0, and the Acadia/Greston street closing 7-0, the council split 3-4 to defeat Item 19, the Hope Valley Commons Business Park comprehensive plan amendment (A15-0010), with Bill Bell, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, and Charlie Reece voting No and Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, and Eddie Davis voting Aye, before continuing companion rezoning Z15-0023 for four cycles. On Item 23, the Cornwallis Road comprehensive plan amendment for Pulte Homes, the council voted 6-1 to adopt the Planning Commission's recommendation to deny the amendment, with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting Aye, and then voted 6-1 (Don Moffitt voting No) to continue companion rezoning Z15-0031 until June 6. The council also unanimously approved 7-0 a $200,000 economic development incentive for Aurobindo Pharma USA (200 manufacturing/R&D jobs) and adopted FY 2016-17 Budget Development Guidelines 7-0 after UE150 municipal workers urged pay, promotion, and grievance reforms.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items including Campus Hills Pool design, Google Fiber network hub agreement, employee fitness dashboard, and Eno River watershed plan, while pulling Item 4 (FY 2016-17 Budget Development Guidelines) for public speakers.
