agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden raised a racial equity concern comparing Moogfest funding with the Art of Cool festival's pending $20,000 request, noting Art of Cool is led by an African American woman. City staff confirmed OEWD was reviewing late financial submissions from Art of Cool ahead of the festival.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Rosewalk at Club Boulevard (Z15-0020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kyle Taylor presented Z15-0020 rezoning 5.59 acres on West Club Boulevard to PDR 10.8 for up to 60 residential units. Developer Robert Chapman and Durham Community Land Trust director Selina Mack described a voluntary letter of intent to include at least 10 affordable units, while Steve Schewel and Mayor Bell asked staff to explore modernizing Durham's tree preservation and mass grading ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Hope Valley Commons Business Park Plan Amendment (A15-0010) and Rezoning (Z15-0023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented A15-0010 to reclassify 4.5 acres near NC 54 and NC 751 from Office to Commercial to enable a self-storage facility. After neighborhood/planning concerns, the plan amendment failed 3-4 with Bill Bell, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, and Charlie Reece voting No; following procedural discussion of reconsideration rules, a motion to reconsider failed for lack of a second and council voted to continue companion rezoning Z15-0023 for four cycles.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: After extensive testimony from environmental scientists Kurt Richardson, Patrick Halpin (Duke Forest), Tom Stuseger, and Colony Park residents warning of stormwater flooding into Sandy Creek, floodplain clear-cutting of 3,000-7,000 trees, and US 15-501 traffic hazards, council voted 6-1 to adopt the Planning Commission's recommendation to deny the Comprehensive Plan amendment, with only Don Moffitt voting No. Pulte attorney Patrick Byker then requested a continuance on companion rezoning Z15-0031, which passed 6-1 to June 6 (Don Moffitt voting No).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the March 24, 2016 City Council Work Session excused the absence of Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden due to a family hospice matter and acted on seven formal votes. Council unanimously suspended the rules to approve Item 13 (an Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance superseding Ordinance #14891 so 70% of grant funds could be expended by year-end) and also approved the City Manager's priority items, a DPAC Oversight Committee appointment (Keeon Brown receiving five votes), the agenda for the next regular meeting, and entry into closed session. During citizen matters, residents spoke on homelessness, urged Durham to pass a 100% renewable energy and solar resolution (which Council referred to the administration for review), and drew a reminder from Mayor Bell to keep public comments focused on local issues rather than national political candidates. Council also reviewed FY 2016-17 budget guidelines, heard a request from the Art of Cool Festival for increased city funding compared to Full Frame and Moogfest (referred to OEWD for review), and discussed quantitative census-tract and qualitative methods for tracking gentrification.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excusal of Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and Council unanimously excused Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's absence while she attended to her brother in hospice. The City Manager requested suspending the rules to vote on Item 13 (Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance) and noted Item 17 (Moogfest presentation) had a 1:45 PM time certain with no action proposed.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice votes excusing absence, accepting priority items, and suspending rules for Item 13)

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent Items and Approval of Item 13 Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including sending back a committee appointment item for re-advertising because applicants submitted no background information, pulling Item 4 (FY 2016-17 Budget Development Guidelines) and Item 5 (Gentrification discussion), and reviewing transit vehicle purchases (Item 8), installment financing (Item 9), Campus Hills pool dehumidification (Item 10), Google network license agreement (Item 11), employee fitness trackers (Item 12), Ellerbe Creek USGS agreement (Item 14), and planning items (Items 19-24). Under the suspended rules, Council approved Item 13, the Employment and Training 2015-2017 Grant Project Ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Homelessness, 100% Clean Energy Proposal, and Comment Scope
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Nelson highlighted housing affordability barriers for shelter residents, and Liz Gazelle urged Council to adopt a clean energy resolution targeting 100% renewable energy, solar goals, and energy efficiency programs using Clean Tech Center and DOE resources; Council referred the clean energy request to the city administration for a response. Speaker John Tarantino performed a politically themed song, prompting Mayor Bell to state that public comment periods should address local issues rather than national or local political candidates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Referred clean energy proposal to administration

agenda_items.title: Budget Guidelines and Art of Cool Festival Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed FY 2016-17 budget development guidelines and heard from Art of Cool Festival organizer Cicely regarding declining city grant allocations ($8,250 in 2014 down to $5,000-$6,000) and a request for $20,000-$25,000 in additional support, noting an estimated $1.6 million economic impact and Hayti Heritage Center transit/shuttle challenges. Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Jillian Johnson voiced interest in exploring additional support relative to Full Frame ($55,000 grant) and Moogfest, and the City Manager agreed to review the request through OEWD's budget and report back in April.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Gentrification Measurement and Census Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members examined methodologies for defining and mapping gentrification across Durham census tracts using 1990-2010 data, Brookings Institution frameworks, and property revaluation records. Jillian Johnson and Don Moffitt discussed balancing quantitative census thresholds with qualitative measures capturing changes in neighborhood character and resident displacement.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment Tally, Setting Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced that Keeon Brown received five votes for appointment to the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Oversight Committee. Council then approved the upcoming regular meeting agenda (Consent items 1, 2, 4, 6-16; GBA items 2, 3, and 17; GBA public hearings 18-24) and voted to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 21, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Returning from a February 15 continuance with all seven members present on March 21, 2016, the Durham City Council held decisive votes on two major transit-corridor rezonings in Southwest Durham. After intense debate pitting the council's 15% affordable housing goal and comprehensive station-area design planning against avoiding low-density by-right single-family sprawl, the council approved Wood Partners' Farrington Mixed Use rezoning (Z15-0009, 500-600 units with 20 affordable Phase 2 apartments and $1.7M in road improvements) by a narrow 4-3 vote, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting No, before passing the consistency statement 7-0. Next, on the Straw Valley mixed-use rezoning at 5441 New Hope Commons Drive (Z14-033), the council passed the project 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No and the remaining six members voting Aye, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement. The council also unanimously approved 7-0 a $95 million installment financing contract resolution, the 3708 Daniel Lane consolidated annexation (BDG1500011), and pulled Item 10 authorizing negotiation to purchase the former Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau facility.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 6 & 13 Supplemental Revisions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented supplemental HIDTA grant documentation on Item 6 (FY15-16 budget amendments) and effective-date corrections on Item 13 (equal business opportunity contracting ordinance).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items including appointments, audits, Brown Green Apartments TEFRA financing, Southside Phase II site agreement, Michie Lake management, equal business opportunity ordinance, DPAC deed extension, and Edgemont Park parcel acquisitions. Council Member Charlie Reece pulled Item 10.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing - $95 Million Installment Financing Contract Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff Chad Cowan presented a public hearing authorizing negotiation of a variable-rate line-of-credit style installment financing contract up to $95 million (at 68.5% of 1-month LIBOR + 0.37%, effective ~0.64%). Council Member Steve Schewel verified draw-down mechanics and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Wood Partners)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from February 15, Wood Partners attorney Ken Spalding and developer Deb Anderson defended Z15-0009 (19.95 acres at 5708 Farrington Road for 500-600 units, office space, $1.7M in NC 54/Farrington intersection upgrades, and 20 affordable units in Phase 2). Opponents Margaret Miller, Debbie McCarthy, Becky Winders, and Spencer Bradford argued 20 units fell far short of the 15% affordable housing goal and urged waiting for Leigh Village design district and housing incentives. Bell, Cole-McFadden, Davis, and Moffitt cited transit ridership, road improvements, and avoiding RS-20 single-family sprawl, passing Z15-0009 4-3 over opposition from Johnson, Reece, and Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Straw Valley (Z14-033, 5441 New Hope Commons Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented Z14-033 rezoning 4.53 acres near I-40 and New Hope Commons Drive to Mixed Use with Development Plan for up to 50 residential units, 25,000 sq ft office, 50,000 sq ft commercial, underground courtyard parking, pedestrian ramps, bus shelter, and half-signal traffic improvements. Neighbor Jim Doer questioned traffic stacking and sidewalks, Don Moffitt questioned non-binding affordable housing remarks from Planning Commission, and council approved Z14-033 6-1 with Charlie Reece voting No.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Initial Zoning - 3708 Daniel Lane (BDG1500011 / Z16-0028)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jacob Wiggins presented voluntary annexation and initial RS-20/FJB zoning for a 3.41-acre lot at 3708 Daniel Lane for one single-family home connecting to city water and sewer (projected $251 net fiscal loss). Planning Director Steve Medlin clarified a memo error, confirming RS-20 was consistent with minimum suburban-tier policy.

agenda_items.title: Authorization to Negotiate Purchase of Former Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Facility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Charlie Reece for clarification, Water Management staff John Grilly confirmed the vote only authorized the city manager and General Services to negotiate the acquisition, with any purchase and subsequent construction contract returning to council.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Council Member Charlie Reece (March 24 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece requested an excused absence from the upcoming March 24, 2016 work session, followed by brief remarks from Mayor Bell about convening an affordable housing workshop.

disagreements.issue: Farrington Mixed Use Rezoning (Z15-0009): Station-Area Density vs. Affordable Housing & Design District Timing
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 approving Wood Partners' 500-600 unit Farrington Mixed Use development near the planned Leigh Village transit station, balancing an unprecedented private proffer of 20 affordable units and $1.7M road upgrades against calls to wait for city affordable housing tools and holistic design district zoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve Z15-0009 immediately to secure transit-supportive density, $1.7M road improvements, and 20 proffered affordable units
side_a_arguments: Rejection risks the site reverting to by-right RS-20 single-family homes with zero affordable units and zero road improvements
High density around light-rail stops supports FTA ridership criteria while city lacks legal authority under NC law to mandate inclusionary zoning
Wood Partners proffered 20 affordable units (tripling station-area affordable stock) plus $1.7M in NC 54/Farrington upgrades
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose or wait until Durham adopts affordable housing incentive tools and completes Leigh Village compact design district planning
side_b_arguments: Ten units at 60% AMI (plus 10 at 80% AMI) in Phase 2 represents a tiny fraction (~1.7%-3.3%) of 600 units against the city's 15% affordable housing goal
Consultant Karen Lado recommended lowering base density so density bonuses can leverage affordable housing
Leigh Village design district planning had not yet been completed (Planning Commission recommended denial 8-2)
disagreements.resolution: Rezoning Z15-0009 passed 4-3 at 02:12:34; companion consistency statement passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Straw Valley Mixed Use Rezoning (Z14-033)
disagreements.summary: On Z14-033 at 5441 New Hope Commons Drive, council approved the project 6-1, with Charlie Reece dissenting and Don Moffitt probing whether any affordable housing commitments were legally bound.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve Z14-033 mixed-use rezoning with traffic, transit, and underground parking improvements
side_a_arguments: Halved projected traffic compared to existing entitlements, funded half-signal improvements at Mt. Moriah/New Hope Commons, and received 9-0 Planning Commission endorsement
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against Z14-033
side_b_arguments: Maintained dissent on station-area rezonings lacking legally committed affordable housing near Patterson Place
disagreements.resolution: Z14-033 passed 6-1 (Charlie Reece voting No) at 02:31:00; consistency statement passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 10, 2016 City Council Work Session—opened by Mayor Bill Bell (who noted he would leave around 2:15 PM)—Council heard a holiday parade plan, unanimously accepted two supplemental priority items (a citizen matter and a resolution supporting Duke University non-tenure track faculty unionization), and received a major presentation from Enterprise Community Partners on Durham's affordable housing needs and strategy. Council voted to suspend the rules to act on Item 29 (the Duke non-tenure track faculty union resolution), with one member requesting changing 'strongly support' to 'support' before the final vote call occurred in a truncated portion of the digest (and staff later confirmed the item was disposed of at the work session). During the Enterprise Community Partners presentation, members and consultants examined neighborhood-targeted vs. citywide affordable housing investments, voucher landlord barriers, avoiding small tax-grant programs in favor of weatherization, land banking, and housing access for residents with disabilities or felony records. Council also recorded unanimous 7-vote appointments for Ricardo Correa (Human Relations Commission) and Rebecca Eckert (Durham Workforce Development Board) and unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Holiday Parade Subcommittee Report, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proposed scheduling a dedicated special workshop to examine the upcoming Affordable Housing Study in depth, and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden reported the Parade Committee's plan for a December 10 'Mayor's Bull City Holiday Parade' along Main, Roxboro, Morgan, and Foster streets ending at the ballpark. The Deputy City Manager introduced two supplemental priority items: Item 27 (citizen matter from Gloria de los Santos) and Item 29 (resolution supporting Duke University non-tenure track faculty union rights), which Council unanimously accepted.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote accepting priority items)

agenda_items.title: Consent and Public Hearing Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed upcoming agenda items, with Steve Schewel praising Finance staff for accurately processing 62,000 invoices annually in the January 2016 Accounts Payable audit (Item 5) and welcoming a 200-unit Housing Authority affordable housing financing item (Item 7, with units at 60% and 30% AMI). Members pulled Items 6 (budget/grant ordinance amendments), 13 (revised Equal Business Opportunity ordinance), 14 (second notice of extension), and 19 (small-scale residential stormwater measures), and reviewed items including a police/fire compensation study contract (Item 17), Liberty Arts lease (Item 15), Edgemont Park parcel acquisitions (Item 16), and planning rezonings (Items 22-24).

agenda_items.title: Item 29: Resolution Supporting Duke University Non-Tenure Track Faculty Union
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted to suspend the rules to take immediate action on Item 29, the resolution supporting the right of non-tenure track faculty at Duke University to form a union. After a motion and second to adopt the resolution, one member requested amending 'strongly support' to 'support' while expressing endorsement; the final voice vote call fell within a truncated portion of the transcript, and the Deputy City Manager later confirmed the item was disposed of at the work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote suspending rules; Item 29 confirmed disposed of at work session)

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Enterprise Community Partners Affordable Housing Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Enterprise Community Partners presented its affordable housing assessment for Durham, advising that concentrating investments in specific appreciating neighborhoods yields greater affordability preservation than spreading small amounts citywide, and identifying voucher landlord reluctance and small developer pipelines as key constraints. Consultants cautioned against administratively heavy small tax-relief grant programs in favor of weatherization or state legislative solutions, explained how project-by-project rezoning increases developer risk premiums and housing costs, and discussed land banking, partnerships with major institutions, and guarantor concepts for residents with felony records.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced seven-vote appointments for Ricardo Correa to the Human Relations Commission and Rebecca Eckert to the Durham Workforce Development Board. Council then unanimously approved the upcoming City Council meeting agenda (Consent items 1-19 and 28; GBA public hearings 21-24; remaining items disposed of).

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 7, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 7, 2016 meeting with all seven council members present, Durham City Council approved referring the police body-worn cameras contract (Item 21) back to the administration while reviewing the 2015 Annual Crime Report (Item 12) and conducting the first FY 2016-17 budget public hearing (Item 13). After a 15-minute presentation by Interim Chief Larry Smith showing an 18% rise in violent crime and 37 criminal homicides alongside a 4% drop in property crime and 25% drop in drug arrests, community speakers from FADE, All Of Us Or None, and residents criticized police consent-search workarounds, racial equity training, and Durham County Jail deaths. On Item 22, a continued public hearing revising fees for underground utility right-of-way inspections (primarily impacting Google Fiber and broadband deployments), council voted 5-2 to adopt City Manager Tom Bonfield's compromise establishing an immediate 50% cost-recovery rate for projects over one mile and a 90-day staff time-logging period for smaller jobs before July 1 rate updates; Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece voted Aye, while Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voted No in favor of higher (75%+) cost recovery. Council also unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0 (minus pulled items), Austin Lawrence Partners' downtown completion extension (Item 14, 7-0), and later adopted pulled Republic Parking (Item 19) and DPAC Oversight Committee appointment (Item 1).

agenda_items.title: Proclamations, Police Commendations, Jail Investigation Comment & Carolina Theatre Closed Session Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented proclamations for Toyama Sister Cities students, CROP Hunger Walk Day, Epilepsy Awareness, Girl Scout Week, International Women's Day, and Charles Bell 'Auto-Erasure' Day. Charlie Reece and Eddie Davis recognized DPD Squad 4C officers Cone, Trice, and Sgt. Butler; Jillian Johnson arranged for Gregory Williams to urge council involvement in investigating Durham County Jail deaths; and Mayor Bell reported closed-session direction to work with Carolina Theatre on financial stability.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Referring Item 21 Body Cameras Back & Supplemental Item 22 Info)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield referred Item 21 (police body-worn cameras contract) back to administration for continued work and distributed supplemental fee schedules for Item 22 (underground utility inspection fees).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 1, 9, and 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent titles including NC-55 widening STIP agreement, GoDurham buses, fire trucks, Google Fiber license agreement, Falls Lake nutrient monitoring, and Durham Sports Commission agreement. Item 19 was pulled for council comment, and Item 1 was pulled by speaker Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Master Agreements for Transportation and Engineering On-Call Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member confirmed prior work-session questions had been answered by staff and moved approval of the transportation and engineering on-call master agreements.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Fourth Quarter and Annual Crime Report & Community Testimony
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Police Chief Larry Smith reported overall Part 1 index crime fell 1% in 2015 (property crime down 4%, burglaries at a 9-year low) while violent crime rose 18% (37 criminal homicides, 10 domestic-related), with 48% of violent crime concentrated in 13.5% of city landmass and 29 operational officer vacancies. Council praised DPD restraint at protests and a 25% drop in drug arrests, while FADE attorney David Hall, All Of Us Or None's Heather Lee, Minister Rafeeq Sayeed, and Victoria Peterson criticized probable-cause search surges, exclusion from police chief search interviews, and gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2016-17 Budget and FY 2017-22 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson opened the public hearing on FY 2016-17 budget priorities. Speakers advocated funding public education on a 'scoop the poop' stormwater/nutrient ordinance, expanding Urban Forestry funding and tree-pruning rules, consulting local soccer clubs on turf/fields, paying DATA Access paratransit drivers a living wage, redirecting police building funds to youth stipends, and creating post-revaluation housing stabilization grants.

agenda_items.title: Economic & Community Development Incentive Amendment - Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Kevin Dick presented an amendment extending the project completion deadline for Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC ($65M minimum downtown City Center investment) from July 1, 2017 to July 1, 2018 at zero financial cost to the city.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Revising Fees for Underground Utility Installations in Rights-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield presented a compromise on underground utility inspection fees following talks with broadband/utility companies: keeping current fees on jobs <=5,280 linear feet while logging actual staff hours for 90 days ahead of July 1 50% cost-recovery rates, while moving immediately to 50% cost-recovery for contracted inspections over 5,280 feet plus $325 reinspection and 3x unpermitted penalties. Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voted No advocating 75%-100% cost recovery, while the five-member majority supported 50% recovery and transparent 90-day cost tracking.

agenda_items.title: Contract Amendment with Republic Parking Systems (Pulled Consent Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell pulled Item 19 to press administration for specific maintenance and security responses regarding incidents and car break-ins in existing downtown parking garages (Corcoran Street / downtown decks) alongside planning for a new Morgan Street garage.

agenda_items.title: DPAC Oversight Committee Mayor's Appointee - Mary Ann Black (Pulled Consent Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 1 to oppose reappointing/appointing Mary Ann Black to the DPAC Oversight Committee, citing her concurrent role at Durham Tech and advocating broader diversity across city boards; council subsequently moved and approved the appointment.

votes.notes: Unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 21 body cameras contract back to administration and added Item 22 supplemental material.

votes.item_title: Item 3: Master Agreements for Transportation and Engineering On-Call Services
votes.notes: Unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved master on-call transportation and engineering service agreements.

votes.notes: Clerk announced 'It passes' without numeric tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed public hearing and accepted citizen budget comments.

votes.notes: No financial cost; unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Extended Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC completion deadline to July 1, 2018.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved Republic Parking Systems contract amendment while Mayor Bell requested specific staff follow-up on garage maintenance and security.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved Mayor's appointment of Mary Ann Black to the Durham Performing Arts Center Oversight Committee.

disagreements.issue: Underground Utility Right-of-Way Inspection Cost Recovery Rate (Item 22)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to adopt the City Manager's 50% cost-recovery fee compromise for private underground utility and broadband installations, with Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel dissenting in favor of recovering 75% to 100% of inspection costs.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt 50% cost-recovery fee structure with 90-day empirical staff time tracking
side_a_arguments: Durham actively recruited broadband providers like Google Fiber and should balance cost recovery with encouraging high-speed infrastructure
90-day staff logging resolves factual disputes with utility companies over actual inspection time before July 1 adjustments

side_b_arguments: Taxpayers should not subsidize 50% of inspection costs generated by private utility construction in public rights-of-way
disagreements.resolution: Ordinance passed 5-2 at 02:25:42 (Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel voting No).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present under Mayor Bill Bell's chairmanship, the February 18, 2016 City Council Work Session covered a contested citizen reimbursement claim, police headquarters design development, and upcoming council items. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority items (Items 9, 18, 19, and 20) and later approved the upcoming regular meeting agenda. On a citizen claim by Trans Perry seeking $9,000 in speed-hump removal expenses, two unidentified council members backed staff's denial under City Code Ordinance 62-97, while Mayor Bill Bell recommended reimbursing 50% of direct costs; Council unanimously suspended the rules to act immediately and passed the 50% reimbursement in a divided voice vote with at least one audible 'No' vote (individual roll-call names were not recorded in the voice vote). Council also received a design development update on the new Police Headquarters and 911 facility at Hood/Elizabeth and Main streets—showing a $9.6 million cost reduction via a smaller 125,800 sq ft footprint—and expressed consensus across Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt in favor of the traditional exterior Option A.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, Priority Items, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven Council members answered roll call. Council Member Jillian Johnson announced she had revised and brought back the Duke non-tenure track faculty union resolution for consideration after citizen comments. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority items—Item 9 (Upper Neuse River Basin Association Falls Lake monitoring resolution), Item 18 (Durham Sports Commission interlocal agreement), Item 19 (Republic Parking Systems contract amendment), and Item 20 (Code Sec. 70-17 frontage charges)—and reviewed upcoming consent and public hearing items including Google Fiber (Item 8) and the FY 2016-17 budget/CIP hearing (Item 13).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote accepting priority items)

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Trans Perry Speed Hump Reimbursement Claim and Police Stop Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Trans Perry submitted invoices seeking $9,000 reimbursement for speed-hump removal costs on Carroll Street, arguing inconsistency with a prior Hillside Street case. Staff and the City Attorney maintained Ordinance 62-97 prohibited speed humps in driveways and two council members opposed overriding staff, while Mayor Bill Bell recommended reimbursing 50% of direct costs. Council unanimously suspended the rules and passed the 50% reimbursement on a divided voice vote with at least one opposing 'No' vote; another resident later spoke regarding a police traffic stop.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote suspending rules; divided voice vote on 50% reimbursement)

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Police Headquarters and 911 Facility Design Development Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services and the design team presented design development progress for the new Police Headquarters and 911 center at Hood/Elizabeth and Main streets, slated for LEED Silver and summer 2018 construction completion. Presenters explained that reducing the building from roughly 162,000 to 125,800 square feet cut costs by $9.6 million to stay within budget, organized around a central spine and public atrium at Elizabeth and Main. Polling Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, Charlie Reece, and Don Moffitt, Council favored exterior Option A (the more traditional brick/thermal facade) over the glass curtain-wall Option B.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Informal consensus on Option A

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 15, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the February 15, 2016 meeting with Mayor Bill Bell's State of the City fireside chat moderated by Bill Shore, all seven Durham City Council members addressed three industrial rezonings, the initial Farrington Mixed Use hearing, UDO omnibus updates, and police body-worn cameras. Council unanimously approved 7-0 three Triangle Business Center / NC 55 plan amendments and industrial rezonings (Items 21-26). On Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Item 27), after Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit speakers and council members debated Wood Partners' newly proffered 20 Phase 2 affordable units against the city's 15% affordable housing goal and upcoming consultant report, Charlie Reece moved to continue the hearing until March 21, passing 6-1 with Don Moffitt voting No and Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel voting Aye. The UDO omnibus text amendment (TC15-0001, Item 28) likewise passed 6-1, with Don Moffitt voting No over unaddressed BPAC recommendations before a 7-0 consistency statement. Finally, after an emotional hour-long debate on pulled Item 14 ($366,738 VieVu body-worn camera contract) in which FADE, ACLU, and residents demanded clear public-release, discipline, and retention protections, council voted 7-0 to delay the purchase three weeks to March 7 and form a subcommittee of Charlie Reece, Steve Schewel, and Jillian Johnson to refine policy recommendations.

agenda_items.title: 2016 State of the City Fireside Chat (Mayor Bill Bell & Bill Shore)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and moderator Bill Shore held a State of the City conversation highlighting Durham's 27-point resident satisfaction improvement, downtown innovation projects (Chesterfield, Jack Tar Hotel, 27-story tower), the dedicated housing penny, Northeast Central Durham poverty reduction task forces and kids' savings accounts, DOJ crime-reduction visits to Boston and Kansas City, HRC police reforms, and Durham-Orange light-rail EIS clearance.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 9 and 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved consent agenda items including board/commission appointments, 2015 municipal election report, HRC Water Management response, Lake Michie land acquisition, Culver Street extension, and North Parking Garage upset-bid proposal. Council Member Don Moffitt noted unreadiness on Item 9 (Republic Parking Systems, delayed) and Item 14 (body-worn cameras) was pulled for public speakers.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0009) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0022) - 1650 T.W. Alexander Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented plan amendment A15-0009 and rezoning Z15-0022 for 13.07-13.25 acres in Triangle Business Center at 1650 T.W. Alexander Drive from Office/Commercial to Light Industrial (up to 200,000 sq ft, protecting the cemetery easement and adding bike lane right-of-way). Planning Commission endorsed both 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0011) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0024) - 5515 & 5517 NC 55
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented A15-0011 and Z15-0024 rezoning 3.5 acres on NC 55 south of Sedwick Road from Commercial Neighborhood to Industrial Light with Development Plan (up to 50,000 sq ft) for a pest control operation. Planning Commission approved 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A15-0008) & Zoning Map Change (Z15-0021) - 462 Stirrup Creek Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented A15-0008 and Z15-0021 cleaning up zoning boundaries on 22.15 acres at 462 Stirrup Creek Drive and T.W. Alexander Drive to Industrial Light with Development Plan (up to 350,000 sq ft warehouse/light industrial and bike/roadway improvements). Planning Commission endorsed 10-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - Farrington Mixed Use (Z15-0009, Wood Partners) Public Hearing & Continuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Wood Partners presented Z15-0009 (19.95 acres at 5708 Farrington Road for 500-600 units, office space, $1.7M in road upgrades), debuting a new Text Commitment 10 offering 10 units at 60% AMI and 10 at 80% AMI for 25 years in Phase 2, alongside Woodland Acres HOA support. Six community speakers (including Christine Westfall, DeDreana Freeman, Becky Winders, Larissa Sibil, Jim Svara) praised the gesture but urged waiting for consultant Karen Lado's March 10 affordable housing report and higher Phase 1 affordability. Charlie Reece moved to continue the hearing to March 21, passing 6-1 over Don Moffitt's No vote.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment - Omnibus Changes 9 (TC15-0001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented UDO Omnibus Text Amendment 9 covering technical updates, removing the 25% local historic district petition minimum, updating wireless rules, and adding non-regulatory UDO intent language supporting affordable housing and socioeconomic diversity. Don Moffitt voted No because Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) requests were not incorporated.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Continuance - Underground Utility Installation Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield reported ongoing negotiations with utility companies regarding inspection cost calculations and recommended continuing the public hearing to March 7, 2016.

agenda_items.title: Body-Worn Cameras Purchase Contract ($366,738, VieVu LLC) & General Order Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Chief Anthony Marsh presented a final draft body camera General Order alongside the $366,738 VieVu purchase contract. Speakers from FADE, People's Alliance, Southern Coalition for Social Justice, and ACLU-NC (Chris Tiffany, Jesse?, Jade Brooks, David Hall, Leslie Nedick, Gregory Williams, Marcus Morrow, Susanna Birdsong) opposed buying cameras until the General Order guaranteed public access to use-of-force videos, barred retention of illegally recorded footage, addressed discipline and civil asset forfeiture funding, and shortened retention. Following detailed recommendations from Steve Schewel, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson, council voted 7-0 to delay three weeks to March 7 and assign Reece, Schewel, and Johnson to work on policy revisions with the City Manager.

disagreements.summary: Six council members voted to continue Wood Partners' Farrington Mixed Use rezoning until March 21 after the consultant's March 10 affordable housing presentation, while Don Moffitt dissented arguing a delay would not change the by-right alternative.
disagreements.side_a_position: Continue public hearing to March 21 to evaluate Wood Partners' last-minute 20-unit affordable housing proffer alongside the consultant's report

disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose omnibus package over omitted BPAC requests

disagreements.issue: Police Body-Worn Camera Contract & Draft General Order Policy Safeguards (Item 14)
disagreements.summary: Public advocates (FADE, ACLU-NC, People's Alliance) urged council to reject the $366,738 VieVu camera contract until the DPD General Order ensured transparency and discipline, while Mayor Bell argued purchasing hardware ahead of policy finalization was practical before agreeing to a three-week committee delay.
disagreements.side_a_position: Withhold approving body camera purchase until DPD General Order strengthens transparency, retention, and accountability
side_a_arguments: Policy should require officers to announce recording, bar criminal-file retention of prohibited recordings, cut unflagged infraction retention from 180 to 90 days, explicitly reference discipline policy, allow video subjects to review footage without filing complaints, and formalize public-release oversight
Without accountability safeguards, cameras risk becoming surveillance tools funded via civil asset forfeiture
disagreements.side_b_position: Purchase hardware immediately while city manager/police refine operational General Orders
side_b_arguments: Writing general orders is an administrative/managerial function and DPD committed not to deploy cameras until policy is finalized

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden before Mayor Bill Bell arrived and presided, the February 4, 2016 City Council Work Session featured two major policy debates—over a proposed Duke University faculty union resolution and police body-worn camera disclosure rules—alongside routine agenda votes. Council Member Jillian Johnson introduced a resolution supporting Duke non-tenure track faculty's right to unionize, which Mayor Bill Bell opposed as drafted due to unverified statistics and a preamble referencing Duke's $8.58 million property tax exemption, proposing instead to send a letter from Council to Duke's President. Later, on Item 14 (the police body-worn camera contract), Council Members Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson pressed the Police Chief for stronger General Order public-disclosure protections—including a per se compelling-public-interest presumption for releasing use-of-force video and Council notification of denied requests—while noting their support for the camera contract depended on policy alignment. Council also approved reordering four presentation items, unanimously approved the City Manager's items (including Consent items 30 and 31), and unanimously approved the upcoming meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Duke Faculty Union Resolution Debate, and Agenda Reordering
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called roll before Mayor Bill Bell joined. Council Member Jillian Johnson introduced a resolution supporting Duke University non-tenure track faculty's right to form a labor union, citing Duke's $8.58 million property tax exemption, tuition increases, and contingent faculty working conditions, and adjunct instructor Jim Haberkamp spoke in favor. Mayor Bell expressed support for labor unions in principle and cited a letter from Duke's Phail Wynn, but opposed the resolution's unverified numbers and tax-exemption framing, recommending a Council letter to Duke's President instead; Council also reordered Items 19, 18, 20, and 14, and Charlie Reece introduced a resolution affirming city boards' and commissions' right to issue public statements.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote reordering items; no vote on Duke resolution)

agenda_items.title: Item 14: Police Body-Worn Camera Contract and General Order Release Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated ongoing cloud-storage costs and public-disclosure rules in the draft Police General Order governing body-worn cameras. Charlie Reece stated he would not back the surveillance investment without a policy reflecting community values, proposing a Council resolution declaring use-of-force footage per se in the compelling public interest and requiring City Manager/Council notice whenever the Chief denies a release request; Jillian Johnson praised the updated written-consent requirement and asked about plainclothes officers and resident notification, while retention periods (180 days for citations/infractions and 90 days otherwise) were also reviewed.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Policy debate without work session vote

agenda_items.title: American Tobacco Parking Deck Expansion Discussion and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Council reviewed financing, construction delivery, and public-use constraints around expanding the American Tobacco parking deck given that the deck is largely leased to one private entity. Council then added Items 30 and 31 to consent, unanimously approved the City Manager's items, and unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda.

votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the upcoming City Council meeting agenda as outlined.

disagreements.issue: Form and Content of Resolution Supporting Duke Non-Tenure Track Faculty Unionization
disagreements.summary: Council Member Jillian Johnson proposed a formal resolution citing Duke's $8.58M property tax exemption and tuition/pay figures to endorse non-tenure track faculty unionization, while Mayor Bill Bell objected to the unverified statistics and tax-exemption clauses and favored sending a concise Council letter instead.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt a formal Council resolution detailing Duke's tax exemption, tuition growth, and contingent faculty working conditions in support of unionization.
side_a_arguments: Non-tenure track faculty lack job security, raises, and benefits despite teaching a growing share of students at Durham's largest employer.
Secure, stable jobs strengthen Durham's broader community.
disagreements.side_b_position: Withhold support for the drafted resolution and instead send a Council letter to Duke's President endorsing faculty's right to organize.
side_b_arguments: Unverified figures (such as tuition rates and Duke's $8.58M property tax exemption) do not belong in a Council resolution without mentioning Duke's positive community contributions.
A formal resolution is less appropriate than a direct letter expressing support for contingent faculty's right to unionize while respecting Duke's right to communicate with employees.
disagreements.resolution: No vote taken on February 4; Jillian Johnson subsequently revised the resolution and brought it back at later work sessions (February 18 and March 10).

disagreements.issue: Police Body-Worn Camera Contract Approval vs. Public Release and Consent Policy Safeguards
disagreements.summary: Council members Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson conditioned their support for the body-worn camera vendor contract on stronger General Order provisions governing public disclosure of use-of-force footage and citizen consent/notification.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require stronger public-release presumptions, Council oversight of withheld videos, and clear consent/notification rules before approving the camera contract.
side_a_arguments: Durham residents sought body cameras primarily for police accountability rather than additional criminal evidence collection.

Council should establish a per se 'compelling public interest' presumption for releasing use-of-force videos and require notice to the City Manager and Council when the Police Chief denies external release requests.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain Police Department General Order discretion over personnel-file/investigative release determinations and move forward with the vendor contract.
side_b_arguments: Public record exceptions and personnel-file protections under state law create legal constraints requiring case-by-case review and closed-session consultation.
If camera procurement depends on General Order language, staff need clear clarity on what policy thresholds satisfy Council.
disagreements.resolution: Debated extensively without a formal vote at the work session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 1, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on February 1, 2016 with all seven members present for a smooth, unanimous 67-minute session. Following an opening tribute proclaiming Dr. Sharon Elliott-Bynum Day and announcements praising free fitness/recreation programming at the Holton Career and Resource Center and Earned Income Tax Credit VITA sites, council approved priority deferrals/referrals and the consent agenda 7-0. In public hearings, council unanimously approved 7-0 closing 431 linear feet of Coventry Road (SC15-06) and adopted the consolidated Historic Properties Local Review Criteria update (Item 14, 7-0) alongside six corresponding historic district preservation plan updates for Fayetteville Street, Cleveland/Holloway Streets, Downtown Durham, Morehead Hill, Trinity Heights, and Watts-Hillandale (Items 15-20, each 7-0 with 7-0 consistency statements), while addressing public questions from NCCU Chancellor Debra Saunders-White and property owner representative Norman Glenn regarding Fayetteville Street corridor code enforcement and economic hardship. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a proclamation declaring January 19, 2016 as Dr. Sharon Elliott-Bynum Day honoring the late CAARE founder. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Lisa Miller explained that because Downtown Durham's preservation plan had been updated in 2011, modifications only swapped in references to the newly adopted consolidated review criteria.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell, Council Member Charlie Reece, and Council Member Jillian Johnson on pre-approved excused absences, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided over a four-member quorum (Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel) at the January 21, 2016 City Council Work Session. Council reviewed a supplemental item supporting Delta Air Lines' Paris service via the Research Triangle Foundation (Item 22), questioned staff on releasing the North Parking Deck from collateral for Capital Broadcasting's potential expansion (Item 4), examined Full Frame Documentary Film Festival's $55,000 city grant budget, and discussed a water utility extension at 8201 Farrington Mill Road (Item 10). Council also heard two detailed staff presentations: Planning's UDO omnibus text amendments (TC1500001) covering technical manual references, neighborhood petition thresholds, and bicycle parking standards, and Neighborhood Improvement Services' (NIS) code enforcement presentation covering housing codes, tall-grass liens, out-of-state landlord enforcement, and NCCU neighborhood cleanups. The session concluded with a single formal voice vote approving the regular meeting agenda after moving Item 4 from Consent to the General Business Agenda alongside Item 8.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Priority Item (Delta Paris Service), and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden convened a four-member quorum (Cole-McFadden, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel) while Mayor Bell, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson were excused. The City Manager introduced supplemental Item 22 (agreement with the Research Triangle Foundation supporting Delta Air Lines' Paris service). Council reviewed items including the 60-cent E-911 phone surcharge funding, North Parking Deck collateral release (Item 4) and Capital Broadcasting's long-term parking rights and expansion plans, Full Frame Documentary Film Festival's $55,000 city grant relative to its $1.1 million budget (with Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel requesting the full festival budget prior to Monday), and single-family development limits on a utility extension at 8201 Farrington Mill Road (Item 10).

agenda_items.title: Item 11: UDO Omnibus Text Amendments (TC1500001) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented omnibus UDO text amendments (TC1500001), addressing UNC School of Government guidance on incorporating technical manuals by reference and explaining that Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit proposals belonged in the Comprehensive Plan. Members discussed tracking Planning Commission votes and rationale in zoning packets, replacing rigid 25% neighborhood petition thresholds with reporting actual signature counts, and establishing minimum indoor bicycle parking standards (one 6-by-2-foot space per residential unit).

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Code Enforcement Activities in the NCCU Area Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Neighborhood Improvement Services (NIS) staff Constance Stancil and Faith Gardner reviewed code enforcement tools under state enabling law and Fourth Amendment limits, including the Minimum Housing Code, Durham's pioneering Non-Residential Building Code, weed/lot abatements over 12 inches with property liens, and abandoned vehicle removal. They explained choosing between criminal summonses and Housing Appeals Board orders—especially for out-of-state owners—and highlighted proactive pre-semester cleanups and assistance for seniors and disabled residents in neighborhoods surrounding NCCU.

agenda_items.title: Set City Council Meeting Agenda and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After brief remarks praising Durham's streamlined council workflow, Council reviewed the agenda for the next regular meeting: Consent items 1-7, 9, 10, and 22; GBA item 8; GBA public hearings 13-20; and Items 11, 12, and 21 disposed of. At a council member's suggestion, Item 4 (deed of partial release) was moved from Consent to GBA to pair with Item 8 before Council approved the agenda by voice vote.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present under Mayor Bill Bell, the January 7, 2016 City Council Work Session handled excused absences for the upcoming January 21 session, priority agenda referrals, housing and infrastructure consent items, and an update on historic preservation standards. Council unanimously approved excused absences on January 21 for Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson (attending the UNC School of Government program for newly elected officials) and for Mayor Bill Bell (attending the U.S. Conference of Mayors), accepted the City Manager's priority items, unanimously referred Item 10 (an economic development incentive agreement with Project Restore) back to administration, and unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda (Consent items 1-8). During citizen matters, Elaine Hyman of the Mews/Orchards community urged Council support in securing a developer to complete roads and infrastructure in their stalled subdivision, while Trans Perry (Item 13) did not appear. Council also reviewed $500,000 in dedicated housing funds for Habitat for Humanity (Items 1-2), stormwater repairs decoupling city drainage from NC Railroad right-of-way (Items 6-7), and a Planning presentation updating historic preservation district criteria across Durham's seven local historic districts.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Crime/Mentoring Announcements, and Jan 21 Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven members answered roll call, and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden commended the Mayor, Sheriff, and Interim Police Chief on their crime press conference while urging community mentorship. Council unanimously approved excused absences for January 21, 2016 for Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson (attending UNC School of Government training) and for Mayor Bill Bell (attending the U.S. Conference of Mayors), leaving the remaining four members to preserve a quorum.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items (Project Restore Referral)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted that Item 10 (public hearing on an economic development incentive agreement with Project Restore) needed to be referred back to administration and that citizen-matter speakers Thelma White and Fred White (Items 11-12) would not appear. Council accepted the City Manager's items and unanimously referred Item 10 back to staff, while the City Attorney noted readiness for a closed session on the Carver Street extension.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote on priority items; unanimous voice vote referring Item 10)

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Failed Subdivision Infrastructure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Elaine Hyman of 3203 Rockford Road spoke on behalf of residents trying for years to recruit a developer to finish roads and infrastructure in their stalled residential subdivision after 17 developers reviewed the site, asking Council to address concerns blocking a prospective developer. Citizen Trans Perry (Item 13) was called later and was absent.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Habitat for Humanity, Stormwater, and Telecom Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Consent items 1-8, including dedicated housing funds for Habitat for Humanity of Durham (Items 1-2, featuring $500,000 in 0% second-mortgage funding and $190,000 in construction write-downs for 10 homes, with a member praising Habitat's 100% repayment record), a VC3 web database amendment (Item 3), an American Tobacco Trail lease with the State (Item 4), a Chamber Legacy Foundation grant (Item 5), streetscape/drainage repairs separating city stormwater pipes from NC Railroad right-of-way (Item 6), emergency stormwater repairs (Item 7, noting seven emergency projects displaced routine right-of-way work), and a managed telecom services contract (Item 8).

agenda_items.title: Planning Presentation: Historic Preservation District Criteria Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed Council ahead of February 1 public hearings on updating Certificate of Appropriateness (COA) criteria across Durham's seven local historic districts and 80+ local landmarks. Staff explained a tiered hierarchy applying the strictest standards to landmarks, moderate standards to contributing structures, and compatibility standards to non-contributing structures and new construction (such as the County Courthouse), noting unanimous October approval by the Historic Preservation Commission and a 9-2 November recommendation from the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Set City Council Meeting Agenda and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting that Trans Perry (Item 13) did not attend, Council unanimously approved placing Consent items 1 through 8 on the upcoming City Council meeting agenda and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Excuse Jan 21 Work Session Absences for Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Council Members Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson from the January 21, 2016 work session to attend the UNC School of Government newly elected officials program.

votes.item_title: Excuse Jan 21 Work Session Absence for Mayor Bill Bell
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Mayor Bill Bell from the January 21, 2016 work session to attend the U.S. Conference of Mayors meeting.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority updates regarding Item 10 (Project Restore) and Items 11-12 (Thelma White and Fred White non-appearances).

votes.item_title: Refer Item 10 (Project Restore Economic Development Incentive Agreement) Back to Staff
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred the public hearing on the proposed economic development incentive agreement between the City of Durham and Project Restore back to the administration.

votes.item_title: Set City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member names were not stated in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the upcoming regular City Council meeting agenda consisting of Consent items 1 through 8.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 4, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the January 4, 2016 Durham City Council meeting with all seven council members attending. Council presented proclamations recognizing January 29, 2016 as George Henry White Day—featuring testimony from Vincent Spaulding of the Benjamin and Edith Spaulding Descendants Foundation—and National Mentoring Month, alongside memorial moments of silence for Dr. Elia Bynum and Lois Caraway. Acting on a City Attorney priority item after staff met earlier that day with contractor Triangle Grading and Paving regarding questions raised at a prior work session, Council voted unanimously 7-0 first to approve the City Attorney's priority item recommendation and then on Council Member Don Moffitt's motion to refer General Business Agenda Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257) back to the City Attorney's Office for legal analysis. Council also unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0, covering the FY 2016-2017 budget development schedule, Urban Ministries of Durham CDBG shelter meal funding, water and street infrastructure contracts, and board appointments, before adjourning at 7:28 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the January 4, 2016 City Council meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., welcomed attendees for the new year, led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Eddie Davis to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk roll call confirmed Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eddie Davis, Jillian Johnson, Don Moffitt, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel were present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: George Henry White Day (January 29, 2016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis read a proclamation signed by Mayor Bill Bell declaring Friday, January 29, 2016 as George Henry White Day in Durham in recognition of the 115th anniversary of Congressman White's 1901 farewell address to Congress and an upcoming commemorative banquet at Duke University featuring Congressman G.K. Butterfield. Vincent Spaulding of the Benjamin and Edith Spaulding Descendants Foundation delivered testimony on behalf of partner historical, legal, and civic organizations highlighting White's legislative legacy and civil rights advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read a National Mentoring Month proclamation highlighting the National Mentoring Partnership established in 2002 and citing youth outcomes associated with mentoring, including higher college enrollment, extracurricular participation, leadership, volunteering, and career readiness.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Memorial Moments of Silence, and Swearing-In Process Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt announced the passing of Dr. Elia Bynum and requested a moment of silence, followed by council remarks honoring Sharon Elia Bynum and local business owner Lois Caraway, who passed away on Christmas Eve. A newly elected council member thanked city staff for their onboarding and assistance since the November election, and brief remarks addressed School of Government guidance on swearing in the Mayor Pro Tempore.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item and Referral of Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Manager, the City Attorney reported that staff from the Attorney's Office, Public Works, and Finance met at 2:00 p.m. that afternoon with Triangle Grading and Paving to address questions raised at a work session the previous year regarding General Business Agenda Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257). The City Attorney recommended referring Item 15 back to the Attorney's Office to compile meeting notes and legal analysis and offered a closed session on Thursday if needed. Council approved the City Attorney's priority recommendation 7-0 and then voted 7-0 on a formal motion by Council Member Don Moffitt to refer Item 15 back to the City Attorney's Office.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (Priority item recommendation and referral motion)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 4-14, 16-17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles, covering Durham Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointments (Item 1), a Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission reappointment (Item 4), street and infrastructure acceptance (Item 5), the FY 2016-2017 budget development schedule (Item 6), a historic preservation fund grant ordinance amendment (Item 7), an Urban Ministries of Durham CDBG contract for emergency shelter meals (Item 8), the November 2015 bid report (Item 9), a sports lighting contract for C.M. Herndon Park baseball fields (Item 10), a land lease with the Durham Regional Association of Realtors Inc. (Item 11), a lien and civil penalty waiver request for 2401 and 2403 (Item 12), a Durham Armory services contract (Item 13), a utility extension agreement for 2639 East Geer Street (Item 14), a commercial water meter replacement phase three contract with Vanguard Utility Services Inc. (Item 17), and a water management LIMS contract (Item 16). Council approved the consent agenda unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: General Business Agenda Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon reaching the General Business Agenda, Mayor Bell noted Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257 award), which Council had already referred back to the City Attorney's Office earlier in the meeting. With no further business remaining, the meeting adjourned at 7:28 p.m.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item Recommendation Regarding Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not explicitly named in the transcript; Mayor Bell confirmed the motion was properly moved and seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the City Attorney's priority report on an afternoon meeting with Triangle Grading and Paving, Public Works, and Finance staff concerning General Business Agenda Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257), Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Attorney's priority item recommendation.

votes.item_title: Referral of General Business Item 15 (Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257) to City Attorney's Office
votes.notes: Seconder was not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Don Moffitt asked whether a formal motion to refer Item 15 back to the City Attorney's Office was appropriate at that point and made the motion to refer Carver Street Extension Contract ST-257 for legal analysis and staff note compilation; the motion was seconded and passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council reviewed consent items, lease renewal terms, contracting integrity concerns, and minority business participation ahead of the winter holidays. On Item 11, Council and the City Attorney examined statutory upset-bid rules for leases extending beyond ten years and initially planned to refer the item back before restoring it to the consent agenda following outside-the-room consultations. Council Member Charlie Reece raised concerns regarding Item 15, a proposed contract with Triangle Paving and Grading—citing a 2011 fatal work-site incident, Department of Labor citations, and a recent federal guilty plea involving undocumented worker hiring—leading Council to place Item 15 on the General Business Agenda for further review. Council also reviewed $7,000 commercial water meter contracts where the bidder subsequently met MBE goals after an initial appeal, announced board appointment ballot results, and set the regular meeting agenda by unopposed voice vote (5-0 among members recorded at initial roll call).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Boards, Budget Schedule, Planning & CDBG Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (Item 3), Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission (Item 4), the FY 2016-17 budget development schedule, a Historic Preservation Fund Grant Project Ordinance Amendment (Item 7), and a 2015-16 CDBG contract with Urban Ministries of Durham (Item 8). Members also discussed minority seat recruitment strategies for city boards and commissions such as the Human Relations Commission (Item 1).

agenda_items.title: Property Lease Renewal and Statutory Upset-Bid Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council examined a proposed second lease term for a city parcel where a prior 10-year lease had expired. The City Attorney explained that state statutes require upset-bid procedures when leasing to the same entity beyond ten years and recommended the administration's proposal of a five-year term with a mutually agreed five-year renewal option (preserving a termination clause for transportation or right-of-way needs) rather than a unilateral tenant renewal option. Following consultations outside the room later in the session, Item 11 was placed back on the consent agenda as presented.

agenda_items.title: Triangle Paving and Grading Contract Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece questioned awarding a contract to Triangle Paving and Grading, noting the city had not contracted with the firm since 2011 after two workers (Mr. Gomez and Mr. Benitez) died at a company work site resulting in Department of Labor citations, and pointing to a federal guilty plea the prior summer regarding hiring undocumented workers. Public Works staff noted the bid-hold period had expired while Triangle agreed to hold its price; Council moved Item 15 to the General Business Agenda to give staff two weeks to evaluate other bidders or gather additional information.

agenda_items.title: Commercial Water Meters Contract & MBE Good Faith Effort Compliance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff addressed the ~$7,000 per-unit cost of commercial water meters and vault replacements. Equal Opportunity/Equity Assurance Director Deborah Giles explained that although the contractor initially failed to demonstrate good faith effort—including through an appeal hearing—the substantial gap between bid prices led to proceeding after the firm subsequently met participation goals using a state-approved MBE contractor.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment Ballots & Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council read appointment ballot results for the Durham Homeless Services Advisory Committee (Emmanuel Kearney with 5 votes, Tony Toss with 6 votes) and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission (Pernell Kennedy with 7 votes), noting ties in two other categories. After confirming Item 11's restoration, Council approved setting the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1, 4-14, 16, and 17; GBA Item 15; Items 2 and 3 referred back) by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1, 4-14, 16, 17; GBA Item 15; Items 2 & 3 Referred Back)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition; five members answered the initial roll call (Bill Bell and Eddie Davis did not record responses at roll call, though seven votes were reported for one board appointment ballot).
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda placing Item 15 (Triangle Paving and Grading) on GBA, restoring Item 11 to consent after offline consultation, and referring Items 2 and 3 back to administration.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 21, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: At its final meeting of 2015, the newly constituted Durham City Council met with all seven members present, welcomed new Council Member Jillian Johnson's remarks thanking staff for her orientation, and approved all items unanimously (7-0). Council adopted the consent agenda covering budget and grant ordinance amendments, a HOPWA contract with Duke University, water and engineering contracts, Southview Park management, a Human Relations Commission ordinance amendment, and a resolution supporting universal pre-kindergarten and early literacy. On the general business agenda, Council unanimously approved closing a 732.25-linear-foot portion of Woodland Drive (SC1500005) for the proposed Rosewalk residential development and approved a consolidated annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial zoning for 4.74 acres at 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway (BDG1500012) after addressing an adjacent resident's traffic, lighting, and buffer concerns.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Ceremonial Oath Administration, and New Member Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:06 PM, led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Eddie Davis to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Following an administrative mix-up regarding a ceremonial oath of office for a city appointee, Council Member Jillian Johnson thanked city staff for helping orient her during her first two weeks in office. The City Manager and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda headings, including City Council minutes, appointments to the Appearance Commission, Open Space and Trails Commission, and Citizens Advisory Committee, FY 2015-16 budget and grant/capital project ordinance amendments, a HOPWA contract with Duke University, engineering contracts with McKim & Creed Inc. and for the High Lift Station abandonment project, Contract SR-63 Wilson Street with Jeff Wilkinson Contracting Co., management of the future Southview Park and conservation areas, an amendment to City Code Section 34-108 (Human Relations Commission Ordinance), stormwater laboratory services, and a resolution supporting universal pre-kindergarten access and early literacy strategies.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Woodland Drive (SC1500005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Department staff member Jacob Wiggins presented a request submitted by Coulter Jewell Thames to close a 732.25-linear-foot portion of Woodland Drive in connection with the proposed Rosewalk residential rezoning expected in early 2016. Staff found that the street segment had been renamed in the late 1930s, posed no service impacts, held little value to the public, and merited closure. No council members raised questions and no members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: 5200 & 5204 Wake Forest Highway / Marlow Builders (BDG1500012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation petition, and initial zoning request from Marlow Builders for two contiguous parcels totaling 4.74 acres at 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway, noting adequate utility capacity and an immediately revenue-positive fiscal impact. Adjacent property owner Mr. Brinkley raised concerns about heavy peak-hour traffic, parking lot cut-through traffic to the neighboring shopping center, lighting, and fencing/vegetative screening along his eastern boundary. Staff clarified that the existing development plan prohibits residential uses, mandates a non-reducible 50-foot buffer with 80% opacity vegetation at maturity, and enforces UDO height and zero-spillover lighting standards at site plan review, while applicant representative Jared Edens agreed to meet with Mr. Brinkley during site design.

votes.item_title: Street Closing: Woodland Drive (SC1500005)
votes.notes: Associated Rosewalk rezoning expected to come before Council in early 2016.
votes.discussion_detail: Jacob Wiggins of the Planning Department presented the application to close 732.25 linear feet of Woodland Drive for the future Rosewalk residential project, confirming no service impacts and recommending approval. No council questions or public comments were offered, and the street closing passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 5200 & 5204 Wake Forest Highway Initial Zoning (BDG1500012)
votes.notes: Required separate statutory consistency vote following initial zoning.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the consolidated annexation and initial zoning for 5200 and 5204 Wake Forest Highway, Council voted 7-0 to adopt the required statutory consistency statement.
