meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members answering roll call, the Durham City Council reviewed affordable housing challenges, special inspections fund accounting, infrastructure contracts, and early childhood literacy support. During Citizens Matters, residents and housing advocates highlighted severe shortages of affordable rentals and difficulty placing Section 8 vouchers even for vetted homeless households. Staff and consultants presented a detailed housing market analysis showing Durham's shift toward rapid-growth affordability pressures—most acute for renters under 30% and 31-50% AMI—alongside expiring LIHTC restrictions, high for-profit ownership of subsidized housing, and UDO barriers to single-room occupancy units. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (including supplemental Item 27 supporting universal pre-kindergarten), approved an excused-absence request for after 2:30 p.m., set the regular meeting agenda, and voted to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Excused Absence Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested moving Item 18 (GoDurham FY 2015 Service Performance Annual Report) ahead of Item 17 and adding supplemental Item 27 (a resolution supporting universal access to pre-kindergarten and early literacy in Durham County). Council unanimously approved the priority items and approved a member's request for an excused absence if the meeting extended past 2:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Affordable Housing, Section 8 Vouchers & Water Contamination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six citizen speakers addressed Council, including Scott Warren and speakers detailing how rising rents prevent Section 8 voucher holders from finding housing in Durham while highlighting coordination with Genesis Home and Urban Ministries to prioritize vetted homeless families on Housing Authority waiting lists. A speaker also criticized lack of action regarding pet waste contaminating local waterways.

agenda_items.title: Consent & Public Hearing Review: Inspections Fund, HOPWA, Water, HRC & Annexation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled several items for staff questions, including Item 5 on how fund balance in the new state-mandated special inspections fund (enacted by House Bill 255 after budget adoption) would be applied toward fee reductions or service enhancements in FY 2016-17. Members also questioned HOPWA coordination with the Durham Crisis Response Center (Item 6), a lift station engineering amendment (Item 7), McKim & Creed hydraulic modeling (Item 8), a Human Relations Commission code amendment (Item 15), stormwater lab services (Item 16), and the Ravenstone/Anderson annexation (Item 20).

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Market Analysis & Expiring Income-Restricted Stock
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants and Community Development staff presented a citywide affordable housing data analysis documenting Durham's transition from disinvestment to rapid growth, identifying the sharpest housing gaps for renters below 30% AMI and at 31-50% AMI. Discussion covered Section 8 Fair Market Rent lags, expiring 15- and 30-year LIHTC affordability covenants, unusually high for-profit ownership of subsidized units, Durham Housing Authority coordination, and UDO restrictions on single-room occupancy (SRO) housing ahead of 60-day staff proposals.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Resolution Confirmation, Agenda Setting & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed the City of Durham resolution text among three attachments for supplemental Item 27 (universal pre-kindergarten) and noted that some members (including Eddie Davis) had departed earlier. Council then approved the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-16 and 27; GBA Public Hearing Items 19 and 20) and voted to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Reorder Item 18 Ahead of 17; Add Supplemental Item 27 Pre-K Resolution)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with all seven members answering initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved Item 18 (GoDurham FY15 annual report) ahead of Item 17 (housing presentation) and added supplemental Item 27 on universal pre-kindergarten.

votes.discussion_detail: Granted an excused absence if the work session continued past 2:30 p.m.

votes.notes: Carried by unopposed voice vote; at 03:07:35 the chair noted departures late in the session (including Eddie Davis and another participant/member after 2:30 p.m.).
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda placing Items 1-16 and 27 on consent and Items 19-20 on GBA public hearing.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Carried by voice vote without opposition following late-session departures.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session at the conclusion of the open work session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 7, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The December 7, 2015 organizational meeting began with certification of the November 2015 municipal election results (19,494 voters, or 10.8% turnout) and farewell tributes and appreciation plaques for retiring 12-year At-Large Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti. Mayor Bill Bell, re-elected Council Member Steve Schewel, and newly elected Council Members Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece were sworn into office, and the newly seated Council unanimously re-elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore (7-0). Council observed a moment of silence in memory of late civic leader R. Kelly Bryant, unanimously approved a nine-item consent agenda (7-0) including the FY 2015 CAFR and Q1 financial report, and received Mayor Bell's committee assignments featuring a newly created Holiday Parade Committee to plan a 2016 parade.

agenda_items.title: Certification of November 2015 Election Results and Farewell Tributes to Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Chair Bill Brian and Director Michael Perry certified the November 2015 municipal election results (19,494 votes cast, 10.8% turnout, including 3,746 early voters) and presented certificates of election to Mayor Bill Bell and At-Large Council Members Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece. Mayor Bell presented appreciation plaques to outgoing At-Large Council Members Eugene A. Brown and Diane Catotti honoring their 12 years of service from December 2003 to December 2015.

agenda_items.title: Oaths of Office and Remarks by Newly Elected and Outgoing Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell, Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel took their oaths of office. Johnson thanked her family and community supporters, Schewel thanked voters, family, city staff, and outgoing mentors Brown and Catotti, and Brown and Catotti delivered farewell addresses reflecting on Durham's 12-year turnaround while highlighting ongoing challenges around poverty, affordable housing, police-community relations, and state legislative relations.

agenda_items.title: Election of Mayor Pro Tempore and Remembrance of R. Kelly Bryant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With the newly elected members seated on the dais, Mayor Bell endorsed Cora Cole-McFadden to continue serving as Mayor Pro Tempore for another two-year term, which Council approved 7-0. Council Member Eddie Davis then honored longtime civil rights and community leader R. Kelly Bryant following his passing at age 98, and Council observed a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney, or City Clerk, Council adopted the nine-item consent agenda. Items included minutes, the October 2015 Cross Connection Control Performance Audit, water engineering contracts with Hazen and Sawyer P.C. and Kimley-Horn and Associates, the October 2015 bid report, an upset-bid property sale, the Priority Trails plan, the FY 2015 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR), and the FY 2015-16 First Quarter Financial Report.

agenda_items.title: Council Committee Assignments and Creation of Holiday Parade Committee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell distributed updated committee assignments for council members to finalize by the Thursday work session. He also announced the creation of a new Holiday Parade Committee—co-chaired by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden with Don Moffitt, Jillian Johnson, and Charlie Reece—to plan staging, timing, and budget inclusion for a Durham holiday parade in 2016.

votes.item_title: Re-elect Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: First formal vote of the newly seated 2015-2017 City Council.
votes.discussion_detail: As the first order of business following the swearing-in of Mayor Bill Bell and Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, and Steve Schewel, Mayor Bell endorsed Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden for another two-year term as Mayor Pro Tempore. The motion passed unanimously 7-0.
